C00.titleEn: From npm scripts to CI Gate: Exit Codes & Blocking False-Green Bugs
C00.summaryEn: Understand Exit Code mechanics in CI validation workflows, prevent False-Green failures (curl --fail, || true, set -euo pipefail), enforce npm ci, and distinguish between CI, Continuous Delivery, and Continuous Deployment.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
When multiple developers collaborate on a project, pushing untested code directly to the main branch (`main`) easily leads to build breaks or disrupts the entire team's workflow. To enforce quality before merging code, modern software development relies on 3 foundational concepts:

- **Pull Request (PR — or Merge Request on GitLab):** Instead of editing directly on `main`, a developer branches off, completes a feature, and opens a PR for peer review and automated verification.
- **Webhook Trigger & Ephemeral Runner:** The moment you open a PR or run `git push`, GitHub sends an automated signal (**Webhook Trigger**) to spin up a clean Linux virtual machine (**Ephemeral Runner** — existing for a few minutes to verify the code, then destroyed upon completion).
- **CI Gate & Exit Code:** The verification VM does not semantically read or understand your source code. The sole basis on which **Continuous Integration (CI)** decides whether to **allow the Merge (pass)** or **block the PR (fail)** is an integer returned by the operating system after each command: ==Exit Code (`0` = Success, `!= 0` = Failure)==.

steps.headingEn: Moving Checks from Local package.json to the CI Gate
steps.bodyEn:
```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "cicd:c00"
alt: "Pipeline cổng kiểm định CI Fail-Fast dựa trên mã thoát POSIX Exit Code 0 so với 1..255 và cách phòng tránh lỗi False-Green"
title: "Cổng kiểm định CI: Tín hiệu POSIX Exit Code & Cơ chế Fail-Fast"
subtitle: "Cách pipeline cho phép Merge khi mọi bước trả 0 và dừng ngay khi gặp mã lỗi 1..255"
caption: "Chuỗi cổng kiểm định tuần tự npm ci -> lint -> test -> build, bảng mã lỗi POSIX đặc trưng (1, 22, 127, 137) và cách phòng tránh lỗi nuốt mã thoát False-Green"
callouts:
  - num: 1
    label: "Chuỗi cổng kiểm định yêu cầu Exit Code == 0"
    desc: "Mỗi tiến trình từ npm ci, eslint, vitest đến build đều phải kết thúc với mã thoát 0 thì nút Merge Pull Request mới được mở khoá."
    tone: emerald
  - num: 2
    label: "Cơ chế Fail-Fast khi gặp mã thoát 1..255"
    desc: "Bất kỳ bước nào trả mã khác 0 (1 lỗi test, 22 lỗi HTTP, 137 tràn RAM OOM) sẽ lập tức huỷ các bước sau và chặn gộp code lỗi."
    tone: rose
  - num: 3
    label: "Phòng tránh lỗi báo xanh giả (False-Green)"
    desc: "Không dùng || true hoặc continue-on-error ở cổng kiểm thử; luôn bật set -euo pipefail và cờ curl --fail-with-body."
    tone: amber
```

In a Node.js/TypeScript project, verification steps are typically declared cleanly in `package.json` (when you run `npm test`, the system executes the corresponding test command below):

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "eslint .",
    "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit",
    "test": "vitest run",
    "build": "tsc -p tsconfig.build.json"
  }
}
```

The key insight of CI/CD architecture is that **the Exit Code `0` vs `!= 0` principle applies uniformly across every programming language**. Whether a project uses Node.js, Python, Go, or Java, a CI pipeline on a Linux VM follows 3 fundamental stages:

| Language / Ecosystem | 1. Locked Dependency Install | 2. Lint & Static Type Checking | 3. Unit Tests & Build |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Node.js / TypeScript** | `npm ci` (matches `package-lock.json`) | `eslint . && tsc --noEmit` | `vitest run && npm run build` |
| **Python (`uv` standard)** | `uv sync --frozen` (matches `uv.lock`) | `uv run ruff check .` | `uv run pytest` |
| **Go (Golang)** | `go mod verify` (matches `go.sum`) | `golangci-lint run` | `go test -race ./... && go build ./...` |
| **Java / Kotlin** | `mvn -B dependency:go-offline` | `./gradlew checkstyleMain` | `./gradlew test assemble` |

The problem with running checks manually on a local machine is human error (forgetting to run tests before pushing) or stale local dependencies lingering in `node_modules` / `.venv`. **CI Gate** eliminates this completely by re-running the exact command sequence on a clean VM and determining the outcome strictly from **Exit Codes** (`process.exit(code)` in Node.js, `sys.exit(code)` in Python, `os.Exit(code)` in Go). Think of it as a standardized exam graded automatically in an isolated environment, free from any quirks on a developer's personal machine.

- [x] **`Exit Code = 0` (`EXIT_SUCCESS`)**: The process completed **successfully**. The pipeline gives a green light and proceeds to the next step.
- [!] **`Exit Code != 0` (`1`..`255`)**: The process **failed**. The pipeline immediately halts (**Fail-Fast**) and locks the Merge button.

| Exit Code | Meaning in Linux & Node.js | Real-World Example on a CI Runner |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`0`** | Complete success (`EXIT_SUCCESS`) | `eslint`, `vitest run`, and `tsc` found zero errors |
| **`1`** | General application error (`process.exit(1)`) | A unit test failed an assertion or a TypeScript syntax error occurred |
| **`22`** | `curl --fail` encountered HTTP `4xx` / `5xx` | Smoke test called `/healthz` and the API returned `500 Internal Server Error` |
| **`127`** | `Command not found` | Typo in command name or invoking `vitest` before running `npm ci` |
| **`137`** | `128 + 9` (`SIGKILL` / OOM Killer) | Node.js or a Jest worker exceeded Runner RAM and was killed by the Linux Kernel |
| **`143`** | `128 + 15` (`SIGTERM`) | Job was actively terminated due to hitting `timeout-minutes` or Concurrency cancelling an older run |

> [!TIP] The Linux Signal `128 + N` Rule
> When a Linux process dies from receiving system signal number `N`, its exit code is always ==`128 + N`==. Therefore, seeing **`137`** (`128 + 9`, i.e., `SIGKILL`) in CI is almost certainly a sign of running out of memory (**Out-Of-Memory — OOM Killer**)!

steps.headingEn: The False-Green Pipeline Risk (Green Pipeline Despite Failing Commands)
steps.bodyEn:
A red pipeline helps catch bugs early so they can be fixed; conversely, a dangerous situation in CI/CD operations is a ==False-Green Pipeline== — the code or service is broken, yet the Pull Request still reports a passing status!

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Ba lỗi cấu hình phổ biến làm mất Exit Code (gây False-Green)"
subtitle: "Một sơ suất nhỏ khi viết lệnh shell có thể vô hiệu hóa toàn bộ quy trình kiểm tra tự động"
left:
  badge: "RỦI RO · Nuốt Exit Code"
  title: "Pipeline báo đạt dù ứng dụng đang lỗi"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # 1. Thiếu cờ --fail: HTTP 500 vẫn trả exit 0!
    curl http://localhost:3000/healthz

    # 2. Toán tử || true ghi đè mã lỗi 1 thành 0:
    npm test || true

    # 3. Không có pipefail: chỉ lấy exit 0 của lệnh tee!
    npm test | tee report.txt
  lang: bash
  bullets:
    - "**`curl` mặc định** chỉ kiểm tra kết nối TCP: dù server trả `HTTP 404` hay `500 Internal Server Error`, `curl` vẫn in nội dung ra rồi kết thúc với **`Exit Code = 0`**."
    - "**Toán tử `A || B`** chạy vế phải khi vế trái lỗi: viết `false || true` hay `npm test || true` sẽ làm `$?` biến thành **`0`** (tương tự việc bật `continue-on-error: true`)."
    - "**Pipeline `|` mặc định** của Bash chỉ lấy mã thoát của lệnh cuối cùng (`tee` ghi file thành công trả `0`), bỏ sót lỗi `1` của `npm test`."
right:
  badge: "CHUẨN MỰC · Fail-Fast Nghiêm Ngặt"
  title: "Phát hiện và dừng ngay khi có lỗi"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail

    # 1. Trả mã lỗi 22 ngay khi gặp HTTP >= 400:
    curl --fail-with-body http://localhost:3000/healthz

    # 2. Giữ nguyên mã lỗi thật của bộ test:
    npm test | tee report.txt
  lang: bash
  bullets:
    - "**`curl --fail`** (hoặc `-f`, `--fail-with-body`) ép `curl` trả mã thoát **`22`** ngay khi gặp HTTP `>= 400`."
    - "**`-e` (`errexit`):** Dừng script ngay tại dòng lệnh đầu tiên trả `Exit Code != 0`."
    - "**`-u` (`nounset`):** Báo lỗi ngay nếu gặp biến chưa khai báo (tránh rủi ro chạy nhầm lệnh như `rm -rf /$EMPTY_VAR`)."
    - "**`-o pipefail`:** Chỉ cần `npm test` ở đầu ống dẫn trả `1`, toàn bộ pipeline `|` lập tức trả `1`."
```

> [!WARNING] Note on the Default Shell in GitHub Actions
> Every `run: |` block written directly in YAML is executed implicitly by GitHub Actions using `bash -eo pipefail {0}`. However, if you extract your script into a separate `.sh` file (e.g., `bash ./scripts/ci-verify.sh`), Bash reverts to its permissive default mode — so **always put `set -euo pipefail` at the top of every `.sh` file** and strictly forbid putting `continue-on-error: true` on `lint`, `typecheck`, `test`, or `build` gates!

steps.headingEn: npm ci vs npm install: Immutable Discipline in CI
steps.bodyEn:
On your laptop when adding a new library, you run `npm install`. On a CI Pipeline, however, `npm install` is a risky anti-pattern because it is allowed to **silently modify `package-lock.json`** if a `^1.2.0` semver range had a new patch released 5 minutes ago.

By contrast, ==`npm ci` (Clean Install)== is built specifically for automated environments:
- [x] **Wipes any existing `node_modules`** to guarantee a 100% clean workspace.
- [x] **Installs exact versions and `integrity` hashes** locked inside `package-lock.json`.
- [x] **Blocks lockfile drift:** If a developer bumps a version in `package.json` but forgets to update `package-lock.json`, `npm ci` immediately aborts with **`Exit Code = 1`** instead of silently guessing! *(In the modern Python ecosystem, the 100% equivalent command is **`uv sync --frozen`** or `pip install --require-hashes`; in Rust Cargo it is `cargo test --locked`).*

steps.headingEn: Clear Distinction: CI vs Continuous Delivery vs Continuous Deployment
steps.bodyEn:
Beginners often lump **"CI/CD"** into a single vague concept. In reality, **"CD"** can mean **2 very different things** at the final button press before reaching real customers:

```visual
kind: groups
title: "Ba Cấp Độ Trưởng Thành Của Pipeline Tự Động Hoá [!badge:cyan:Core Concepts]"
subtitle: "Từ tự động gác cổng Pull Request (CI) -> sẵn sàng phát hành bằng 1 cú nhấp chuột (Delivery) -> tự động lên thẳng Production (Deployment)"
columns: 3
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: check
    title: "Continuous Integration"
    badge: "Tích hợp liên tục (CI)"
    tone: sky
    desc: "Tự động kiểm định mã nguồn trên máy ảo sạch mỗi khi có commit hoặc mở Pull Request vào nhánh chính."
    bullets:
      - "Chạy tự động cài đặt khoá phiên bản -> `lint` -> `test` -> `build`"
      - "Phát hiện xung đột logic và vỡ kiểu dữ liệu sớm ngay trong vài phút"
    footer: "Mục tiêu: Nhánh main luôn biên dịch và chạy test xanh 100%"
  - num: 2
    icon: shield
    title: "Continuous Delivery"
    badge: "Chuyển giao liên tục (1-Click)"
    tone: amber
    desc: "Tự động đóng gói sản phẩm và đẩy lên môi trường thử nghiệm Staging, sẵn sàng lên Production chỉ bằng 1 cú nhấp chuột!"
    bullets:
      - "Tự động hoá trọn vẹn khâu đóng gói & kiểm thử trên `staging`"
      - "Giữ **Cổng phê duyệt con người (Manual Approval Gate)** trước `environment: production`"
    footer: "Sẵn sàng 100% — Tech Lead chủ động bấm nút chọn giờ lên Prod"
  - num: 3
    icon: rocket
    title: "Continuous Deployment"
    badge: "Triển khai liên tục (Auto-Prod)"
    tone: emerald
    desc: "Xoá bỏ hoàn toàn bước bấm nút thủ công — tự động hoá xuyên suốt từ lúc merge code tới thẳng tay người dùng thật."
    bullets:
      - "Mọi commit vượt qua toàn bộ cổng kiểm thử tự động trên `main` tự động triển khai thẳng ra **Production**"
      - "Đòi hỏi độ phủ test tự động, Canary và cơ chế tự động Rollback cực kỳ vững chắc"
    footer: "Phát hành lên Production hàng chục lần mỗi ngày không cần chạm tay"
```

> [!REMEMBER] Pocket Takeaways
> - The CI Runner judges pass/fail strictly by **Exit Code**: `0` = success, `!= 0` = failure (`137` = `SIGKILL` / OOM memory overflow).
> - Prevent **False-Green**: always use `curl --fail`, enable `set -euo pipefail` in Bash scripts, and never append `|| true` to verification steps.
> - Always use **`npm ci`** in CI to enforce `package-lock.json` strictly.
> - **Continuous Delivery** pauses for human approval before Production · **Continuous Deployment** pushes straight to Production automatically.

readings.noteEn: Minimal 2026-standard CI template for a Node.js 22 app: read-only permissions, checkout@v4, setup-node@v4, and sequential npm ci -> lint -> test.
readings.taskEn: Look at the steps from lines 30 to 38: if `npm run lint` on line 34 detects 1 ESLint error and exits with code `1`, will the `npm test` step on line 37 still execute? Why?
readings.answerEn: No! When `npm run lint` returns `Exit Code = 1` (non-zero), GitHub Actions' default Fail-Fast mechanism immediately marks that Step as failed, skips all subsequent Steps (`npm test`), and blocks the PR gate.

readings.noteEn: False-Green failure scenario: TypeScript, Unit Tests, and the Staging API are all broken, yet the workflow still reports success.
readings.taskEn: Identify the exact 3 mechanisms swallowing Exit Codes in the `Typecheck`, `Run Unit Tests`, and `Smoke check staging health` steps.
readings.answerEn: 1) The `Typecheck` step enables `continue-on-error: true`, causing compilation errors to still count as passing; 2) The `Run Unit Tests` step appends `|| true`, forcing the exit code to always be `0`; 3) The `Smoke check` step invokes `curl` without the `--fail` (or `-f`) flag, so an HTTP 500 still returns exit code `0`.

cicd-q-c00-1.qEn: When a `run: npm test` step on GitHub Actions has 2 failing test cases, how does the test runner signal the CI Runner to block the Pull Request?
choicesEn: Prints red "ERROR" text to stdout for GitHub's AI to interpret
Exits the process with a non-zero exit code (Exit Code != 0, typically 1)
Sends a separate HTTP webhook back to the developer's machine
Automatically deletes the Git branch that was just pushed
cicd-q-c00-1.explainEn: The CI Runner does not parse console text; it relies solely on the OS process Exit Code: `0` means success (green), and non-zero means failure (red).

cicd-q-c00-2.qEn: Predict the exit code (`$?`) printed on the last line when running the following Bash snippet (knowing that `false` always returns error code `1` and `true` always returns `0`):
cicd-q-c00-2.explainEn: The `||` operator executes the right-hand side (`true`) when the left-hand side (`false`) fails. Since `true` returns `0`, the entire `false || true` expression exits with Exit Code `0` — this is the exact cause of the False-Green trap when writing `npm test || true`.

cicd-q-c00-3.qEn: By default, when calling `curl https://api.example.com/health` and the server responds with `HTTP 500 Internal Server Error`, the `curl` command still exits with Exit Code `0`.
cicd-q-c00-3.explainEn: True! By default, `curl` considers establishing the network connection and receiving the HTTP response (even 404 or 500) as completing its job (`exit 0`). You must add `--fail` (or `-f`) so `curl` returns exit code `22` on HTTP >= 400.

cicd-q-c00-4.qEn: In a multi-line Bash script containing the pipeline `npm test | tee report.txt`, which option in `set -euo pipefail` ensures the command does not turn false-green when `npm test` fails while `tee` still succeeds in writing the file?
choicesEn: -e (errexit)
-u (nounset)
-o pipefail
No flag is needed because the | operator automatically propagates the first failure
cicd-q-c00-4.explainEn: By default, Bash returns the exit code of the last command in a pipeline (`tee`, which returns `0`). The `-o pipefail` option forces the pipeline to return the non-zero exit code of the rightmost failing command inside the pipe (`npm test`).

cicd-q-c00-5.qEn: What happens when `npm ci` runs in a CI Pipeline after a developer bumped a library version in `package.json` without updating `package-lock.json`?
choicesEn: npm ci automatically updates package-lock.json and continues running normally
npm ci ignores package-lock.json and pulls the latest version from the npm registry
npm ci immediately aborts with an error (Exit Code != 0) because the two files are out of sync
npm ci installs only packages in dependencies and skips devDependencies
cicd-q-c00-5.explainEn: `npm ci` guarantees strict reproducible builds: if `package.json` and `package-lock.json` do not match, it immediately fails and exits non-zero rather than silently rewriting the lockfile.

cicd-q-c00-6.qEn: Your engineering team automates all testing, image building, and Staging deployments, but before going to Production the Job pauses at `environment: production` waiting for the Tech Lead to click Approve. What is this model called?
choicesEn: Continuous Integration
Continuous Delivery
Continuous Deployment
Traditional Manual Ops
cicd-q-c00-6.explainEn: Continuous Delivery automates everything up to release-readiness with an explicit approval gate (Manual Gate) for Production; Continuous Deployment pushes automatically straight to Production with no human click required.

cicd-q-c00-7.qEn: When a container or test process on a Linux CI Runner suddenly terminates with `Exit Code 137`, the most common cause is that the process received `SIGKILL` (typically due to an Out-Of-Memory condition — OOM Killer).
cicd-q-c00-7.explainEn: By Linux convention, a process terminated by signal `N` exits with `128 + N`. For `SIGKILL` (`9`), the exit code is `128 + 9 = 137`, the classic signature of Out-Of-Memory (OOM).

cicd-card-c00-1.frontEn: How does the Exit Code convention work on POSIX systems / CI Runners?
cicd-card-c00-1.backEn: `0` means success (green CI step). Any value from `1` to `255` means failure (red CI step, triggering Fail-Fast to stop subsequent steps).

cicd-card-c00-2.frontEn: Why is calling `curl http://localhost:3000/health` without `--fail` dangerous in a Smoke Test step?
cicd-card-c00-2.backEn: Because by default `curl` still returns `Exit Code = 0` even when the API crashes with HTTP `404` or `500`, creating a False-Green Pipeline. Always use `curl --fail` (or `-f`) so it returns exit code `22`.

cicd-card-c00-3.frontEn: What does the trio of flags `set -euo pipefail` mean in a CI Bash script?
cicd-card-c00-3.backEn: `-e`: exit immediately if any command fails; `-u`: error when referencing an unset variable; `-o pipefail`: capture failures from any command inside a `|` pipe.

cicd-card-c00-4.frontEn: What are the 3 core differences between `npm ci` and `npm install` when running in a Pipeline?
cicd-card-c00-4.backEn: 1) Deletes any existing `node_modules` before installing; 2) Installs exact versions from `package-lock.json` (never overwrites the lockfile); 3) Fails immediately if `package.json` is out of sync with `package-lock.json`.

cicd-card-c00-5.frontEn: What incidents do Exit Code `137` and `143` signal on a CI Runner respectively?
cicd-card-c00-5.backEn: `137` (`128 + 9` SIGKILL): process was forcefully killed immediately, typically due to RAM exhaustion (OOM Killer). `143` (`128 + 15` SIGTERM): process received a graceful shutdown signal due to hitting a timeout or Job cancellation.

cicd-card-c00-6.frontEn: What is the single difference between Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment?
cicd-card-c00-6.backEn: Continuous Delivery includes a manual approval gate (e.g., `environment: production` 1-click approval) before Production, whereas Continuous Deployment deploys automatically to Production as soon as all tests pass.

cicd-card-c00-7.frontEn: What is the version-locked installation command equivalent to `npm ci` (Node.js) in the modern Python ecosystem (`uv`)?
cicd-card-c00-7.backEn: `uv sync --frozen` (strictly reads `uv.lock` and immediately returns `Exit Code != 0` if the lockfile is out of sync, following the exact same immutability philosophy as `npm ci`).

cicd-ex-c00-1.promptEn: The `smoke` job checks API health after startup with `curl http://localhost:3000/healthz`. Because the HTTP failure flag is missing, even when the server returns `500 Internal Server Error`, the check still passes falsely (`Exit Code 0`). Add the `--fail` (or `-f`) flag to the `curl` command in `jobs.smoke.steps[0].run`.
hintsEn: By default `curl` only returns a non-zero exit code on TCP/DNS network failures, not HTTP 4xx/5xx responses.
Update the first step's `run:` line to `curl --fail http://localhost:3000/healthz` (or use `-fsSL`).

cicd-ex-c00-2.titleEn: Remove || true and continue-on-error error-swallowing traps
cicd-ex-c00-2.promptEn: A teammate previously added both `continue-on-error: true` and `|| true` to the `npm test` step (the 3rd step — `steps[2]`) to rush past last week's deadline, letting dozens of bugs slip straight into `main`. Completely remove the `continue-on-error` property and strip `|| true` so `npm test` truly gates the pipeline when tests fail.
hintsEn: Delete the `continue-on-error: true` line from the `Run unit tests` step (`jobs.test.steps[2]`).
Change `run: npm test || true` to `run: npm test` to preserve the test runner's actual exit code.

cicd-ex-c00-3.titleEn: Harden a multi-line script with set -euo pipefail
cicd-ex-c00-3.promptEn: The `Verify and log` step (`jobs.verify.steps[2]`) runs a multi-line script using a pipe `|` (`npm run lint | tee lint.log`, followed by `npm run build` and `echo "Done"`), while configured with `shell: bash --noprofile --norc {0}`, so Bash does not enable pipe failure detection automatically. Add `set -euo pipefail` at the very top of the `run:` block so any lint or build error halts execution immediately before reaching `echo "Done"`.
hintsEn: Place `set -euo pipefail` as the first command line under `run: |` (indented 10 spaces to align with `npm run lint`).
Keep the `npm run lint | tee lint.log`, `npm run build`, and `echo "Done"` commands underneath.

cicd-ex-c00-4.titleEn: Lock down immutable dependencies with npm ci
cicd-ex-c00-4.promptEn: The current workflow uses `npm install` in the dependency installation step (`jobs.build.steps[2]`), which allowed a new minor/patch release on the npm registry this morning to break CI even though it stayed green on a colleague's laptop. Replace `npm install` with the deterministic `npm ci` command.
hintsEn: Locate the `Install dependencies` step (`jobs.build.steps[2].run`).
Replace `npm install` with `npm ci` to strictly adhere to `package-lock.json`.

cicd-ex-c00-5.titleEn: Set up a Continuous Delivery approval gate for Production
cicd-ex-c00-5.promptEn: Right now, the `deploy-prod` job runs in parallel with the `test` job and pushes straight to the live server with zero protection! Convert the workflow into a safe **Continuous Delivery** model with 2 edits on `jobs.deploy-prod`: (1) declare `needs: test` so it waits for `test` to pass, and (2) attach `environment: production` to require human approval.
hintsEn: Under `deploy-prod:`, add `needs: test` (or `needs: [test]`) at the same indentation level as `runs-on`.
Also add `environment: production` to `deploy-prod` to enable the GitHub Deployment Protection Gate.

C01.titleEn: GitHub Actions Architecture: Trigger, Workflow, Job, Step & Ephemeral Runner
C01.summaryEn: Master the Trigger -> Workflow -> Job -> Step -> Action hierarchy, understand Ephemeral Runners, and configure working-directory for multi-folder repositories.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
When opening a `.github/workflows/ci.yml` or `.gitlab-ci.yml` file for the first time, learners often encounter nested keywords like `on`, `jobs`, `runs-on`, `steps`, `uses`, `run`, and `defaults`. However, **every modern CI/CD platform** — whether for Node.js, Python, Go, or Java — operates on ==6 core components==:

- **Webhook Trigger:** The moment you run `git push` or open a **Pull Request (PR)**, the Git server immediately dispatches a network event (Webhook JSON) to trigger the CI system automatically without manual intervention.
- **Ephemeral Runner:** Instead of running on a long-lived shared server (prone to stale config, full disks, or malware persistence), each **Job** is provisioned a **fresh, clean Linux virtual machine**, runs for a few minutes, and is **automatically torn down and wiped** as soon as the Job finishes.

Understanding the boundaries between these 6 components lets you design accurate pipelines and avoid common pitfalls like missing files across separate Jobs.


To draw a Node.js analogy: **Trigger (`on:`)** is like an HTTP Webhook receiving an event, **Workflow** is the top-level orchestrator function, each **Job** is an isolated worker process on a separate server, and **Steps** are individual commands running sequentially inside that worker.

> [!TIP] Industry CI/CD Ecosystem Map
> In real-world engineering teams, you will encounter several CI/CD platforms, and all 6 entities map 1-to-1 across every one of them:
> - **GitHub Actions** (`.github/workflows/*.yml`): #1 most popular for Cloud & Open-Source projects, with a massive marketplace of prebuilt Actions.
> - **GitLab CI/CD** (`.gitlab-ci.yml` — covered in depth in lesson `C09`): The gold standard in banks and enterprises running internal self-managed infrastructure, excelling at pure container execution.
> - **Jenkins** (`Jenkinsfile` written in Groovy): A long-standing staple in large enterprises (*Enterprise Legacy*); often runs a persistent Controller + Agent model, making Docker/Kubernetes Agents essential to avoid environment pollution.
> - **CircleCI & Buildkite**: Known for ultra-fast caching and Hybrid models (cloud orchestration with Runners hosted inside the company's private AWS/GCP network).
> - **Dagger**: A next-generation "Pipeline-as-Code" tool allowing build pipelines written in TypeScript/Python/Go to run inside BuildKit containers identically 100% on both laptops and any CI server!

steps.headingEn: Environment Isolation Principle: Steps in One Job Share Disk, Separate Jobs Run on Isolated VMs
steps.bodyEn:
This is the single most common source of confusion when learning CI/CD configuration.

Within the same **Job** (for example `jobs.verify`), every **Step** runs sequentially on **the exact same Runner VM (`ubuntu-latest`)**: Step 1 `actions/checkout@v4` pulls the code onto disk -> Step 2 `actions/setup-node@v4` adds Node 22 to `PATH` -> Step 3 `run: npm ci` creates `node_modules/` on the SSD -> Step 4 `run: npm test` immediately sees both the source code and the installed `node_modules/`!

However, if you split them into **two separate Jobs**, `jobs.install` and `jobs.test`, they run on ==two completely isolated Ephemeral VMs==:

```visual
kind: layers
title: "Ranh Giới Vật Lý Của Ephemeral Runner Giữa Hai Job Riêng Biệt"
subtitle: "Mỗi Job thức dậy trên một máy ảo sạch tinh từ con số 0 — vừa bảo mật chống mã độc tồn lưu, vừa triệt tiêu rác cấu hình"
columns:
  - title: "Job 1: install (Ephemeral VM #1)"
    badge: "Tự huỷ ngay khi xong Step cuối"
    tone: amber
    layers:
      - label: "Step 1: uses: actions/checkout@v4"
        note: "Tải mã nguồn vào /home/runner/work/repo/repo"
        tone: sky
      - label: "Step 2: uses: actions/setup-node@v4"
        note: "Gắn binary Node 22 vào PATH của VM #1"
        tone: cyan
      - label: "Step 3: run: npm ci"
        sub: "Sinh ra thư mục node_modules/ trên ổ SSD của VM #1"
        note: "Tồn tại cục bộ"
        tone: emerald
      - label: "Kết thúc Job 1 -> Tiêu huỷ toàn bộ Máy Ảo #1!"
        note: "Ổ đĩa bị xoá sổ vĩnh viễn"
        tone: rose
    footer: "Mọi tệp chưa đẩy lên Cache / Artifact đều biến mất cùng VM #1"
  - title: "Job 2: test (Ephemeral VM #2 mới tinh)"
    badge: "Khởi tạo trắng tinh hoàn toàn"
    tone: rose
    layers:
      - label: "Hệ điều hành Ubuntu sạch như vừa cài mới"
        sub: "Thư mục workspace trống trơn — CHƯA CÓ cả mã nguồn Git!"
        note: "Trống rỗng 100%"
        tone: slate
      - label: "Nếu gọi ngay: run: npm test (Thiếu checkout & npm ci)"
        sub: "Gặp lỗi tức khắc: ENOENT: Could not read package.json!"
        note: "Lỗi thường gặp"
        tone: rose
      - label: "Quy tắc chuẩn: Job tự thân vận động (Self-Contained)"
        sub: "Tự checkout@v4 + setup-node@v4 (cache: 'npm') + npm ci trên VM #2"
        note: "Chuẩn công nghiệp"
        tone: emerald
    footer: "Muốn truyền sản phẩm dist/ giữa 2 Job? Dùng upload-artifact@v4 & download-artifact@v4!"
```

- [x] **Every independent Job must be self-contained:** Call `actions/checkout@v4` itself, run `actions/setup-node@v4` itself (with `cache: 'npm'` enabled to restore packages in seconds), and run `npm ci` itself.
- [x] **Transfer outputs over the network when needed:** To pass a compiled `dist/` directory or test report from one Job to another, package it via **Artifacts** (`actions/upload-artifact@v4` and `actions/download-artifact@v4`).

steps.headingEn: Distinguishing uses: (Prebuilt Action) vs run: (Shell Command)
steps.bodyEn:
Each item in a `steps:` list must choose **one of the two** execution keywords (never combine both `uses` and `run` in the same Step):

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Hai Hình Thức Thực Thi Trong Một Step: uses: vs run:"
left:
  badge: "ACTION · uses: + with:"
  title: "Gọi module đóng gói sẵn (TypeScript / Docker)"
  tone: sky
  code: |
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js 22 LTS
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Tái sử dụng module chuẩn của GitHub hoặc cộng đồng"
    - "Truyền tham số cấu hình thông qua khối **`with:`** (tương tự truyền object `options` vào hàm JS)"
    - "**Cảnh báo:** Runner mới bật **không tự tải code Git** — luôn nhớ `actions/checkout@v4` ở đầu Job!"
right:
  badge: "SHELL · run:"
  title: "Thực thi trực tiếp câu lệnh CLI trong subshell"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    steps:
      - name: Install locked dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Verify types & unit tests
        run: |
          npm run typecheck
          npm test
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Mở trình thông dịch Shell (mặc định là `bash`) để gõ lệnh giống hệt Terminal"
    - "**Lưu ý quan trọng về Subshell:** Mỗi Step `run:` khởi chạy trong một **subshell mới** đặt lại tại thư mục gốc workspace!"
    - "Nếu Step 1 chạy `mkdir sub && cd sub`, sang Step 2 lệnh `basename \"$PWD\"` **vẫn in ra tên thư mục gốc `repo`** chứ không đứng ở `sub`!"
```

steps.headingEn: Handling Projects in Subdirectories with defaults.run.working-directory
steps.bodyEn:
In real-world repositories (especially Monorepos or repositories split into `apps/backend` and `apps/frontend`), `package.json` often does not live at the repository root (`/`).

Because `cd apps/backend` in one Step does not persist into the next Step, instead of repeating `cd apps/backend && ...` on every line, declare ==`defaults.run.working-directory`== at the Job or Workflow level:

```yaml
jobs:
  backend-ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: apps/backend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
          cache-dependency-path: apps/backend/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
```

> [!REMEMBER] Pocket Takeaways
> - By default, **Jobs** without `needs:` run **in parallel** on **completely isolated Ephemeral VMs** (no shared disk or RAM).
> - **Steps** inside the same Job run **sequentially** on the same Runner (sharing disk), but each `run:` Step spawns a **fresh subshell** at the workspace root (`cd` does not carry over to the next Step).
> - A freshly provisioned VM starts **completely empty without code** — always begin with `uses: actions/checkout@v4`, and use `defaults.run.working-directory` when the project lives in a subdirectory!

readings.noteEn: Observe all 6 canonical entities together: Trigger (`on`), Workflow (`name`), Runner (`runs-on: ubuntu-latest`), Job (`verify`), 5 sequential Steps, and 2 Actions (`checkout@v4`, `setup-node@v4`).
readings.taskEn: How many Jobs and how many Steps are in this file? Why can the `npm test` Step on line 37 read the `node_modules` directory created by `npm ci` on line 31?
readings.answerEn: The file has 1 Job (`verify`) containing 5 Steps. Because all Steps within the same Job run sequentially on the same Runner VM (`ubuntu-latest`) and share the same workspace directory on disk.

readings.noteEn: Classic real-world scenario: the `build` Job compiles `dist/`, yet in the `deploy` Job `ls -la dist/` crashes with `No such file or directory`.
readings.taskEn: Even though the `deploy` Job declared `needs: build` to run after `build`, why does the `deploy` Job's disk contain neither `dist/` nor the source code?
readings.answerEn: Because each Job runs on a completely separate Ephemeral Runner (single-use VM). Once the `build` Job finishes, its VM and `dist/` folder are destroyed; `needs: build` only coordinates execution order, not shared storage between the two VMs.

cicd-q-c01-1.qEn: Which statement BEST describes the execution environment difference between `Step`s within the same Job versus different `Job`s within the same Workflow?
choicesEn: Steps run in parallel across multiple VMs; Jobs run sequentially on the same VM
Steps run sequentially on the same Runner and share the workspace disk; each Job runs on a brand-new, completely isolated Runner VM
Both Steps and Jobs share the default `/home/runner` disk without any extra configuration
Each Step boots a fresh Ubuntu VM from scratch
cicd-q-c01-1.explainEn: Within a single Job, Steps run sequentially on the same VM and share the filesystem. Two different Jobs run on two separate Ephemeral VMs with no shared disk or RAM.

cicd-q-c01-2.qEn: When a GitHub-hosted Runner (`ubuntu-latest`) starts up for a Job, the repository's Git source code is already present in the working directory, so you can call `run: npm ci` right away without `actions/checkout@v4`.
cicd-q-c01-2.explainEn: False! A newly provisioned Runner VM has a completely empty workspace directory. You must invoke `uses: actions/checkout@v4` to fetch the current commit/PR's source code onto disk before running `npm ci`.

cicd-q-c01-3.qEn: In a `steps:` list item, when do you use the `uses:` keyword instead of `run:`?
choicesEn: Use `uses:` for multi-line Bash commands, whereas `run:` only executes single-line commands
Use `uses:` to invoke a prepackaged Action (such as `actions/setup-node@v4`), and `run:` to execute CLI commands in a Shell
Use `uses:` for TypeScript projects and `run:` for plain JavaScript projects
The two keywords are identical and can be combined in the same Step
cicd-q-c01-3.explainEn: `uses:` loads and runs a reusable GitHub Action (with `with:` inputs), while `run:` opens a Shell (default `bash`) to execute CLI commands directly such as `npm ci` or `npm test`. A single Step cannot contain both `uses` and `run`.

cicd-q-c01-4.qEn: Given the configuration below (2 consecutive Steps inside the same Job), what final directory name (`basename $PWD`) will the second Step print?
cicd-q-c01-4.explainEn: Each `run:` Step starts in a fresh subshell at the repository's workspace root (e.g., `/home/runner/work/repo/repo`), so `cd sub` in Step 1 does not carry over to Step 2! To change the directory for all Steps, use `defaults.run.working-directory` (if the repo is named `repo`, `basename "$PWD"` remains the root directory name `repo`).

cicd-q-c01-5.qEn: An API service has its `package.json` located at `apps/backend/package.json`. Which configuration is the cleanest and least repetitive way to run `npm ci`, `npm run lint`, and `npm test` inside `apps/backend`?
choicesEn: Add a first Step containing only `run: cd apps/backend`
Declare `defaults.run.working-directory: apps/backend` at the Job or Workflow level
Change `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` to `runs-on: apps/backend`
Move every file to the repository root because GitHub Actions does not support subdirectories
cicd-q-c01-5.explainEn: `defaults.run.working-directory: apps/backend` automatically sets the default working directory for all `run:` steps in that scope without repeating `cd apps/backend && ...` in every Step.

cicd-q-c01-6.qEn: By default, if you declare two sibling Jobs `lint` and `test` inside `jobs:` WITHOUT using the `needs:` keyword, how will GitHub Actions schedule them?
choicesEn: Sequentially from top to bottom matching their line order in the YAML file
Runs only the first Job and skips the second Job
Provisions 2 separate Runner VMs and executes both Jobs in parallel simultaneously
Throws a YAML syntax error due to missing execution priority
cicd-q-c01-6.explainEn: By default, all Jobs without `needs` constraints start simultaneously (in parallel) on independent VMs to minimize total feedback wait time for developers.

cicd-q-c01-7.qEn: The Ephemeral (single-use and destroyed) nature of Hosted Runners prevents configuration debris from accumulating across builds and reduces the risk of malware persisting from one run to the next.
cicd-q-c01-7.explainEn: Correct! Provisioning a clean VM for every Job both guarantees 100% consistent test environments and eliminates the risk of data leaks or persistent malware left on disk from prior Jobs.

cicd-card-c01-1.frontEn: Name the 6 core entities that make up a GitHub Actions pipeline from outside to inside.
cicd-card-c01-1.backEn: 1) Event/Trigger (`on`) -> 2) Workflow (`.yml` file) -> 3) Job (`jobs.<id>`) -> 4) Runner (`runs-on`) -> 5) Step (`steps`) -> 6) Action (`uses`) / Shell command (`run`).

cicd-card-c01-2.frontEn: What is an Ephemeral Runner and how does it affect `node_modules` or `dist/` between 2 Jobs?
cicd-card-c01-2.backEn: It is a clean VM that lives only for the duration of 1 Job and is then completely wiped. Therefore, a downstream Job CANNOT see `node_modules` or `dist/` on the upstream Job's disk unless it reinstalls or transfers them via Artifacts/Cache.

cicd-card-c01-3.frontEn: Why must nearly every code-testing Job begin with `uses: actions/checkout@v4`?
cicd-card-c01-3.backEn: Because a newly booted Runner VM is completely empty and lacks the project's Git source code. `actions/checkout@v4` fetches the exact commit/branch that triggered the event into the workspace directory.

cicd-card-c01-4.frontEn: Why doesn't adding a standalone `- run: cd apps/backend` Step put the next Step inside `apps/backend`?
cicd-card-c01-4.backEn: Because each `run:` Step executes in an independent subshell that always resets the current directory to `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE`. Use `defaults.run.working-directory: apps/backend` instead.

cicd-card-c01-5.frontEn: What is the difference between `with:` and `env:` when calling an Action via `uses:`?
cicd-card-c01-5.backEn: `with:` passes official input parameters defined in that Action's `action.yml` (e.g., `node-version: "22"`), whereas `env:` sets operating system environment variables for the process.

cicd-card-c01-6.frontEn: What does the label `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` mean inside a Job?
cicd-card-c01-6.backEn: It asks the CI platform to provision a Linux VM running the latest stable Ubuntu LTS managed by GitHub (GitHub-hosted Runner) to execute all Steps of that Job.

cicd-ex-c01-1.titleEn: Declare the Workflow name and push & pull_request trigger pair
cicd-ex-c01-1.promptEn: The starter workflow file currently uses a placeholder name `____` and only listens to `workflow_dispatch` (manual click), so the CI gate stays silent when developers push code or open Pull Requests! Do two things: (1) set a clear non-empty `name` (e.g., `Backend CI`), and (2) configure the `on:` block to trigger automatically on both `push` and `pull_request` events.
hintsEn: Replace `name: ____` with a descriptive name like `name: Backend CI`.

Under `on:`, declare `push:` (e.g., with `branches: [main]` or `{}`) and `pull_request:` (or use the array form `on: [push, pull_request]`). Note that map syntax requires child values such as `branches: [main]` or `{}`.

cicd-ex-c01-2.titleEn: Assign the standard ubuntu-latest virtual machine for the Job
cicd-ex-c01-2.promptEn: The `verify` Job currently specifies an invalid runner label (`runs-on: my-laptop-local`), leaving the Job stuck indefinitely in `Queued — Waiting for a runner to pick up this job` because GitHub cannot find any matching runner. Change `jobs.verify.runs-on` to the standard Linux VM `ubuntu-latest`.
hintsEn: Find the `runs-on:` line inside `jobs.verify`.
Replace `my-laptop-local` with `ubuntu-latest`.

cicd-ex-c01-3.titleEn: Order the 4 code verification Steps correctly inside a Job
cicd-ex-c01-3.promptEn: Complete the exact 4 sequential steps in `jobs.verify.steps` (`steps[0]` through `steps[3]`) following standard verification order: (0) fetch source code with `uses: actions/checkout@v4`, (1) install dependencies with `run: npm ci`, (2) check code standards with `run: npm run lint`, and (3) run tests with `run: npm test`.
hintsEn: The first Step (`steps[0]`) uses `uses: actions/checkout@v4` (note: never mix `uses` and `run` in the same step).
The next three Steps (`steps[1]`, `steps[2]`, `steps[3]`) use `run: npm ci`, `run: npm run lint`, and `run: npm test` respectively.

cicd-ex-c01-4.titleEn: Fix the Ephemeral Runner trap: make the test Job fully self-contained
cicd-ex-c01-4.promptEn: The previous author split `install` and `test` into 2 separate Jobs, assuming `jobs.test` would already see the code and `node_modules` from `jobs.install`! As a result, `jobs.test` boots on a brand-new empty VM and crashes right on `npm test`. Turn `jobs.test` into a complete, self-contained Job with 4 steps in order: (0) `actions/checkout@v4`, (1) `actions/setup-node@v4` with `node-version: "22"`, (2) `run: npm ci`, and (3) `run: npm test`.
hintsEn: Look at `jobs.lint` as a reference: each Job runs on a fresh VM, so `jobs.test` must also check out code, set up Node 22, and run `npm ci` before `npm test`.
Ensure `jobs.test.steps` contains all 4 items: `actions/checkout@v4` -> `actions/setup-node@v4` (`node-version: "22"`) -> `npm ci` -> `npm test`.

cicd-ex-c01-5.titleEn: Configure defaults.run.working-directory for the apps/backend subproject
cicd-ex-c01-5.promptEn: In this repository, the API source code and `package.json` live inside the `apps/backend` subdirectory rather than the repo root. The previous author tried adding a `- run: cd apps/backend` Step, which had no effect because every Step spawns a fresh subshell! Remove that redundant `cd` Step and declare `defaults.run.working-directory: apps/backend` at the Workflow level (root of the YAML file) so all `run:` commands execute automatically in `apps/backend`.
hintsEn: Add a `defaults:` block at the root level of the YAML file (at the same level as `name`, `on`, `jobs`): inside it add `run:` -> `working-directory: apps/backend`.
Delete the `Wrong cd attempt` Step (`run: cd apps/backend`) to keep the `steps` list clean.

C02.titleEn: Trunk-Based Development & 5 Causes of Local vs. CI Environment Drift
C02.summaryEn: Practice short-lived Trunk-Based Git branching workflows and fix 5 root causes of environment drift between a personal laptop and a CI Runner (Node latest, Watch mode, Timezone, Case-sensitivity, Worker OOM 137).

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
A common scenario in software development is when source code passes all tests on a personal machine but fails or hangs when pushed to a Pull Request. For a CI Pipeline to run reliably and deterministically, engineering teams need to combine two practices: ==a short-lived branching strategy (Trunk-Based Development)== and ==environment parity between local machines and the CI Runner==.

steps.headingEn: Five Common Causes of Divergent Results Between Local and CI Runners
steps.bodyEn:
Environment Drift happens because your personal MacBook/Windows machine (**16–32 GB RAM**, **case-insensitive** filesystem, **`Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` GMT+7** timezone, interactive keyboard) differs sharply from a standard GitHub-hosted Runner VM (`ubuntu-latest` Linux `ext4`, with only ==2 vCPU & 7 GB RAM==, completely headless with no screen or keyboard!):

```visual
kind: troubleshoot
title: "5 Nguyên nhân phổ biến gây lệch kết quả giữa máy cá nhân và CI Runner [!badge:amber:Must Know]"
subtitle: "Kiểm tra đúng 5 cấu hình này giúp xử lý phần lớn sự cố sai khác giữa môi trường Local và CI"
items:
  - symptom: "Hôm qua vẫn xanh, sáng nay mọi PR đồng loạt gãy native addon dù không sửa code"
    badge: "1. Trôi bản Node & npm"
    tone: rose
    cause: "Khai báo `node-version: latest` khiến CI tự kéo bản Node Major mới vừa phát hành, hoặc dùng `npm install` thay vì `npm ci`."
    fix: "Ghim cứng phiên bản LTS cụ thể `node-version: \"22\"` (hoặc đọc `.nvmrc` qua `node-version-file`) kết hợp `npm ci`."
    cmd: "node-version: \"22\" && npm ci"
  - symptom: "Step 'Run tests' quay vòng tròn suốt 360 phút (6 tiếng) không bao giờ kết thúc"
    badge: "2. Treo Watch Mode"
    tone: amber
    cause: "Gọi `npx vitest` (thiếu `run`) hoặc đặt `CI: false` khiến công cụ bật chế độ Watch tương tác ngồi chờ người nhấn phím `q` vô thời hạn."
    fix: "Luôn đặt biến `CI: true` trong `env:` và gọi tường minh lệnh chạy một lần `npx vitest run` (hoặc `npx jest --ci`)."
    cmd: "CI=true npx vitest run"
  - symptom: "Laptop macOS chạy êm, lên Ubuntu phát sinh lỗi: Cannot find module './UserCard'"
    badge: "3. Hoa/thường Linux ext4"
    tone: cyan
    cause: "Ổ đĩa APFS (macOS) / NTFS (Windows) mặc định không phân biệt hoa thường nên import `./UserCard` cho tệp `userCard.tsx` vẫn lọt; còn Linux `ext4` phân biệt tuyệt đối!"
    fix: "Bật cờ kiểm tra nghiêm ngặt tên tệp trong `tsconfig.json` để bắt lỗi ngay lúc gõ code trên máy cá nhân."
    cmd: "\"forceConsistentCasingInFileNames\": true"
  - symptom: "Snapshot ngày giờ trên máy cá nhân ra 15h, lên CI ra 8h làm vỡ bài test"
    badge: "4. Lệch múi giờ (TZ)"
    tone: sky
    cause: "Laptop đặt múi giờ Việt Nam (`GMT+7`), trong khi Runner đám mây dùng giờ chuẩn quốc tế `UTC` (`08:30Z` -> `getHours()` trả `8` thay vì `15`)."
    fix: "Ghim cứng biến môi trường `TZ: \"UTC\"` cho toàn bộ Job kiểm thử để kết quả xử lý `Date` đồng nhất toàn cầu."
    cmd: "TZ=UTC node -e \"console.log(new Date('2026-05-01T08:30:00Z').getHours())\" # -> 8"
  - symptom: "Bộ test TypeScript lớn đang chạy giữa chừng bị sập đột ngột với Exit Code 137"
    badge: "5. Tràn RAM Worker (OOM)"
    tone: rose
    cause: "Jest/Vitest đọc nhầm số nhân CPU vật lý của host mẹ (16–32 core) rồi đẻ 15 worker con ngốn 9 GB RAM, vượt trần 7 GB RAM của `ubuntu-latest` nên bị Linux OOM Killer bắn `SIGKILL` (`137`)."
    fix: "Giới hạn số worker khớp với ngân sách 2 vCPU của Runner kết hợp khoá trần bộ nhớ Heap V8 rõ ràng."
    cmd: "NODE_OPTIONS=\"--max-old-space-size=4096\" npx jest --ci --maxWorkers=2"
```

steps.headingEn: Standardized Configuration Against Environment Drift (Node.js, Python & Multi-Language)
steps.bodyEn:
> [!WARNING] Note on configuring single-run (Non-watch Mode) test commands
> Most modern test frameworks (Vitest, Jest, Playwright) check the `process.env.CI === "true"` environment variable to automatically disable interactive Watch Mode. If `CI: false` is misconfigured or the `run` subcommand is omitted, the process will sit waiting for keyboard input until it hits the **360-minute** timeout limit!

With just the 6-line configuration block below, you lock down all 3 standardized environment variables (`CI: true`, `TZ: UTC`, `NODE_OPTIONS`) along with a `--maxWorkers=2` cap tailored to the **2 vCPU / 7 GB RAM** budget of a Hosted Runner:

```yaml
- name: Run test suite within 2-vCPU / 7GB RAM runner budget
  env:
    CI: true
    TZ: UTC
    NODE_OPTIONS: "--max-old-space-size=4096"
  run: npx jest --ci --maxWorkers=2
```

> [!TIP] This anti-drift rule applies identically to Python, Go & Java!
> - **Python:** Always lock versions with `uv sync --frozen` (strictly reading `uv.lock`), set `TZ: UTC` when testing `datetime`, watch out for case-sensitive filenames on Linux (`import user_service` != `User_Service.py`), and cap `pytest -n 2` to avoid `Exit 137` RAM exhaustion.
> - **Go & Java:** Use `TZ=UTC go test -race ./...` (locked by `go.sum`) or cap JVM memory with `JAVA_OPTS: "-Xmx3g"` on Gradle/Maven so you don't exceed the CI VM's 7 GB RAM ceiling!

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **Trunk-Based Development:** Create short-lived branches (a few hours to 1–2 days), merge into `main` daily; use a **Feature Flag** to hide large features whose UI is not yet complete.
> - Linux `ext4` is strictly case-sensitive (`UserCard.tsx` != `userCard.tsx`) -> always enable `"forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true`.
> - Lock down the stability trio on a 2 vCPU / 7 GB RAM Runner: ==`node-version: "22"`== (avoid `latest`), ==`CI: true` + `TZ: UTC`==, and ==`--maxWorkers=2` + `--max-old-space-size=4096`== to eliminate `Exit Code 137`.

readings.noteEn: A workflow file containing 4 common configuration mistakes that cause a project to run fine locally yet use the wrong version or hang in CI.
readings.taskEn: Identify all 4 configuration mistakes marked in `github/local-vs-ci-drift.yml` and explain how to fix each one.
readings.answerEn: 1) Missing `timeout-minutes` (hangs for up to 360 minutes) -> add `timeout-minutes: 10`; 2) Floating `node-version: latest` -> pin `node-version: "22"`; 3) Loose `npm install` -> switch to `npm ci`; 4) Setting `CI: false` and calling `npx vitest` which hangs in watch mode -> set `CI: true` and run `npx vitest run`.

readings.noteEn: Compare against the reference configuration: includes `timeout-minutes: 10`, pinned `node-version: "22"`, `cache: "npm"` enabled, and deterministic installation via `npm ci`.
readings.taskEn: If your Unit Test suite handles dates (`new Date().toLocaleDateString()`), which environment variable should you add to the `verify` Job so results on a GMT+7 laptop and the Runner always match?
readings.answerEn: Add `env: { TZ: "UTC" }` to the Job (as well as your local test script) so all date/time calculations are normalized to UTC.

cicd-q-c02-1.qEn: What is the core philosophy of the Trunk-Based Development branching model when combined with modern CI/CD?
choicesEn: Each developer keeps a separate branch for 2–3 months and merges everything in one big batch at the end of the quarter
Create short-lived feature branches (a few hours to 1–2 days), validate automatically via PRs, and merge continuously into the `main` trunk
Delete the `main` branch entirely and push code straight from laptops to the Production server via FTP
Create a separate Git branch for every customer using the software
cicd-q-c02-1.explainEn: Trunk-Based Development minimizes the size of each merge, keeps CI fast, makes code reviews easy, and eliminates Merge Hell caused by long-lived branches.

cicd-q-c02-2.qEn: On a personal MacBook, `import Card from "./UserCard"` runs fine even though the actual file on disk is `userCard.tsx`, yet when pushed to an `ubuntu-latest` runner the `npm run build` step immediately fails with `Cannot find module "./UserCard"`. Why does this happen?
choicesEn: Because Ubuntu does not support React `.tsx` file extensions
Because macOS's default filesystem (APFS) is case-insensitive, whereas Linux's ext4 filesystem strictly distinguishes `UserCard` from `userCard`
Because `actions/checkout@v4` automatically renames all files to uppercase
Because the `TZ: UTC` environment variable is missing
cicd-q-c02-2.explainEn: Linux `ext4` is strictly case-sensitive (`UserCard.tsx` != `userCard.tsx`), while macOS/Windows are case-insensitive by default. Enabling `forceConsistentCasingInFileNames: true` in `tsconfig.json` catches this error immediately on developer machines.

cicd-q-c02-3.qEn: Specifying `node-version: latest` in `actions/setup-node@v4` is a Production best practice because it automatically upgrades the project to the newest Node.js release on launch day.
cicd-q-c02-3.explainEn: False! Using `latest` means that one fine morning when Node releases a new Major version with breaking changes, every Pull Request across the company breaks simultaneously even though nobody touched a line of code. Always pin a specific LTS version such as `"22"`.

cicd-q-c02-4.qEn: Why does running `npx vitest` with `CI: false` on an automated runner cause the Job to hang indefinitely and never finish?
choicesEn: Because Vitest automatically enters interactive Watch Mode and waits indefinitely for keyboard input in the terminal
Because Vitest has to download a 50 GB Chrome browser
Because GitHub blocks the `npx` command on Ubuntu
Because `CI: false` disables the VM's network interface
cicd-q-c02-4.explainEn: Without the `run` subcommand and with `CI` not set to `true`, `vitest` defaults to file-watching mode (watch mode) waiting for interactive keyboard input — which does not exist on a headless CI runner.

cicd-q-c02-5.qEn: With the environment variable `TZ=UTC` set, what hour number (`getHours()`) will the following Node.js expression print?
cicd-q-c02-5.explainEn: An ISO string ending in `Z` represents 08:30 in UTC. With `TZ=UTC`, `getHours()` returns exactly `8` on any machine worldwide (instead of returning `15` on a laptop set to Vietnam's GMT+7 timezone).

cicd-q-c02-6.qEn: A Jest test suite runs smoothly on a 32 GB RAM laptop but repeatedly crashes with `Exit Code 137` on a standard GitHub-hosted Runner (2 vCPU, 7 GB RAM). Which configuration pair directly fixes the root cause?
choicesEn: Append `|| true` after the `jest` command to ignore exit code 137
Cap child worker processes with `--maxWorkers=2` combined with an appropriate V8 heap limit via `NODE_OPTIONS: "--max-old-space-size=4096"`
Switch `npm ci` back to `npm install --force`
Disable TypeScript type checking completely
cicd-q-c02-6.explainEn: Capping `--maxWorkers=2` prevents Jest from spawning too many workers and exhausting the 2-core VM's 7 GB RAM, while `--max-old-space-size=4096` explicitly bounds V8 heap memory so the Linux OOM Killer won't send `SIGKILL` (137).

cicd-q-c02-7.qEn: When building a large feature whose UI takes 2 weeks to finish, a team practicing Trunk-Based Development can hide the unfinished feature behind a Feature Flag so they can still safely merge small daily increments into `main`.
cicd-q-c02-7.explainEn: True! Feature Flags decouple "code integration" (daily merges) from "enabling the feature for users" (release), keeping `main` always green and avoiding multi-week branches.

cicd-card-c02-1.frontEn: What principle does Trunk-Based Development use to solve the "Merge Hell" nightmare?
cicd-card-c02-1.backEn: Every developer creates short-lived branches (`short-lived branch` < 1–2 days) from `main`, validates automatically via small PRs, and merges back into `main` daily (using Feature Flags for multi-day features).

cicd-card-c02-2.frontEn: Name the 5 most common culprits behind "It works on my machine, but turns red on CI".
cicd-card-c02-2.backEn: 1) Node/npm version drift (`latest`, `npm install`); 2) Hanging Watch/Interactive prompts (`CI` not enabled); 3) Filename case-sensitivity on Linux; 4) Timezone drift (`TZ`); 5) Spawning too many test workers causing RAM exhaustion (`OOM 137`).

cicd-card-c02-3.frontEn: How does the `CI: true` environment variable affect Node.js tools like Vitest, Jest, Playwright, and npm?
cicd-card-c02-3.backEn: It signals an unattended automated environment: disables Watch Mode, automatically rejects interactive Y/n prompts, and turns off animated progress bars that pollute logs.

cicd-card-c02-4.frontEn: What are the default hardware specs of a standard `ubuntu-latest` GitHub-hosted Runner to keep in mind when tuning Node.js workers?
cicd-card-c02-4.backEn: Around 2–4 vCPUs and 7–16 GB RAM depending on the image generation (commonly 2 vCPU / 7 GB RAM on standard tiers), so letting Jest/Vitest spawn 8–16 parallel workers easily hits OOM 137.

cicd-card-c02-5.frontEn: How do you prevent date/time Snapshot test mismatches between a local laptop in Vietnam (`Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`) and the CI server?
cicd-card-c02-5.backEn: Set the `TZ: "UTC"` environment variable consistently in the CI Job configuration and in local test scripts.

cicd-card-c02-6.frontEn: Which modern Git command replaces `git checkout -b <branch>` for creating and switching to a new feature branch more explicitly?
cicd-card-c02-6.backEn: `git switch -c <branch>` (for example `git switch -c feat/healthz`), and use `git switch main` to return to the main branch.

cicd-ex-c02-1.titleEn: Practice the Short-Lived Trunk-Based Git Cycle and Tag v1.0.0
cicd-ex-c02-1.promptEn: The Git repository is currently on the `main` branch with 1 initial commit and an unstaged modified file `src/healthz.ts`. Complete the full **Trunk-Based Development** cycle: (1) create and switch to the short-lived branch `feat/healthz` (`git switch -c feat/healthz`), (2) stage the file (`git add .`) and create a commit (`git commit -m "feat: add healthz"`), (3) switch back to `main` (`git switch main`), merge `feat/healthz` into `main` (`git merge feat/healthz`), and (4) create the release tag `v1.0.0` (`git tag v1.0.0`).
hintsEn: Use `git switch -c feat/healthz`, followed by `git add .` and `git commit -m "feat: add healthz"`.
Return to the main branch with `git switch main`, merge the code with `git merge feat/healthz`, and finally tag the milestone with `git tag v1.0.0`.

cicd-ex-c02-2.titleEn: Pin Node.js 22 LTS to Replace the Floating latest Tag
cicd-ex-c02-2.promptEn: The workflow currently sets `node-version: latest` in the `actions/setup-node@v4` step (`jobs.test.steps[1]`), causing a newly released Node version this morning to break a crypto library in CI even though developer machines running Node 22 LTS still pass. Pin `node-version` to `"22"` (or `22`, `"22.x"`).
hintsEn: Locate the path `jobs.test.steps[1].with.node-version`.
Replace `latest` with `"22"` to match the project's Node.js 22 LTS version.

cicd-ex-c02-3.titleEn: Fix Pipeline Hanging Caused by Vitest Running in Watch Mode
cicd-ex-c02-3.promptEn: The `unit` Job is hanging for hours on its final step (`steps[3]`) because the author set `env.CI: false` and invoked `npx vitest` without the `run` flag, causing Vitest to enter Watch Mode waiting for keyboard input! Fix it by: (1) changing `jobs.unit.env.CI` to `true`, and (2) updating the command in `jobs.unit.steps[3].run` to `npx vitest run`.
hintsEn: Change `CI: false` under `jobs.unit.env` to `CI: true`.
Update `run: npx vitest` in the last step to `run: npx vitest run` so it runs once and exits with a proper Exit Code.

cicd-ex-c02-4.titleEn: Standardize Timezone TZ=UTC to Stop Date Snapshot Failures
cicd-ex-c02-4.promptEn: Payment invoice Snapshot Tests pass on developers' laptops in Ho Chi Minh City (`Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh`) but fail in CI due to shifted order dates. The team has agreed to standardize all tests to `UTC`. Set the environment variable `jobs.test.env.TZ` to `"UTC"`.
hintsEn: Locate the `TZ` key inside `jobs.test.env`.
Change `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` to `UTC` (or `"UTC"`).

cicd-ex-c02-5.titleEn: Fix Worker OOM (Exit Code 137) on a 2-vCPU Runner
cicd-ex-c02-5.promptEn: The project's large test suite invokes `npx jest --maxWorkers=16` with a memory limit of only `256` MB, causing processes to repeatedly crash mid-run with `Exit Code 137` (OOM) or V8 Heap exhaustion on the 2-vCPU runner. Fix `jobs.test` by: (1) setting `jobs.test.env.NODE_OPTIONS` to `"--max-old-space-size=4096"`, and (2) adjusting the flag in `jobs.test.steps[3].run` to `--maxWorkers=2`.
hintsEn: Update `jobs.test.env.NODE_OPTIONS` to `"--max-old-space-size=4096"`.
Change `--maxWorkers=16` in `jobs.test.steps[3].run` to `--maxWorkers=2` to fit the 2-vCPU VM.

C03.titleEn: Building a Standard GitHub Actions Workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
C03.summaryEn: Build a complete .github/workflows/ci.yml from scratch: smart push/PR branch filtering, upgrading to checkout@v4 & setup-node@v4 with npm caching, running the npm ci/build/test pipeline, and adding a manual workflow_dispatch trigger.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
Once you understand Exit Codes, Ephemeral Runners, and environment parity principles, you are ready to build a complete, **production-grade GitHub Actions Workflow** from scratch. Be careful not to copy outdated 2020–2022 tutorials that use legacy Actions (`v1`–`v3`) or `node-version: 16`, as those older runtimes on Hosted Runners have reached End of Life (EOL) and will fail.

steps.headingEn: Structure of .github/workflows/ci.yml and YAML Syntax Rules
steps.bodyEn:
GitHub only automatically discovers files with the `.yml` or `.yaml` extension placed inside the exact ==`.github/workflows/`== directory path. If the folder name is misspelled (for instance missing the `s`, like `.github/workflow/ci.yml`) or indented with **hard Tab (`\t`)** characters, the configuration file will be ignored or immediately fail with a syntax error (always use **2 spaces** per indentation level).

```visual
kind: anatomy
title: "Các từ khóa cốt lõi trong Workflow GitHub Actions [!badge:cyan:GitHub Actions v4]"
subtitle: "Đọc từ trên xuống dưới theo cấu trúc chuẩn của tệp .github/workflows/ci.yml"
items:
  - keyword: "on.push / pull_request"
    role: "Bộ lọc sự kiện & nhánh"
    tone: amber
    summary: "Xác định thời điểm kích hoạt tự động và lọc theo nhánh đích để chống chạy trùng lặp."
    bullets:
      - "Luôn lọc rõ `branches: [main]` cho cả `push` lẫn `pull_request`"
    example: "on: { push: { branches: [main] }, pull_request: { branches: [main] } }"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: "workflow_dispatch"
    role: "Nút bấm chạy thủ công"
    tone: cyan
    summary: "Hiển thị nút 'Run workflow' kèm menu chọn tham số ngay trên giao diện Web của GitHub."
    bullets:
      - "Định nghĩa tham số đầu vào qua `inputs:` (ví dụ `type: choice`, `default: \"staging\"`)"
      - "Đọc lại giá trị người dùng chọn bằng biểu thức `${{ inputs.target_env }}`"
    example: "echo \"Target=${{ inputs.target_env }}\""
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: "runs-on"
    role: "Chọn hệ điều hành máy ảo"
    tone: sky
    summary: "Yêu cầu GitHub cấp phát một máy ảo Ephemeral Runner sạch cho Job."
    bullets:
      - "`ubuntu-latest` là lựa chọn tiêu chuẩn nhanh và tiết kiệm chi phí nhất cho Node.js Backend"
    example: "runs-on: ubuntu-latest"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: "actions/checkout@v4"
    role: "Tải mã nguồn nông (Shallow)"
    tone: cyan
    summary: "Kéo mã nguồn của commit hiện tại về thư mục làm việc của Runner."
    bullets:
      - "Mặc định chỉ tải 1 commit mới nhất (**`fetch-depth: 1`**) để khởi động xong trong 1–2 giây"
      - "Chỉ truyền `with: { fetch-depth: 0 }` khi dùng công cụ cần toàn bộ lịch sử Git (SonarQube, semantic-release, Turborepo)"
    example: "- uses: actions/checkout@v4"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: "actions/setup-node@v4"
    role: "Cài Node 22 & Đệm ~/.npm"
    tone: emerald
    summary: "Cài đặt phiên bản Node.js LTS hiện đại và tự động quản lý bộ đệm gói thư viện."
    bullets:
      - "Ghim rõ `node-version: \"22\"` (tránh các bản 14/16/18 đã End-of-Life)"
      - "Bật `cache: \"npm\"` để tự băm SHA-256 của `package-lock.json` làm khoá đệm thư mục `~/.npm`"
    example: "with: { node-version: \"22\", cache: \"npm\" }"
    lang: yaml
```

steps.headingEn: The @v4 Actions Standard and Built-in cache: "npm" Mechanism
steps.bodyEn:
JavaScript Actions execute directly on the Runner's embedded Node.js runtime. Legacy `@v2` / `@v3` versions rely on Node 12 and Node 16 runtimes that have reached End of Life (EOL) on GitHub-hosted Runners. In 2026, the mandatory standard is upgrading across the board to **`@v4`** paired with **Node `"22"` LTS**:

| Component | Outdated Legacy (2020–2022) | Mandatory 2026 Standard | Core Technical Reason |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Checkout Git Source** | Legacy `checkout` (`v1`–`v3`) | **`actions/checkout@v4`** | Runs on modern Node 20+ runtime; defaults to ultra-fast shallow clone `fetch-depth: 1` |
| **Setup Node.js** | Legacy `setup-node` (`v1`–`v3`) | **`actions/setup-node@v4`** | Seamless Node 22 LTS compatibility; built-in `~/.npm` caching in 1 line |
| **Node Version** | `14`, `16`, `18` (EOL) | **`"22"` (Active/Maintenance LTS)** | Latest V8 security patches, built-in native `fetch`, `--env-file`, and ESM/CJS support |

> [!WARNING] Mandatory Requirement When Enabling `cache: "npm"` in `actions/setup-node@v4`
> Under the hood, `cache: "npm"` computes the SHA-256 hash of ==`package-lock.json`== (or `npm-shrinkwrap.json`) as the cache key for the global `~/.npm` cache directory (containing compressed `.tgz` packages). If your repository forgot to commit `package-lock.json` to Git, the `setup-node@v4` step will immediately fail saying the lockfile cannot be found!

Beyond automated Git events, when an operations engineer wants to **manually click a button in the GitHub Web UI to trigger checks** (without pushing an empty commit `git commit --allow-empty`), add `workflow_dispatch` with `inputs` to the complete `.github/workflows/ci.yml` file:

```yaml
name: Node.js 22 CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      target_env:
        description: "Môi trường đích cần kiểm tra"
        required: true
        default: "staging"
        type: choice
        options: [staging, qa, production]

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: "npm"
      - run: echo "Target=${{ inputs.target_env }}"
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npm test
```

> [!TIP] `workflow_dispatch` Default Value Behavior & Extending to Python / Go
> - When an engineer opens the **Actions -> Run workflow** tab and clicks run without changing the dropdown/input, `${{ inputs.target_env }}` automatically receives `default: "staging"` (so the `echo` command above prints `Target=staging`).
> - If tomorrow you switch to a **Python** or **Go** project, 95% of the YAML skeleton above stays identical: simply swap `setup-node@v4` + `npm ci` for `astral-sh/setup-uv@v5` (`enable-cache: true`) + `uv sync --frozen && uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest` (for Python), or `actions/setup-go@v5` + `go test ./...` (for Go)!

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - Place files in **`.github/workflows/*.yml`**, indented with **2 spaces** (never Tabs).
> - Combine `push.branches: [main]` and `pull_request.branches: [main]` (filtering by **target / base branch**) to prevent running twice on PRs.
> - Standardize on **`actions/checkout@v4`** (default `fetch-depth: 1`) and **`actions/setup-node@v4`** (`node-version: "22"`, `cache: "npm"` hashed from `package-lock.json`).

readings.noteEn: Reference 2026 blueprint for `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: filters `main`, grants least-privilege `contents: read`, uses the `@v4` pair, and enables `cache: "npm"`.
readings.taskEn: When configuring `cache: "npm"` in `actions/setup-node@v4`, which directory is actually cached: the project's `node_modules/` or the global `~/.npm` cache directory?
readings.answerEn: The global `~/.npm` cache directory (containing compressed npm `.tgz` tarballs) is cached keyed on the hash of `package-lock.json`, allowing `npm ci` to perform a clean extraction and integrity check at high speed without risking cross-architecture binary mismatches.

readings.noteEn: Legacy 2020–2022 workflow pattern commonly found in older un-upgraded repositories.
readings.taskEn: If you run `legacy-v2-set-output.yml` as-is on a GitHub-hosted Runner in 2026, which lines are deprecated/unsupported and what versions must they be upgraded to?
readings.answerEn: `actions/checkout@v2` and `actions/setup-node@v2` (running on legacy Node 12/16 runtimes) must be upgraded to `@v4`; `node-version: "16"` (EOL) must be upgraded to `"22"`; and `::set-output` on line 24 has been disabled so it must be rewritten to append to `"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`.

cicd-q-c03-1.qEn: Which directory path in a Git repository is mandatory for GitHub to automatically detect and execute GitHub Actions Workflow configuration files?
choicesEn: `.github/actions/*.yml`
`.github/workflows/*.yml` (or `*.yaml`)
`ci/pipelines/*.yml`
`workflows/github/*.json`
cicd-q-c03-1.explainEn: All GitHub Actions workflow files must be placed directly inside `.github/workflows/` with a `.yml` or `.yaml` extension.

cicd-q-c03-2.qEn: When you configure the filter `on.pull_request.branches: [main]`, what happens if a teammate opens a Pull Request from branch `feat/payment-qr` targeting `main`?
choicesEn: The workflow does NOT run because the teammate's branch is named `feat/payment-qr` rather than `main`
The workflow AUTOMATICALLY RUNS because `pull_request.branches` filters on the target (base) branch, which is `main`
The workflow only runs after the PR has been merged
GitHub throws an error because you cannot use the same branch name `main` under `pull_request`
cicd-q-c03-2.explainEn: For the `pull_request` event, the `branches:` filter applies to the target (base) branch. Every PR from any `feat/*` or `fix/*` branch targeting `main` will be checked automatically!

cicd-q-c03-3.qEn: Writing a bare `on: [push, pull_request]` without branch filters causes every commit pushed to a branch with an open PR to trigger 2 identical duplicate workflow runs, doubling CI minute usage.
cicd-q-c03-3.explainEn: True! Combining `push: branches: [main]` with `pull_request: branches: [main]` ensures a PR triggers only 1 verification run per code update.

cicd-q-c03-4.qEn: Why must we upgrade `actions/checkout@v2` and `actions/setup-node@v3` to `@v4` in 2026?
choicesEn: Because `@v2`/`@v3` use JSON syntax instead of YAML
Because older versions run on Node 12/16 runtimes that have reached End of Life (EOL) on GitHub-hosted Runners, while `@v4` uses a modern, faster, and more secure runtime
Because `@v4` automatically writes Unit Tests for the project
Because `@v2` only runs on Windows
cicd-q-c03-4.explainEn: GitHub has deprecated Node 12 and Node 16 runtimes for JavaScript Actions on Hosted Runners; `@v4` updates to a modern runtime with security fixes and faster download speeds.

cicd-q-c03-5.qEn: When enabling `cache: "npm"` inside `actions/setup-node@v4`, which file in the repository does the Action use by default to generate its hashed cache key?
choicesEn: `README.md`
`tsconfig.json`
`package-lock.json` (or `npm-shrinkwrap.json`)
`.gitignore`
cicd-q-c03-5.explainEn: `setup-node@v4` automatically hashes `package-lock.json` as the cache key for `~/.npm`. If you forget to commit `package-lock.json` to Git, `cache: "npm"` will error out!

cicd-q-c03-6.qEn: Given the `workflow_dispatch` configuration below, if an engineer clicks **Run workflow** in the GitHub UI and leaves the default value unchanged, what string will the `run` step print?
cicd-q-c03-6.explainEn: When triggered manually via `workflow_dispatch` without editing the input field, `inputs.target_env` receives `default: "staging"`, so `echo` prints `Target=staging`.

cicd-q-c03-7.qEn: By default, `actions/checkout@v4` fetches only the single latest commit (`fetch-depth: 1` — shallow clone) instead of the entire history of thousands of commits to save bandwidth and job startup time.
cicd-q-c03-7.explainEn: Correct! The default `fetch-depth: 1` lets the checkout step finish in just 1–2 seconds. Only when tools need to compare Git history (like SonarQube, semantic-release, or Turborepo affected) should you pass `with: { fetch-depth: 0 }`.

cicd-card-c03-1.frontEn: What is the standard `on` configuration to avoid running twice when pushing to a feature branch with an open PR targeting `main`?
cicd-card-c03-1.backEn: Set `on.push.branches: [main]` and `on.pull_request.branches: [main]` — PRs run once per update, and `push` only runs after merging into `main`.

cicd-card-c03-2.frontEn: What is the official 2026 Action pair for checking out code and installing Node.js 22 with caching on GitHub Actions?

cicd-card-c03-3.frontEn: What is the prerequisite in a Git repo for `cache: "npm"` in `actions/setup-node@v4` to work without errors?
cicd-card-c03-3.backEn: The `package-lock.json` lockfile must be committed to the Git repository so the Action can hash it to compute the cache key.

cicd-card-c03-4.frontEn: Which trigger event creates a **Run workflow** button with an input form in the GitHub Web UI?

cicd-card-c03-5.frontEn: Why should TypeScript projects include `npm run build` alongside `npm test` in CI?
cicd-card-c03-5.backEn: Many modern test runners (like Vitest/SWC) transpile TS rapidly while skipping strict type checking (`tsc`); running `npm run build` verifies both TypeScript type checking and the `dist/` bundle.

cicd-card-c03-6.frontEn: When do you need to pass `fetch-depth: 0` to `actions/checkout@v4`?
cicd-card-c03-6.backEn: When downstream steps need full Git history or base branches (e.g., `git diff origin/main`, automated changelog generators, or commit history scanners), because `checkout@v4` defaults to a shallow `fetch-depth: 1`.

cicd-ex-c03-1.promptEn: Complete a minimal valid skeleton for the project's first `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: (1) set a non-empty `name` (replace `____`), (2) trigger on the `push` event in the `on` block, and (3) set `jobs.ci.runs-on` to `ubuntu-latest`.
hintsEn: Set `name: Node CI` and change `on: []` to `on: [push]` (or `on:\n  push:\n    branches: [main]`).
Change `runs-on: ____` under `jobs.ci` to `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`.

cicd-ex-c03-2.titleEn: Filter main for Both push and pull_request to Prevent Double Runs
cicd-ex-c03-2.promptEn: Currently `on: [push, pull_request]` causes every commit on a branch with an open PR to run twice, wasting double CI minutes. Restructure the `on:` block into an object so both `on.push.branches` and `on.pull_request.branches` specify the array `["main"]`.
hintsEn: Replace `on: [push, pull_request]` with an `on:` block containing two child keys: `push:` and `pull_request:`.
Under each child key, declare `branches: ["main"]` (indented by 4 spaces).

cicd-ex-c03-3.promptEn: You just inherited an older service written in 2021 that still calls `actions/checkout@v2` (running on the Node 12 runtime, which is no longer supported on GitHub-hosted Runners). Upgrade the checkout step in `jobs.verify` to `actions/checkout@v4`.
hintsEn: Locate `uses: actions/checkout@v2` in the first step of `jobs.verify`.
Change `@v2` to `@v4`.

cicd-ex-c03-4.titleEn: Configure actions/setup-node@v4 with Node 22 and npm Cache

C04.titleEn: Environment Variables (env), $GITHUB_OUTPUT, if: Conditionals & Path Filtering
C04.summaryEn: Master the 3 env variable scopes, pass outputs via $GITHUB_OUTPUT, control execution with if: failure() / github.ref, filter paths with paths-ignore, and prevent infinite push loops.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
A static workflow file that simply runs top-to-bottom is like a function with no parameters, no `return`, and no `if/else`. To build flexible CI Pipelines — passing version tags between steps, automatically collecting error logs when E2E tests fail, and skipping runs when only `README.md` documentation changes — you need to master the 4 core flow-control mechanisms in GitHub Actions.

```visual

subtitle: "Truyền dữ liệu an toàn giữa các bước/Job và điều hướng thông minh khi pipeline gặp lỗi hoặc chỉ sửa tài liệu"
caption: "Thứ tự ưu tiên ghi đè biến môi trường (Step > Job > Workflow), luồng xuất biến qua $GITHUB_OUTPUT và các hàm kiểm tra trạng thái thực thi"
callouts:

    label: "Tháp phạm vi env: & Che giấu secrets.*"
```
