steps.headingEn: 3-Tier Environment Variable Hierarchy (env:): Override Precedence
steps.bodyEn:
Similar to *Lexical Scope* in JavaScript (where a local variable inside a function shadows an outer global variable), GitHub Actions lets you declare `env:` blocks across **3 hierarchical levels**:

```visual
kind: layers
title: "Tháp Ưu Tiên 3 Tầng Biến Môi Trường (env:) Trong GitHub Actions"
subtitle: "Khi trùng tên biến (ví dụ STAGE), tầng có phạm vi hẹp nhất sẽ luôn thắng tuyệt đối!"
columns:
  - title: "Thứ Tự Ghi Đè Từ Cao Xuống Thấp"
    badge: "Step > Job > Workflow"
    tone: emerald
    layers:
      - label: "Tầng 3: Step env (steps[i].env) — ƯU TIÊN CAO NHẤT"
        sub: "Chỉ sống trong duy nhất tiến trình của Step đó · Ghi đè cả Job lẫn Workflow"
        note: "Thắng tuyệt đối!"
        tone: emerald
      - label: "Tầng 2: Job env (jobs.<job_id>.env) — ƯU TIÊN TRUNG BÌNH"
        sub: "Áp dụng cho mọi Step bên trong Job đó · Ghi đè tầng Workflow"
        note: "Phạm vi cấp Job"
        tone: sky
      - label: "Tầng 1: Workflow env (Gốc tệp YAML) — ƯU TIÊN THẤP NHẤT"
        sub: "Đặt ngang hàng on: và jobs: · Giá trị mặc định chung cho toàn bộ tệp"
        note: "Mặc định toàn cục"
        tone: slate
    footer: "Trong khối run: đọc qua biến Shell $STAGE · Ở các trường YAML (if:, with:) đọc qua ${{ env.STAGE }}"
```

```yaml
env:
  STAGE: "global"             # Tầng 1: Mặc định toàn cục
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      STAGE: "job-level"      # Tầng 2: Ghi đè "global"
    steps:
      - env:
          STAGE: "step-level" # Tầng 3: Ghi đè cả 2 tầng trên!
        run: echo "$STAGE"    # -> Kết quả in ra: step-level
```

steps.headingEn: Passing Data Between Steps Using the "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" Environment File
steps.bodyEn:
In CI, each Step runs in its own isolated subshell process, so running `export SHA=abc` in Step 1 vanishes completely by Step 2!

> [!WARNING] Security Warning: Permanently Remove Legacy `::set-output` Commands!
> Before 2023, many older tutorials showed printing the special `::set-output` command to `stdout`. GitHub has **completely removed that legacy mechanism** due to a **Command Injection** vulnerability (input containing newline characters `\n` could inject spoofed workflow commands into the Runner).

The mandatory 2026 standard is to assign an `id:` to the producing Step and append (`>>`) `key=value` pairs to the ==`"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`== environment file (or write to ==`"$GITHUB_ENV"`== to dynamically inject environment variables into subsequent Steps within the same Job):

```visual
kind: flow
title: "Cơ Chế Truyền Đầu Ra An Toàn Giữa Các Step Trong Cùng Một Job"
steps:
  - icon: terminal
    badge: "Step phát (id: build_meta)"
    title: "Ghi Vào $GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    desc: "Nối chuỗi key=value vào đường dẫn tệp tạm được bảo vệ của Runner"
    code: "echo \"image_tag=v1.2.0\" >> \"$GITHUB_OUTPUT\""
    tone: sky
    edge: "Runner lưu trữ"
  - icon: lock
    badge: "Bộ nhớ ngữ cảnh"
    title: "steps.<id>.outputs"
    desc: "GitHub tách biệt dữ liệu an toàn khỏi luồng log stdout thông thường"
    code: "steps.build_meta.outputs"
    tone: cyan
    edge: "biểu thức ${{ }}"
  - icon: rocket
    badge: "Step nhận phía sau"
    title: "Đọc Giá Trị Đã Xuất"
    desc: "Sử dụng ở bất kỳ Step kế tiếp nào bên trong cùng Job đó"
    code: "${{ steps.build_meta.outputs.image_tag }}"
    tone: emerald
```

```yaml
steps:
  - name: Compute short commit SHA
    id: meta
    run: echo "sha=${GITHUB_SHA::7}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  - name: Print Docker tag
    run: echo "Image tag will be app:${{ steps.meta.outputs.sha }}"
```

steps.headingEn: if: Conditional Expressions and the 4 Execution Status Functions
steps.bodyEn:
By default, every Step carries an implicit `if: success()` condition. To control branching logic — such as publishing only on merges to `main` (`if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'`) or collecting failure diagnostics — you need to know the **4 status check functions**:

```visual
kind: groups
title: "4 Hàm Kiểm Tra Trạng Thái Trong Điều Kiện if: [!badge:violet:Flow Control]"
columns: 2
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: check
    title: "success() — Mặc định ngầm"
    badge: "Khi mọi bước trước đều đạt"
    tone: emerald
    bullets:
      - "Tự động áp dụng nếu bạn không viết dòng `if:` nào"
      - "Chỉ trả `true` khi tất cả các Step phía trên trong Job đều kết thúc với `Exit Code 0`"
  - num: 2
    icon: alert
    title: "failure()"
    badge: "Chỉ chạy khi có bước bị lỗi"
    tone: rose
    bullets:
      - "Trả `true` khi bất kỳ Step nào phía trước bị thất bại"
      - "**Ứng dụng thực tế:** Gắn vào bước `Upload Playwright Screenshots` hoặc gửi cảnh báo Slack để thu thập dữ liệu chẩn đoán ngay khi bài test E2E thất bại."
  - num: 3
    icon: refresh
    title: "always()"
    badge: "Chạy bất chấp đạt, lỗi hay Cancel"
    tone: amber
    bullets:
      - "Luôn thực thi kể cả khi bước trước lỗi hoặc người dùng bấm nút **Cancel** huỷ Job"
      - "Thích hợp cho bước dọn dẹp hạ tầng tạm thời (xóa test container/cloud sandbox tránh tốn chi phí)"
  - num: 4
    icon: shield-check
    title: "!cancelled()"
    badge: "Chạy cả khi đạt lẫn lỗi (trừ khi Cancel)"
    tone: sky
    bullets:
      - "Kết hợp hàm `cancelled()`: chạy khi Job thành công HOẶC thất bại, nhưng dừng ngay nếu người dùng chủ động huỷ ngang"
      - "Lựa chọn phù hợp để tải báo cáo HTML tổng hợp ở cuối bộ kiểm thử"
```

steps.headingEn: Path Filters (paths / paths-ignore) & Preventing Infinite Push Loops
steps.bodyEn:
To avoid wasting CI minutes on commits that only edit text documentation:
- [x] **`paths-ignore: ["**.md", "docs/**"]`**: Skips the entire workflow if every modified file in the commit/PR matches the exclusion list.
- [x] **`paths: ["apps/api/**", "packages/shared/**"]`**: Only triggers the API service checks when relevant files are modified.
- [!] **Mandatory Syntax Rule:** You cannot specify both `paths:` and `paths-ignore:` together on the same `on.push` event. If you need both inclusion and exclusion in the same event, use `paths:` alone with the negation prefix ==`!`== (e.g., `paths: ["apps/api/**", "!apps/api/**.md"]`).

> [!WARNING] Preventing Infinite Self-Triggering Loops (Infinite Push Loop)
> If a Job triggered by `on: push` edits `CHANGELOG.md` or bumps a version number and then runs `git commit` and `git push` using a **Personal Access Token (PAT)**, GitHub treats that push as a human user pushing code, emits a new `push` event, and triggers the exact same workflow in an endless loop.
>
> Always prevent this with **3 safeguards**:
> 1. Prefer the default **`GITHUB_TOKEN`** (events created by `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger new workflow runs).
> 2. Include **`[skip ci]`** in automated bot commit messages.
> 3. Add `paths-ignore` filters or an `if: github.actor != 'release-bot'` condition.

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - `env:` precedence order: **`step.env` > `job.env` > `workflow.env`**.
> - 2026 standard for passing outputs between Steps: `echo "key=val" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` -> read via `${{ steps.<id>.outputs.<key> }}` (never use `::set-output`).
> - Use `if: failure()` to upload screenshots/logs only on failure · `if: always()` to clean up temporary resources even if cancelled.
> - Never combine `paths` and `paths-ignore` at the same level · Watch out for **Infinite Push Loops** when running `git push` with a PAT!

readings.noteEn: Reference workflow combining all 4 techniques: `paths-ignore` to skip Markdown files, writing `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` to pass tags between 2 Jobs, and automatically collecting error logs with `if: failure()`.
readings.taskEn: In the `test-and-package` Job, if all Unit Tests on line 42 pass GREEN (`Exit Code 0`), will the `Thu thập nhật ký lỗi` step on line 45 run? Why does this save Artifact storage?
readings.answerEn: No, it will not run! `if: failure()` only evaluates to `true` when at least one previous step in the Job has failed. When tests pass completely, the upload step is `Skipped`, avoiding wasted Artifact storage.

readings.noteEn: Side-by-side comparison showing `echo "::set-output name=short_sha::..."`, which GitHub disabled due to security vulnerabilities.
readings.taskEn: Rewrite the exact `run:` line in the `id: vars` Step (line 24) using the 2026 `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` standard while keeping the downstream `${{ steps.vars.outputs.short_sha }}` expression on line 27 unchanged.
readings.answerEn: Replace it with `run: echo "short_sha=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` — keeping `id: vars` and the key name `short_sha` identical so subsequent steps continue reading it without modification.

readings.noteEn: Misconfiguration scenario that continuously burns CI resources because the Job commits and pushes back to `main` using a PAT.
readings.taskEn: Why does switching `token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_BOT_PAT_PLACEHOLDER }}` back to the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` or adding `[skip ci]` to the commit message on line 26 break the infinite loop?
readings.answerEn: By GitHub's anti-loop design, events generated by the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger new `on: push` workflows; additionally, `[skip ci]` in the commit message instructs GitHub's scheduler to skip creating a CI run for that automated commit.

cicd-q-c04-1.qEn: Given the 3-tier hierarchical environment variable configuration below, what string value will the `echo` command in the Step print?
cicd-q-c04-1.explainEn: Following the narrowest-to-broadest scoping rule in GitHub Actions: `step.env` has the highest precedence, overriding both `job.env` and `workflow.env`, so `$STAGE` resolves to `step-level`.

cicd-q-c04-2.qEn: Which syntax is the 2026 standard for a Step with `id: build_meta` to emit an output variable named `image_tag` so later Steps can read `${{ steps.build_meta.outputs.image_tag }}`?
choicesEn: `echo "::set-output name=image_tag::v1.2.0"`
`export image_tag="v1.2.0"`
`echo "image_tag=v1.2.0" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`
`return { image_tag: "v1.2.0" }`
cicd-q-c04-2.explainEn: Appending `key=value` to the `"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` environment file is the sole officially supported standard replacing the removed `::set-output` command.

cicd-q-c04-3.qEn: You want the `Upload Playwright Screenshots` step to trigger ONLY when the preceding E2E test step fails (to capture failure screenshots). Which conditional expression should you attach to the upload step?
choicesEn: `if: success()`
`if: failure()`
`if: cancelled()`
`if: false`
cicd-q-c04-3.explainEn: The `failure()` function returns `true` whenever any preceding step in the Job fails, bypassing the default skip behavior so logs/screenshots are collected in time.

cicd-q-c04-4.qEn: If you need a temporary resource cleanup step (such as tearing down a cloud test environment) to ALWAYS run regardless of whether previous steps passed, failed, or were cancelled by the user, you should use `if: always()`.
cicd-q-c04-4.explainEn: True! `if: always()` guarantees the cleanup step still executes even if the Job fails or is cancelled mid-run (unless the physical runner host loses connectivity entirely).

cicd-q-c04-5.qEn: Which configuration prevents a Workflow from wasting CI minutes when a commit only edits `README.md` or guide files inside the `docs/` folder?
choicesEn: Use `branches-ignore: ["**.md", "docs/**"]`
Use `paths-ignore: ["**.md", "docs/**"]` under the `push` / `pull_request` event
Set `env: IGNORE_DOCS: true`
Remove `actions/checkout@v4` from the Job
cicd-q-c04-5.explainEn: `paths-ignore` inspects the list of changed file paths in the commit/PR: if EVERY changed file matches the exclusion patterns (`**.md`, `docs/**`), the entire workflow is skipped immediately.

cicd-q-c04-6.qEn: Within the same `on.push` event, you can declare both `paths:` and `paths-ignore:` side by side.
cicd-q-c04-6.explainEn: False! GitHub Actions forbids using both `paths` and `paths-ignore` on the same event. If you need both inclusion and exclusion in a single event, use `paths:` with the `!` negation prefix (e.g., `["apps/api/**", "!apps/api/**.md"]`).

cicd-q-c04-7.qEn: What is the root cause of an "Infinite Push Loop" (endless CI runs) when automatically updating a version file inside a Job?
choicesEn: Enabling `cache: "npm"` in `setup-node@v4`
A Job triggered by `on: push` runs `git commit` and `git push` using a Personal Access Token (PAT) without `[skip ci]` or a bot-exclusion condition
Using `npm ci` instead of `npm install`
Setting `timeout-minutes: 10`
cicd-q-c04-7.explainEn: Pushing with a PAT is treated by GitHub as a real user action, emitting a new `push` event. Without `[skip ci]`, `paths-ignore`, or a `github.actor` filter, it creates an infinite recursive loop.

cicd-card-c04-1.frontEn: What is the precedence order from highest to lowest for the 3 `env:` levels in GitHub Actions?
cicd-card-c04-1.backEn: `Step env` (highest) -> `Job env` -> `Workflow env` (lowest). A variable in a narrower scope overrides one with the same name in a broader scope.

cicd-card-c04-2.frontEn: How do you pass a dynamic value from Step A to Step B within the same Job using the 2026 standard?
cicd-card-c04-2.backEn: Assign `id: step_a` to Step A, run `echo "key=val" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`, and read it in Step B via `${{ steps.step_a.outputs.key }}`.

cicd-card-c04-3.frontEn: What is the difference between the 3 status functions `success()`, `failure()`, and `always()` in `if:` expressions?
cicd-card-c04-3.backEn: `success()` (default): runs only if all prior steps passed; `failure()`: runs only if a prior step failed; `always()`: runs in all cases (passed, failed, or cancelled).

cicd-card-c04-4.frontEn: Which `if:` expression guarantees a release Step only executes when code is pushed directly to `main` (and never on Pull Requests)?

cicd-card-c04-5.frontEn: When should you use `paths-ignore` vs. `paths` on `push` / `pull_request` events?
cicd-card-c04-5.backEn: Use `paths-ignore` (e.g., `**.md`, `docs/**`) in a single-app repo to skip documentation edits; use `paths` (e.g., `apps/api/**`) in a Monorepo to run a service's workflow only when its code changes.

cicd-card-c04-6.frontEn: Name the 2 simplest safeguards to stop a Job that runs `git push` from triggering itself endlessly.
cicd-card-c04-6.backEn: 1) Add `[skip ci]` to the automated commit message (`git commit -m "chore: release [skip ci]"`); 2) Use the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` or filter with `paths-ignore` / `if: github.actor != ...`.

cicd-ex-c04-1.titleEn: Declare Hierarchical Environment Variables at the Workflow and Step Levels
cicd-ex-c04-1.promptEn: Configure environment variables at the proper scopes for the test pipeline: (1) at the Workflow level (root of the YAML file), declare `env.NODE_ENV: "test"` shared across all Jobs, and (2) in the API test step (`jobs.verify.steps[3]`), declare a step-scoped variable `env.API_URL: "http://localhost:3000"`.

Inside step 4 (`Run API smoke tests` — `jobs.verify.steps[3]`), add `env:\n  API_URL: "http://localhost:3000"` at the same level as `name` and `run`.

cicd-ex-c04-2.promptEn: The `Compute short SHA` step (`jobs.build.steps[1]`, with `id: meta`) uses `echo "::set-output name=sha::${GITHUB_SHA::7}"`, which GitHub has disabled due to an Injection vulnerability. Upgrade the `run:` line of the `id: meta` step to `echo "sha=${GITHUB_SHA::7}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`.
hintsEn: Keep `id: meta` on `jobs.build.steps[1]` so the next step can still read `${{ steps.meta.outputs.sha }}`.
Replace the old command with `echo "sha=${GITHUB_SHA::7}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`.

cicd-ex-c04-3.titleEn: Guard the Publish Package Step to Run Only on Pushes to main
cicd-ex-c04-3.promptEn: This workflow listens to both `pull_request` and `push`, yet the final `Publish Package` step (`jobs.release.steps[4]`) lacks a guard condition — causing anyone opening a draft PR to accidentally publish a package to the Registry! Attach an `if:` property to `Publish Package` checking both `github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` and `github.event_name == 'push'`.
hintsEn: Locate step 5 (`Publish Package` — `jobs.release.steps[4]`).
Add `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'` right under `name: Publish Package`.

cicd-ex-c04-4.titleEn: Auto-Upload Debug Logs When Tests Fail Using if: failure()
cicd-ex-c04-4.promptEn: When the `npm test` step (`steps[3]`) fails, default behavior skips the `Upload debug logs` step (`steps[4]`) below it, leaving engineers without the `reports/` files needed to investigate; conversely, when `npm test` passes, uploading logs is unnecessary! Attach `if: failure()` to `jobs.test.steps[4]` so it ONLY runs when a prior step fails.
hintsEn: Locate the `Upload debug logs` step (`jobs.test.steps[4]`).
Add `if: failure()` (or `if: ${{ failure() }}`) at the same indentation level as `uses:`.

cicd-ex-c04-5.titleEn: Save CI Minutes by Ignoring Docs with on.push.paths-ignore
cicd-ex-c04-5.promptEn: Every time Technical Writers fix a typo in `README.md` or update docs in `docs/`, the heavy 8-minute test suite runs unnecessarily. Add a `paths-ignore` list under `on.push` containing both `"**.md"` and `"docs/**"`.
hintsEn: Under `on.push` (at the same level as `branches: [main]`), add the `paths-ignore:` key.
Remember to wrap `"**.md"` in double quotes because a leading `*` in unquoted YAML is parsed as an alias!

cicd-ex-c04-6.titleEn: Filter Monorepo Path apps/api/** and Prevent Infinite Push Loops
cicd-ex-c04-6.promptEn: This workflow needs 2 safeguards at once: (1) on `on.pull_request`, add a `paths` filter containing `"apps/api/**"` so it only runs when the API service changes; and (2) in the `sync-changelog` Job running on pushes to `main`, a previous developer forgot to mark the automated commit, causing the bot to trigger endlessly — add `[skip ci]` to the `git commit -m "..."` command in `jobs.sync-changelog.steps[1].run` AND add `if: github.actor != 'release-bot'` to `jobs.sync-changelog`.
hintsEn: Under `on.pull_request`, add `paths: ["apps/api/**"]`.
In `jobs.sync-changelog.if`, check `github.actor != 'release-bot'`, and add `[skip ci]` to the `git commit` message in `jobs.sync-changelog.steps[1].run`.

C05.titleEn: Job Dependency Graph (DAG needs:) & Multi-Environment Testing (Matrix)
C05.summaryEn: Speed up feedback with the parallel Fan-out / Fan-in pattern (needs), test across multiple Node versions and OSes using strategy.matrix (fail-fast: false), and pass outputs between two Jobs.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
As a Node.js project grows, a single Job running sequentially `lint` (2 min) -> `typecheck` (2 min) -> `unit-test` (5 min) -> `build` (3 min) forces developers to wait **12 minutes** for every push.

To shorten feedback loops, modern CI systems orchestrate work using a **DAG (*Directed Acyclic Graph*)**: independent steps (such as `lint`, `typecheck`, `unit-test`) run **in parallel simultaneously**, and only the aggregation step (`build`) waits for all preceding steps to finish via the **`needs:`** keyword. In JavaScript/Python programming, this mechanism is equivalent to **`await Promise.all([lint(), typecheck(), unitTest()])`** before calling `await build()`. (Think of it like an assembly line where chassis fabrication, engine inspection, and interior work run concurrently before final assembly).

```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "cicd:c05"
src: "/illustrations/cicd/cicd-dag-fanout-matrix.jpg"
```

steps.headingEn: Fan-Out / Fan-In Architecture with needs:
steps.bodyEn:
By default, every Job declared under `jobs:` launches **in parallel at second 0** (known as *Root Jobs* — **Fan-Out**). When you add `needs: [lint, unit-test]` to the `build` Job, you create a convergence gate (**Fan-In**):

```visual
kind: flow
title: "Đồ Thị Phụ Thuộc DAG: Quạt Rộng Song Song (Fan-Out) & Hội Tụ (Fan-In)"
subtitle: "Ví dụ thực tế: lint (2p) và unit-test (5p) chạy song song -> hội tụ vào build (3p) chỉ tốn max(2, 5) + 3 = 8 phút thay vì 10 phút!"
steps:
  - icon: git-pr
    badge: "Giây 0 · Kích hoạt"
    title: "Push / Pull Request"
    desc: "Đánh thức đồng thời mọi Root Job không khai báo needs"
    code: "on: [push, pull_request]"
    tone: sky
    edge: "Fan-Out song song"
  - icon: zap
    badge: "Song song · max(2p, 5p)"
    title: "lint (2p) + unit-test (5p)"
    desc: "Chạy đồng thời trên 2 máy ảo độc lập giống hệt Promise.all"
    code: "Wall-clock: 5 phút"
    tone: cyan
    edge: "Fan-In (AND)"
  - icon: package
    badge: "Cổng hội tụ · +3p"
    title: "Job: build"
    desc: "Chỉ chạy khi TẤT CẢ Job trong needs đều xanh (1 nhánh đỏ -> Skipped!)"
    code: "needs: [lint, unit-test]"
    tone: cyan
    edge: "nhánh main?"
  - icon: rocket
    badge: "Triển khai có điều kiện"
    title: "Job: deploy-staging"
    desc: "Dừng sau build nếu là PR; tự động đẩy lên Staging khi merge vào main"
    code: "needs: build"
    tone: emerald
footer: "Chữ 'Acyclic' trong DAG cấm tuyệt đối vòng lặp phụ thuộc (ví dụ A needs B và B needs A sẽ bị từ chối ngay lúc kiểm tra cú pháp!)"
```

- [x] **Save wall-clock time:** Total wait time drops from `2 + 5 + 3 = 10 minutes` down to `max(2, 5) + 3 = 8 minutes` (the more branches like `typecheck` and `security-scan` you have, the more dramatic the speedup).
- [x] **Strict `AND` gate logic:** If `lint` fails (`Exit Code 1`) even though `unit-test` is green (`Exit Code 0`), the `build` Job immediately transitions to **`Skipped`**, wasting zero VM money packaging broken code.
- [x] **Block deployment on PR branches:** The `deploy-staging` Job combines `needs: build` and `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` so it only deploys once code is merged into the main branch.

steps.headingEn: Multi-Environment Testing with strategy.matrix and fail-fast
steps.bodyEn:
Suppose you develop a library/CLI package that must work reliably across multiple Node versions (**`20`**, **`22`**) and operating systems (`ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest`, `windows-latest`). Instead of duplicating 6 separate Jobs, ==`strategy.matrix`== automatically generates the Cartesian product (`3 operating systems × 2 Node versions = 6` parallel Job runs):

```yaml
unit-test:
  runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
  strategy:
    fail-fast: false
    matrix:
      os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
      node: [20, 22]
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
        cache: "npm"
    - run: npm ci
    - run: npm test
```

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Hành vi mặc định của strategy.fail-fast khi chạy Matrix"
subtitle: "Một dòng cấu hình quyết định việc nhận đầy đủ kết quả chẩn đoán hay dừng toàn bộ các tổ hợp còn lại"
left:
  badge: "MẶC ĐỊNH · fail-fast: true"
  title: "Một tổ hợp lỗi -> Hủy ngay toàn bộ các Job còn lại"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    strategy:
      # Không khai báo -> Mặc định là fail-fast: true!
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
        node: [20, 22]
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Khi tổ hợp `(macos-latest, Node 20)` gặp lỗi ở phút thứ 3, GitHub lập tức gửi lệnh **`Cancel` hủy luôn 3 máy ảo đang chạy dở**."
    - "Bạn thiếu thông tin chẩn đoán: không biết lỗi đó chỉ xảy ra trên Node 20 hay cả Node 22 trên Ubuntu cũng gặp phải."
    - "Chỉ phù hợp khi dùng Runner chi phí cao và chỉ cần biết nhanh có lỗi hay không."
right:
  badge: "KHUYÊN DÙNG · fail-fast: false"
  title: "Giữ các tổ hợp còn lại chạy nốt để gom trọn vẹn kết quả"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
        node: [20, 22]
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Tổ hợp lỗi cứ báo đỏ, nhưng **3 tổ hợp kia vẫn chạy tới cùng** để trả về bảng tương thích đầy đủ ngay trong 1 lần chạy"
    - "Chuẩn mực bắt buộc cho kiểm thử đa phiên bản Node/OS và chia mảnh Test Sharding"
    - "Kết hợp thêm `exclude:` để cắt bớt tổ hợp thừa hoặc `include:` để gắn biến đặc thù"
```

> [!WARNING] Cost consideration on Private repos: Watch out for the `macos-latest` billing multiplier!
> On Private repositories, GitHub bills runner minutes with an OS multiplier: **`macos-latest` costs ~10x more** than a standard Linux `ubuntu-latest` VM (and `windows-latest` costs ~**2x** more)! Therefore, use `exclude:` to enable `macos-latest` only on the required Node LTS version when your tool genuinely touches macOS-specific filesystems or binaries.

steps.headingEn: Passing Data Between Jobs via jobs.<id>.outputs
steps.bodyEn:
In lesson `C04`, we used `"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` to pass data between two Steps **within the same Job**. However, because two Jobs run on two separate virtual machines, all Step outputs are scoped to that Job by default. To pass a `version` number from the `build` Job to the `deploy` Job, you must declare ==3 linked steps==:

```visual
kind: flow
title: "Quy trình 3 bước truyền dữ liệu giữa hai Job độc lập"
subtitle: "Thiếu bất kỳ bước nào (đặc biệt là bước 2) sẽ khiến giá trị bên nhận thành chuỗi rỗng \"\""
steps:
  - icon: terminal
    badge: "Mắt xích 1 · Trong Step"
    title: "Ghi $GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    desc: "Step gắn id: pkg và ghi giá trị vào tệp output nội bộ"
    code: "echo \"version=1.4.2\" >> \"$GITHUB_OUTPUT\""
    tone: sky
    edge: "ánh xạ lên vỏ Job"
  - icon: upload
    badge: "Mắt xích 2 · Vỏ Job nguồn"
    title: "jobs.build.outputs"
    desc: "Phơi bày tường minh giá trị từ Step ra giao diện ngoài của Job build"
    code: "outputs: { version: ${{ steps.pkg.outputs.version }} }"
    tone: amber
    edge: "ràng buộc needs"
  - icon: rocket
    badge: "Mắt xích 3 · Job đích"
    title: "needs.build.outputs"
    desc: "Job deploy khai báo needs: build và đọc qua ngữ cảnh needs"
    code: "${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}"
    tone: emerald
```

```yaml
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.pkg.outputs.version }}   # Mắt xích 2: Phơi bày ra vỏ Job!
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: pkg                                   # Mắt xích 1: Step có id rõ ràng
        run: echo "version=$(node -p \"require('./package.json').version\")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  deploy:
    needs: build                                  # Mắt xích 3a: Bắt buộc có needs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo "Deploying release v${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}" # Mắt xích 3b
```

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **DAG `needs:`** behaves like `Promise.all` (`AND` logic, forbids cycles `A <-> B`), reducing total time to `max(parallel branches) + convergence step`.
> - The number of Jobs in `strategy.matrix` equals the **Cartesian product** of its dimensions; the default is `fail-fast: true`, so explicitly set **`fail-fast: false`** to see the full failure matrix, and keep in mind `macos-latest` burns ~10x Linux minutes on Private repos.
> - Passing data between 2 Jobs always requires all 3 links: **`"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` -> `jobs.<id>.outputs` -> `needs.<id>.outputs`**.

readings.noteEn: Production DAG architecture: run 3 parallel tracks `lint`, `typecheck`, and `unit-test` (Node 20 & 22 matrix with `fail-fast: false`), then converge at the `build` gate.
readings.taskEn: How many Runner VMs in total are provisioned for a single run of `dag-matrix-fanin.yml` (assuming all checks pass)? How many upstream VMs must finish before the `build` Job starts running?
readings.answerEn: A total of 5 Runner VMs: 1 for `lint` + 1 for `typecheck` + 2 for the `unit-test` matrix (Node 20 and Node 22) running in parallel in the first wave, and only after all 4 of those VMs turn GREEN does the 5th VM for the `build` Job (`needs: [lint, typecheck, unit-test]`) start.

cicd-q-c05-1.qEn: In a Workflow with 3 Jobs: `lint` (takes 2 min, no `needs`), `unit-test` (takes 5 min, no `needs`), and `build` (takes 3 min, declares `needs: [lint, unit-test]`). Assuming enough idle runners, approximately how long is the total wall-clock time from trigger until `build` finishes?
choicesEn: 10 minutes (2 + 5 + 3 running back-to-back)
8 minutes (`lint` and `unit-test` run in parallel taking max(2, 5) = 5 minutes, plus 3 minutes for `build`)
5 minutes (all 3 Jobs run in parallel from the start)
3 minutes
cicd-q-c05-1.explainEn: The two root jobs `lint` (2m) and `unit-test` (5m) start simultaneously like `Promise.all`, completing after 5 minutes; immediately afterward the convergence gate `build` runs for another 3 minutes -> total is only 8 minutes.

cicd-q-c05-2.qEn: Given the `strategy.matrix` configuration below, how many total parallel Job runs will GitHub Actions generate from this matrix?
cicd-q-c05-2.explainEn: The matrix produces the Cartesian product of its dimensions: `3 operating systems × 2 Node versions = 6` independent Job combinations.

cicd-q-c05-3.qEn: By default in GitHub Actions, if you do not specify `fail-fast`, the default value is `fail-fast: true` — meaning that as soon as 1 combination in the Matrix fails, all other in-progress combinations are cancelled immediately.
cicd-q-c05-3.explainEn: True! That is why in cross-version compatibility testing we usually set `fail-fast: false` explicitly so we can inspect the complete result table across all Node/OS versions.

cicd-q-c05-4.qEn: When the `build` Job needs to export a value from Step `id: pkg` so the `deploy` Job can read it via `${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}`, which declaration must be present at the `build` Job level?
choicesEn: `exports: { version: "${{ steps.pkg.version }}" }`
`outputs: { version: "${{ steps.pkg.outputs.version }}" }`
`env: { version: "${{ steps.pkg.outputs.version }}" }`
Nothing extra is needed; all Step outputs are automatically exposed to other Jobs
cicd-q-c05-4.explainEn: Step outputs are encapsulated within that Job by default. You must explicitly map them via `jobs.build.outputs.version: ${{ steps.pkg.outputs.version }}` so dependent Jobs (`needs: build`) can read them.

cicd-q-c05-5.qEn: In the convergence gate pattern where `build` has `needs: [lint, unit-test]`, what happens to the `build` Job if `lint` fails (`Exit Code 1`) while `unit-test` succeeds (`Exit Code 0`)?
choicesEn: The `build` Job still runs normally because at least 1 upstream Job succeeded
The `build` Job is automatically skipped (`Skipped`) because by default `needs` requires ALL prerequisite Jobs to succeed
The `build` Job runs but automatically deletes the `dist/` directory
GitHub automatically retries `lint` 5 more times
cicd-q-c05-5.explainEn: The `needs: [A, B]` gate acts like a logical `AND` (`Promise.all`): `build` is only allowed to start when both `lint` AND `unit-test` succeed.

cicd-q-c05-6.qEn: The `needs:` dependency graph allows circular declarations (e.g., Job `A` has `needs: B` and Job `B` simultaneously has `needs: A`) so the two Jobs can cross-check each other.
cicd-q-c05-6.explainEn: False! "Acyclic" in DAG means **no cycles**. Creating a circular dependency `A <-> B` causes GitHub Actions' syntax validator to reject the workflow immediately at startup.

cicd-q-c05-7.qEn: Why should adding `macos-latest` to `strategy.matrix` be weighed more carefully than `ubuntu-latest` on Private repositories?
choicesEn: Because macOS VMs have a much higher per-minute billing multiplier (typically 10x) compared to standard Linux VMs
Because macOS cannot install Node.js 22
Because `actions/checkout@v4` does not work on macOS
Because macOS forces every command to run sequentially 20x slower
cicd-q-c05-7.explainEn: On GitHub Actions for Private repos, macOS Runner minutes cost roughly 10x Linux Runner minutes (and Windows costs 2x). Only enable `macos-latest` in a matrix for CLI/desktop packages that genuinely have OS-specific behavior.

cicd-card-c05-1.frontEn: What is the closest JavaScript analogy for the Fan-Out / Fan-In pattern using `needs: [lint, unit-test]`?
cicd-card-c05-1.backEn: Just like `await Promise.all([lint(), unitTest()]); await build();` — run independent tasks in parallel first, then converge once all of them finish.

cicd-card-c05-2.frontEn: What does DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) mean in CI/CD?
cicd-card-c05-2.backEn: A directed graph with no cycles: Jobs connect along `needs:` dependency arrows, allowing parallel branching and convergence while strictly forbidding circular dependencies.

cicd-card-c05-3.frontEn: What is the effect of `strategy.fail-fast: false` when running a Node `[20, 22]` Matrix?
cicd-card-c05-3.backEn: It prevents GitHub from cancelling the Node 22 Job if the Node 20 Job fails, allowing developers to get complete test results across every version in a single run.

cicd-card-c05-4.frontEn: Name all 3 required links to pass a `version` variable from the `build` Job to the `deploy` Job.
cicd-card-c05-4.backEn: 1) A Step in `build` with `id: pkg` writing to `"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"`; 2) `jobs.build.outputs.version: ${{ steps.pkg.outputs.version }}`; 3) `jobs.deploy` declaring `needs: build` and reading `${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}`.

cicd-card-c05-5.frontEn: How do you make the `deploy-staging` Job wait for `build` on every PR/push, yet ONLY execute deployment when the branch is `main`?
cicd-card-c05-5.backEn: Combine both attributes on `deploy-staging`: `needs: build` and `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`.

cicd-card-c05-6.frontEn: Which expressions dynamically inject the OS and Node version from `strategy.matrix` into a Job configuration?
cicd-card-c05-6.backEn: `runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}` at the Job level and `node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}` inside `actions/setup-node@v4`.

cicd-ex-c05-1.titleEn: Split a slow sequential Job into 2 parallel Root Jobs: lint and unit-test
cicd-ex-c05-1.promptEn: Currently `npm run lint` and `npm test` are crammed into a single `all-in-one` Job that runs sequentially and slowly. Remove/split it into two independent parallel Root Jobs named `jobs.lint` and `jobs.unit-test` (both using `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, neither declaring `needs`, and each checking out the repo, setting up Node 22, running `npm ci`, and executing its own command).
hintsEn: Create 2 keys under `jobs:`: `lint:` and `unit-test:` (omit `needs` on both Jobs so they start in parallel at second 0).
Remember each Job runs on its own Ephemeral Runner, so both `lint` and `unit-test` need `checkout@v4`, `setup-node@v4`, and `npm ci`.

cicd-ex-c05-2.titleEn: Create a Fan-In gate: have the build Job wait for both lint and unit-test to pass
cicd-ex-c05-2.promptEn: In the starter file, the `build` Job has no dependencies declared so it runs in parallel from the start — wasting a VM bundling artifacts even if `lint` or `unit-test` fails! Configure `jobs.build.needs` as a list waiting for both `["lint", "unit-test"]`.
hintsEn: Inside `jobs.build` (at the same indentation level as `runs-on`), add `needs: ["lint", "unit-test"]`.

cicd-ex-c05-3.titleEn: Add a deploy-staging Job depending on build that only runs on the main branch
cicd-ex-c05-3.promptEn: Add a new Job named `deploy-staging` under `jobs:` that satisfies: (1) runs on `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, (2) declares `needs: ["build"]` (or `needs: build`) to wait for packaging, (3) sets condition `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` so PRs don't overwrite Staging, and (4) has at least 1 `run:` Step executing deployment.
hintsEn: Add the `deploy-staging:` key under `jobs:` (indented 2 spaces like `build:`).
Inside it, declare `needs: ["build"]`, `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`, and a `steps:` array with at least 1 `run:` command.

cicd-ex-c05-4.titleEn: Set up a Strategy Matrix to test on Node 20 and Node 22 in parallel
cicd-ex-c05-4.promptEn: Your company's internal library must stay compatible with both Node 20 and Node 22. Configure `jobs.unit-test.strategy.matrix.node` to `[20, 22]`, then pass the dynamic expression `${{ matrix.node }}` into `jobs.unit-test.steps[1].with.node-version`.
hintsEn: Add `strategy:\n  matrix:\n    node: [20, 22]` under `jobs.unit-test`.
Change `node-version: "22"` in `steps[1].with` to `node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}`.

cicd-ex-c05-5.titleEn: Expand to a multi-OS matrix (Ubuntu + macOS) and disable fail-fast
cicd-ex-c05-5.promptEn: Your CLI tool needs to be tested on both Linux and macOS without aborting mid-run when one machine fails. On `jobs.unit-test`: (1) add `strategy.matrix.os: ["ubuntu-latest", "macos-latest"]`, (2) change `runs-on` to `${{ matrix.os }}`, and (3) set `strategy.fail-fast: false`.
hintsEn: Place `fail-fast: false` under `strategy:` (at the same level as `matrix:`).
Add `os: ["ubuntu-latest", "macos-latest"]` inside `matrix:` and update `runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}`.

cicd-ex-c05-6.titleEn: Bridge outputs.version from the build Job to the deploy Job
cicd-ex-c05-6.promptEn: Step `id: pkg` in the `build` Job already extracts the version number from `package.json` into `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, but in the `deploy` Job `echo` prints an empty string because the bridge between the 2 Jobs is missing! Connect all 3 links: (1) declare `jobs.build.outputs.version: "${{ steps.pkg.outputs.version }}"`, (2) add `needs: build` to `jobs.deploy`, and (3) pass `${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}` into the `run` command of `jobs.deploy.steps[0]`.
hintsEn: In `jobs.build`, add an `outputs:\n  version: "${{ steps.pkg.outputs.version }}"` block at the same level as `runs-on`.
In `jobs.deploy`, add `needs: build` and update `steps[0]`'s `run:` command to read `${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}`.

C06.summaryEn: Run real Integration Tests with Postgres 16 & Redis 7 Service Containers using pg_isready / redis-cli ping healthchecks, cap budgets with timeout-minutes, and prevent race conditions via concurrency.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
Unit Tests using mocked data (`vi.mock('pg')`) run fast but fail to catch bugs in SQL queries, column names, or database migrations. Locally, developers typically run `docker compose up -d postgres redis` for integration testing. When moving to GitHub Actions, you need to combine **3 core operational mechanisms**: spinning up **PostgreSQL 16 + Redis 7** tied to the Job lifecycle, setting a **`timeout-minutes`** cap to prevent hung jobs from burning budget, and configuring **`concurrency`** appropriately between Pull Requests and Production.

```visual
kind: groups
title: "Ba cơ chế kiểm soát và bảo vệ Pipeline Kiểm thử & Triển khai [!badge:emerald:Production Grade]"
columns: 3
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: shield-alert
    title: "timeout-minutes"
    badge: "Giới hạn thời gian chạy"
    tone: rose
    desc: "Dừng các tiến trình bị treo thay vì để chạy hết ngưỡng mặc định 6 giờ."
    bullets:
      - "Mặc định nếu bỏ trống, GitHub cho Job chạy tới ==**360 phút (6 tiếng)**== mới tự huỷ."
      - "Luôn khai báo rõ `timeout-minutes: 10` (hoặc `15`) ở mọi Job CI."
  - num: 2
    icon: layers
    title: "concurrency"
    badge: "Điều phối xung đột & Lãng phí"
    tone: amber
    desc: "Kiểm soát các lượt chạy trùng nhánh trên PR hoặc xếp hàng tuần tự trên Production."
    bullets:
      - "Trên PR: `cancel-in-progress: true` để huỷ ngay bản chạy cũ lỗi thời."
      - "Trên Production: `cancel-in-progress: false` để xếp hàng tuần tự, bảo vệ DB migration."
  - num: 3
    icon: database
    title: "services:"
    badge: "Postgres 16 & Redis 7"
    tone: sky
    desc: "Đính kèm container cơ sở dữ liệu thật dùng một lần ngay bên cạnh Job kiểm thử."
    bullets:
      - "Tự động bật trước Step đầu tiên và **xoá sạch dữ liệu** khi Job kết thúc."
      - "Kết hợp `--health-cmd` để loại bỏ lỗi kết nối sớm `ECONNREFUSED`."
```

steps.headingEn: Capping Job Runtime with timeout-minutes (Avoiding the 360-Minute Default)
steps.bodyEn:
```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "cicd:c06"
alt: "Ba cơ chế vận hành gồm Service Containers (PostgreSQL 16 + Redis 7 kèm healthcheck), giới hạn timeout-minutes và điều phối concurrency"
title: "Ba cơ chế vận hành CI: Service Containers, Timeout & Concurrency"
subtitle: "Kiểm thử tích hợp trên cơ sở dữ liệu thật dùng một lần, giới hạn tiến trình treo 6 tiếng và điều phối xung đột luồng"
```

By default in GitHub Actions, **if you omit `timeout-minutes`, a hung Job continues running for up to ==360 minutes (6 hours)==** before the system forcefully terminates it. If an integration test forgets to close a database connection and leaves the Node.js process hanging, 10 Pull Requests in a single day will burn **3,600 CI minutes** of your team's quota.

```yaml
jobs:
  integration:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10   # Bắt buộc khai báo trần hợp lý (10–15 phút)!
```

steps.headingEn: Controlling Contention with concurrency: When to Cancel vs Queue?
steps.bodyEn:
When a developer spots a typo and pushes 4 commits in 2 minutes to the same PR branch, letting all 4 workflows run in parallel wastes resources. Conversely, on the `main` branch running a **Production deployment** with database schema updates, cancelling an in-flight process will corrupt state locks and cause downtime.

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Hai Chiến Lược Đối Lập Của concurrency: Pull Request vs Production"
subtitle: "Cùng một từ khoá nhưng đảo ngược cờ cancel-in-progress theo đúng mức độ rủi ro của môi trường"
left:
  badge: "KIỂM THỬ NHÁNH / PR · Huỷ bản cũ"
  title: "Tiết kiệm tài nguyên cho commit mới nhất"
  tone: sky
  code: |
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Nhóm theo `github.workflow` + `github.ref` để **cô lập riêng từng nhánh/PR** (tuyệt đối không dùng khoá toàn cục làm huỷ nhầm PR của đồng nghiệp khác!)"
    - "**`cancel-in-progress: true`**: Vừa đẩy commit sửa lỗi mới lên nhánh -> huỷ tức khắc lượt chạy cũ đang dở dang"
right:
  badge: "TRIỂN KHAI PRODUCTION · Xếp hàng tuần tự"
  title: "Bảo vệ an toàn tuyệt đối cho DB Migration & Terraform"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    concurrency:
      group: deploy-production
      cancel-in-progress: false
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Đặt tên nhóm cố định theo môi trường đích (`deploy-production`)"
    - "**`cancel-in-progress: false`**: Tuyệt đối không ngắt ngang bản đang chạy! Đợt deploy mới nhất được giữ ở trạng thái chờ (**`Pending`**) cho tới khi bản trước hoàn tất trọn vẹn"
```

steps.headingEn: Service Containers: Replacing compose.yaml with Proper Healthchecks
steps.bodyEn:
The ==`services:`== block lets you run `postgres:16-alpine` and `redis:7-alpine` alongside your Job. However, there is a common pitfall: Docker reports the container as `Running` as soon as PID 1 starts, yet PostgreSQL still needs 2–4 seconds to run `initdb` before opening TCP port `5432`. If your `npm run db:migrate` Step executes immediately, you will hit ==`ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432`==.

```visual
kind: flow
title: "Vòng Đời Khởi Động Service Containers Chống Lỗi ECONNREFUSED"
steps:
  - icon: container
    badge: "1. Khởi tạo Container"
    title: "Pull & Map Ports"
    desc: "Bật postgres:16-alpine (5432:5432) & redis:7-alpine (6379:6379)"
    code: "ports: [\"5432:5432\"]"
    tone: sky
    edge: "kiểm tra sức khoẻ"
  - icon: doctor
    badge: "2. Chốt chặn Healthcheck"
    title: "Đợi trạng thái healthy"
    desc: "Runner kiên nhẫn chờ pg_isready và redis-cli ping trả mã 0"
    code: "--health-cmd pg_isready"
    tone: amber
    edge: "DB sẵn sàng 100%"
  - icon: play
    badge: "3. Thực thi Step"
    title: "Migrate & Test Thật"
    desc: "Node.js trên host VM gọi thẳng localhost:5432 và localhost:6379"
    code: "localhost:5432"
    tone: emerald
    edge: "Job kết thúc"
  - icon: trash
    badge: "4. Dọn sạch Ephemeral"
    title: "Huỷ Container & Dữ Liệu"
    desc: "Xoá sổ toàn bộ DB tạm ngay lập tức, lần chạy sau lại sạch tinh"
    code: "Auto Destroy"
    tone: rose
```

Instead of guessing with `sleep 10`, configure standard Docker Healthcheck flags inside `options:`:

```yaml
jobs:
  integration:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: app
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test_ephemeral_password
          POSTGRES_DB: app_test
        ports:
          - "5432:5432"
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U app -d app_test"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10

      redis:
        image: redis:7-alpine
        ports:
          - "6379:6379"
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 5
```

steps.headingEn: Two Golden Rules for Node.js Developers: localhost Networking & Closing Pools in afterAll()
steps.bodyEn:
- [x] **Connect via `localhost` (using `ports:`) when running directly on the VM:** When Steps execute directly on the `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` host (without a Job-level `container:`), the Node.js process lives on the host network outside the Docker network. Therefore, you **must map `ports: ["5432:5432"]` and connect via `localhost:5432` / `localhost:6379`** (`postgresql://app:test_ephemeral_password@localhost:5432/app_test`). *(Only when the entire Job is wrapped in `container: node:22-alpine` do you connect via the service name `postgres:5432`).*
- [!] **Close Connection Pools cleanly in `afterAll()`:** Libraries like `pg.Pool`, `PrismaClient`, and `ioredis` keep open TCP sockets in the Event Loop. If you forget to call `await prisma.$disconnect()`, `await pool.end()`, and `await redis.quit()` in `afterAll()`, your test suite will pass 100% and still hang until it hits `timeout-minutes: 10`!

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - Omitting `timeout-minutes` = default max runtime of **360 minutes** -> always declare `timeout-minutes: 10` (or `15`).
> - `concurrency`: Use `ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with **`cancel-in-progress: true` for PRs**, but strictly **`cancel-in-progress: false` for Production**.
> - `services:` are **Ephemeral** (wiped clean when the Job ends): remember to expose `ports:` to connect over **`localhost`**, add `--health-cmd` (**`pg_isready`** for Postgres, **`redis-cli ping`** for Redis), and close DB connections in `afterAll()`.

readings.noteEn: Complete integration test configuration: `timeout-minutes: 15`, running `postgres:16-alpine` + `redis:7-alpine` in parallel with `--health-cmd` before executing `npm run db:migrate`.
readings.taskEn: If you delete the `options:` block containing `--health-cmd "pg_isready ..."` on lines 27–31 of `postgres-redis-services.yml`, what flaky error is very likely to occur during the `npm run db:migrate` step?
readings.answerEn: `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432`! Without `--health-cmd`, the Runner starts executing Steps right after the Docker container spawns its process, while PostgreSQL is still running its internal `initdb` script and not yet accepting TCP connections.

readings.noteEn: Side-by-side comparison of two opposite `concurrency` patterns between Pull Request and Production environments.
readings.taskEn: Why must the `production-safe-rollout` Job (lines 37–39) set `cancel-in-progress: false` and use a fixed group name `deploy-production-lock` instead of embedding `${{ github.sha }}` in the group name?
readings.answerEn: If you embed `${{ github.sha }}`, every commit lands in a different group, allowing 2 deployments to overlap concurrently! Using a fixed group `deploy-production-lock` with `cancel-in-progress: false` guarantees that at most 1 rollout runs cleanly to completion at any time while the next one queues up.

cicd-q-c06-1.qEn: If you forget to declare `timeout-minutes` on a GitHub Actions Job and a Node.js process hangs on an unclosed database connection, up to how many minutes will the system let that Job run before automatically cancelling it?
cicd-q-c06-1.explainEn: The default limit in GitHub Actions is `360` minutes (6 hours). Always set `timeout-minutes: 10` (or `15`) explicitly to protect your team's CI minute budget.

cicd-q-c06-2.qEn: Which `concurrency` configuration is best suited for a Pull Request test workflow to immediately cancel stale runs when a developer pushes a new fix commit to the same branch?
choicesEn: `group: global-lock` and `cancel-in-progress: true` (cancelling PRs of all other teammates in the company!)
`group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` and `cancel-in-progress: true`
`group: ci-${{ github.sha }}` and `cancel-in-progress: true`
`group: ci-${{ github.ref }}` and `cancel-in-progress: false`
cicd-q-c06-2.explainEn: Grouping by `github.workflow` + `github.ref` ensures only runs from the **same branch/PR** supersede each other (`cancel-in-progress: true`), without affecting anyone else's PR.

cicd-q-c06-3.qEn: For a Production deployment Job (which runs database migrations or infrastructure updates), you should enable `cancel-in-progress: true` to immediately abort the older deployment whenever a newer one arrives.
cicd-q-c06-3.explainEn: Critically false! Aborting an in-progress DB migration or infrastructure state update (Terraform/Helm) risks corrupting state locks and taking down Production. For Production, always set `cancel-in-progress: false` to queue sequentially.

cicd-q-c06-4.qEn: When Job Steps run directly on the `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` VM (not inside a Job `container:`), which hostname should the Node.js app use to connect to `services.postgres`, and what configuration is required on the service?
choicesEn: Connect via `localhost:5432` and explicitly map ports `ports: ["5432:5432"]` in `services.postgres`
Connect via `postgres.internal.cloud:9999` with no port mapping needed
PostgreSQL must be installed manually via `sudo apt-get install` because `services:` cannot be used
The `/var/lib/postgresql` directory must be downloaded via `actions/download-artifact@v4`
cicd-q-c06-4.explainEn: When Steps run directly on the host VM (`ubuntu-latest`), the service's Docker container must publish its port to the host (`ports: ["5432:5432"]`) so Node.js code can connect to `localhost:5432`.

cicd-q-c06-5.qEn: Why do we pass `--health-cmd pg_isready` in `services.postgres.options:` instead of simply declaring `image: postgres:16-alpine`?
choicesEn: To change PostgreSQL's default password
To force the GitHub Runner to wait until PostgreSQL finishes initializing the DB and is genuinely ready to accept TCP connections before starting test Steps
To shrink the Docker image size by half
To automatically export SQL data to a Markdown file
cicd-q-c06-5.explainEn: Without `--health-cmd`, the Runner only waits for the container to `start` before running Steps, often hitting Postgres while it is still running `initdb` and hasn't opened its port yet, causing flaky `ECONNREFUSED` errors.

cicd-q-c06-6.qEn: What is the standard healthcheck command typically placed in `--health-cmd` for a `redis:7-alpine` container?
choicesEn: `pg_isready`
`redis-cli ping`
`npm test`
`curl http://localhost:6379`
cicd-q-c06-6.explainEn: `redis-cli ping` sends a health probe to the Redis server and receives `PONG` (Exit Code `0`) as soon as Redis is ready to serve requests.

cicd-q-c06-7.qEn: All data written to `services.postgres` and `services.redis` during Integration Tests is automatically and completely wiped as soon as the Job finishes.
cicd-q-c06-7.explainEn: True! Service Containers are Ephemeral just like the Runner: every Job run gets a clean database starting from zero, and once the Job ends, all containers and temporary data are destroyed.

cicd-card-c06-1.frontEn: What is the default `timeout-minutes` in GitHub Actions, and what should you set it to for a typical CI Job?
cicd-card-c06-1.backEn: The default is `360` minutes (6 hours!). Always set `timeout-minutes: 10` (or `15`) on every Job to catch hung connections or watch-mode processes early.

cicd-card-c06-2.frontEn: What is the core difference in `cancel-in-progress` between Concurrency for PRs and Concurrency for Production Deploy?
cicd-card-c06-2.backEn: On PRs, set `cancel-in-progress: true` (grouped by `github.ref`) to cancel stale runs and save minutes; on Production, set `cancel-in-progress: false` (fixed lock group) to queue sequentially and never interrupt an active rollout.

cicd-card-c06-3.frontEn: What is the purpose of the `services:` block inside a GitHub Actions Job?
cicd-card-c06-3.backEn: It launches auxiliary Docker containers (such as `postgres:16-alpine`, `redis:7-alpine`) alongside the Job for real Integration Testing, then automatically cleans them up when the Job finishes.

cicd-card-c06-4.frontEn: How do you permanently fix flaky `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432` errors when connecting to `services.postgres` at the start of a Job?
cicd-card-c06-4.backEn: Add Docker healthcheck flags to `services.postgres.options`: `--health-cmd pg_isready --health-interval 5s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 10` so the Runner waits until Postgres is actually `healthy`.

cicd-card-c06-5.frontEn: What is the standard `REDIS_URL` and healthcheck flag when attaching `redis:7-alpine` to `services:` on `ubuntu-latest`?
cicd-card-c06-5.backEn: Map `ports: ["6379:6379"]`, set `--health-cmd "redis-cli ping"` in `options:`, and pass `REDIS_URL: "redis://localhost:6379"` in `env:`.

cicd-card-c06-6.frontEn: If a `concurrency` group currently has 1 `Running` Job and 1 `Pending` Job, what happens when a 3rd run arrives with `cancel-in-progress: false`?
cicd-card-c06-6.backEn: The `Running` Job continues safely to completion; the middle `Pending` Job is replaced by the newest 3rd run — at most 1 running + 1 latest queued run are kept.

cicd-ex-c06-1.titleEn: Set a timeout-minutes: 10 ceiling to replace the dangerous 360-minute default
cicd-ex-c06-1.promptEn: Last week a leaked DB connection in an integration test caused the `integration` Job to hang for 6 straight hours (the 360-minute default)! Add `timeout-minutes: 10` (must be a number `<= 15` and `>= 5`) to `jobs.integration` to automatically cut off hung processes early.

Make sure to write `10` as a numeric value (not wrapped in quotes).

cicd-ex-c06-2.titleEn: Configure Concurrency to auto-cancel stale runs when new commits are pushed to a PR
cicd-ex-c06-2.promptEn: When developers push 3 quick fixes in a row to the same PR branch, all 3 old and new workflows run concurrently and clog the Runner queue. Add a top-level `concurrency:` block to the Workflow with `group` containing `github.ref` (e.g. `ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}`) and set `cancel-in-progress: true`.

Inside it, declare `group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` and `cancel-in-progress: true`.

cicd-ex-c06-3.titleEn: Attach a PostgreSQL 16 Service Container to the integration test Job
cicd-ex-c06-3.promptEn: The `integration` Job needs a real PostgreSQL database running at `localhost:5432` to execute migrations and SQL tests. Declare `jobs.integration.services.postgres` with: (1) `image: "postgres:16-alpine"`, (2) a non-empty `env.POSTGRES_PASSWORD` (e.g. `"ci_test_only_pass"`), and (3) port mapping `ports: ["5432:5432"]`.
hintsEn: Inside `jobs.integration` (same level as `runs-on`, `timeout-minutes`, `env`), add `services:` -> `postgres:`.
Declare `image: "postgres:16-alpine"`, `env: { POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "ci_test_only_pass" }`, and `ports: ["5432:5432"]`.

cicd-ex-c06-4.titleEn: Prevent ECONNREFUSED using --health-cmd pg_isready for PostgreSQL
cicd-ex-c06-4.promptEn: The `postgres` container starts, yet `npm run db:migrate` occasionally fails with `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432` because it runs too early before Postgres finishes initializing the DB. Add `options` to `jobs.integration.services.postgres` containing `--health-cmd` calling `pg_isready` (along with `--health-interval 5s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 10`).
hintsEn: Under `jobs.integration.services.postgres` (same level as `image`, `env`, `ports`), add `options: >-`.
Provide the flag string `--health-cmd pg_isready --health-interval 5s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 10`.

cicd-ex-c06-5.titleEn: Add a Redis 7 Service Container with redis-cli ping healthcheck and REDIS_URL
cicd-ex-c06-5.promptEn: The payment API just added a BullMQ queue, so Integration Tests now need a Redis 7 server running alongside PostgreSQL. Complete `jobs.integration` by: (1) adding `services.redis` using `image: "redis:7-alpine"`, mapping `ports: ["6379:6379"]`, and setting `options` with `--health-cmd "redis-cli ping"` (plus interval/retries), and (2) declaring environment variable `jobs.integration.env.REDIS_URL: "redis://localhost:6379"`.
hintsEn: Under `services:` (same level as `postgres:`), add `redis:` with `image: "redis:7-alpine"`, `ports: ["6379:6379"]`, and `options` containing `--health-cmd "redis-cli ping"`.
Under `jobs.integration.env`, add `REDIS_URL: "redis://localhost:6379"`.

C07.titleEn: Cache vs Artifact, Lockfile Hash Keys & Read-Only Cache
C07.summaryEn: Distinguish between Cache (speeding up ~/.npm installs keyed by lockfile hashFiles) and Artifact (passing immutable dist/ build outputs between Jobs), and apply Read-Only Cache safely.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
In earlier lessons, you learned how **Ephemeral Runners** work: each Job runs on a brand-new VM that is destroyed once the Job finishes. This raises two practical problems for performance and data transfer:
1. How do we avoid having 4 parallel Jobs (`lint`, `typecheck`, `unit-test`, `build`) each re-download hundreds of megabytes of packages from `registry.npmjs.org`?
2. After the `build` Job compiles TypeScript/Vite into `dist/`, how do we pass the intact `dist/` folder to the `deploy` Job without running `npm run build` again?

The solution lies in properly distinguishing two storage mechanisms with completely different purposes:
- **`Cache` (Cross-run dependency cache):** Stores network-downloaded dependency directories (`~/.npm`, `~/.cache/uv`, `~/.m2`) across different workflow runs to shorten install times. Cache is *best-effort*: if the cache is evicted or expires, the pipeline still downloads packages from the internet and succeeds, just slower.
- **`Artifact` (Outputs of a single run):** Stores finished build outputs (`dist/`, `.jar` files, Playwright HTML reports, `sbom.json`) to pass data from one Job to another within the same workflow run, or to download for inspection. Artifacts are *required*: if an expected input Artifact is missing, downstream deployment (`deploy`) Jobs will fail.

*(Put simply: `Cache` is like a pantry of prepped ingredients reused across days to save prep time, whereas `Artifact` is the sealed finished product of one specific order handed from manufacturing to shipping).*

```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "cicd:c07"
alt: "Đối chiếu kiến trúc Dependency Cache băm theo lockfile xuyên lượt chạy với Build Artifacts truyền gói thành phẩm xuyên các Job"
title: "Cơ chế lưu trữ Pipeline: Dependency Cache xuyên lượt vs Artifact xuyên Job"
subtitle: "Tăng tốc cài đặt thư viện qua mã băm package-lock.json và đảm bảo nguyên tắc Build Một Lần, Triển Khai Mọi Môi Trường"
caption: "Cơ chế Cache Key theo mã băm hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') của Cache (main ghi, PR đọc) đối lập với quy trình upload/download-artifact bất biến giữa các Job"
callouts:
  - num: 1
    label: "Dependency Cache — Tăng tốc xuyên các lượt chạy"
    desc: "Đệm kho ~/.npm theo mã băm SHA-256 của package-lock.json; nhánh main ghi chuẩn, các PR kéo về dùng lại trong vài giây (xoá đi vẫn chạy được)."
    tone: cyan
  - num: 2
    label: "Build Artifacts — Chuyển giao thành phẩm giữa các Job"
    desc: "Đóng gói thư mục dist/, báo cáo Playwright và SBOM gắn chặt với đúng Commit SHA để truyền từ máy ảo build sang các máy ảo sau."
    tone: cyan
  - num: 3
    label: "Triển khai đồng nhất & Tối ưu retention-days"
    desc: "Staging và Production cùng tải đúng 1 gói Artifact duy nhất mà không biên dịch lại; đặt retention-days: 7 giúp tiết kiệm 90% dung lượng."
    tone: emerald
```
