steps.headingEn: Detailed Layer Configuration and Reducing Alert Fatigue
steps.bodyEn:
A common mistake that causes teams to ignore security tools is **setting alert thresholds that are too noisy**: for example, flagging `devDependencies` that only run on developer machines (`eslint`, `vitest`), or blocking a pipeline over a `LOW`-severity Debian kernel vulnerability when the vendor has not yet released a patch.

Apply the following industry-standard tuning parameters:

### 1) Layer 1 — Git History Secret Scanning with `Gitleaks` (Must set `fetch-depth: 0`)
By default, `actions/checkout@v4` performs a shallow clone of only **the last 1 commit** (`fetch-depth: 1`). If a developer accidentally commits a secret in commit #1 of a PR and deletes that line in commit #2, a shallow scan will **miss the secret still sitting in commit #1's history**.
- [x] Always set ==`fetch-depth: 0`== to fetch the full commit history.
- [x] Always pass the **`--redact`** flag so Gitleaks masks secrets with `***` instead of printing discovered secret strings to CI logs.

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0
- name: Quét rò rỉ khoá bí mật xuyên suốt lịch sử commit
  run: gitleaks detect --source . --no-banner --redact
```

### 2) Layers 2 & 3 — First-Party Code Analysis (`Semgrep`) and Third-Party Dependencies (`npm audit --omit=dev`)
- **`SAST` (`Semgrep`):** Scans for security flaws in the codebase written by your own development team.
- **`SCA` (`npm audit`):** Use the modern standard flag ==`--omit=dev`== (replacing the legacy `--production` flag) to **audit only packages that actually run in Production (`dependencies`)**, skipping development tools:

```yaml
- name: Kiểm toán lỗ hổng thư viện Production (SCA)
  run: npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high

- name: Phân tích mã nguồn tĩnh SAST
  run: semgrep ci
```

### 3) Layers 4 & 5 — Configuring the `Trivy` Quality Gate and Generating `CycloneDX SBOM`
> [!WARNING] Important note on Trivy: `--exit-code` defaults to `0`
> If you only run `trivy image ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:1.0` and **forget to pass `--exit-code 1`**, even if Trivy detects **12 `CRITICAL` vulnerabilities**, it will only print a warning table and return exit code `0`—causing the pipeline to pass green and push the vulnerable image straight to Production.

Always combine these **3 critical flags** on the Trivy security gate:
1. ==`--exit-code 1`==: Forces a non-zero exit code (`1`) to block the pipeline when violations are found.
2. **`--severity CRITICAL`**: Focuses pipeline blocking on high-impact critical vulnerabilities.
3. ==`--ignore-unfixed`==: Blocks only on CVEs that **already have an official fix** from the OS/library maintainer—ensuring that whenever the pipeline fails, developers always have a clear upgrade path instead of turning on `continue-on-error: true`.

```yaml
- name: Cổng chặn lỗ hổng Container mức CRITICAL đã có bản vá
  run: trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:${{ github.sha }}

- name: Xuất hồ sơ nguyên liệu CycloneDX SBOM
  run: trivy image --format cyclonedx --output sbom.cdx.json ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:${{ github.sha }}
```

steps.headingEn: Risks of Docker-in-Docker (`privileged`) and Rootless Container Builds with **Kaniko**
steps.bodyEn:
On GitLab CI or shared internal Kubernetes Runner clusters, building a Docker image inside a CI container traditionally enabled the `docker:dind` service with `privileged: true`, or bind-mounted the physical host's `/var/run/docker.sock` socket directly into the Runner.

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Đóng Gói Container Trên Cụm Runner Nội Bộ: docker:dind (Privileged) vs Kaniko Rootless"
subtitle: "Không bao giờ trao quyền root máy chủ vật lý cho một tiến trình CI đang biên dịch mã nguồn từ Pull Request!"
left:
  badge: "RỦI RO LEO THANG ĐẶC QUYỀN · Cách cũ"
  title: "docker:dind (privileged: true) / Gắn docker.sock"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # NGUY HIỂM TRÊN RUNNER DÙNG CHUNG:
    build_image:
      image: docker:27
      services:
        - name: docker:27-dind
          # Mở toang quyền nhân Linux của máy chủ vật lý!
      variables:
        DOCKER_HOST: tcp://docker:2375
      # Hoặc gắn trực tiếp /var/run/docker.sock của Host
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Bật ==`privileged: true`== hoặc gắn `docker.sock` tương đương **trao thẳng quyền `root` tối cao của máy chủ Runner vật lý** cho mã lệnh trong Job"
    - "Tin tặc có thể thoát khỏi container (*Container Escape*), đọc trộm biến môi trường và mã nguồn của mọi dự án khác đang chạy chung trên Node đó!"
right:
  badge: "CHUẨN CLOUD-NATIVE · Daemonless & Rootless"
  title: "Kaniko Executor / BuildKit Rootless"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # AN TOÀN TUYỆT ĐỐI TRÊN KUBERNETES / GITLAB RUNNER:
    build_image:
      stage: build
      image:
        name: gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor:debug
        entrypoint: [""]
      script:
        - /kaniko/executor
          --context "${CI_PROJECT_DIR}"
          --dockerfile "${CI_PROJECT_DIR}/Dockerfile"
          --destination "${CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE}:${CI_COMMIT_SHA}"
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "**Kaniko** giải nén từng lớp `Dockerfile` hoàn toàn trong không gian người dùng (*Userspace*)"
    - "**Không cần Docker Daemon chạy ngầm** và **không cần cờ `privileged: true`** — đóng gói xong đẩy thẳng ảnh lên Registry an toàn tuyệt đối"
```

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **Gitleaks** requires **`fetch-depth: 0`** to scan the full commit history · **SAST (`Semgrep`)** scans first-party code vs. **SCA (`npm audit --omit=dev`)** scans third-party dependencies.
> - The **`trivy image`** gate MUST include **`--exit-code 1`** (since it defaults to `0`!) combined with **`--severity CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed`**.
> - **SBOM (`CycloneDX` / `SPDX`)** stores a release component inventory for instant Zero-day impact lookups.
> - Stay away from `docker:dind` (`privileged: true`) on shared Runners; prefer **Kaniko** or **Rootless BuildKit**!

readings.noteEn: A complete 5-layer DevSecOps pipeline from scanning commit history for leaked secrets to publishing a CycloneDX SBOM.
readings.taskEn: Why must the checkout step for Gitleaks specify `fetch-depth: 0` instead of leaving the default?
readings.answerEn: By default, `actions/checkout@v4` fetches only the latest commit (`fetch-depth: 1`). If a developer accidentally commits a password in an earlier commit and deletes it in a later commit within the same PR, the password remains in the branch history—only `fetch-depth: 0` lets Gitleaks scan the entire commit history!

readings.noteEn: Analyzing the host-escape privilege escalation risk of running `docker:dind` with `privileged: true` and migrating to Kaniko.
readings.taskEn: Explain the mechanism that allows Kaniko to build a Dockerfile into a complete container image without running a `dockerd` daemon.
readings.answerEn: Kaniko extracts the base image and executes each Dockerfile instruction entirely in userspace inside a single container, snapshots the filesystem after each step, and pushes the resulting image layers directly to the Registry over the HTTPS API.

C11-Q1.qEn: If you run `trivy image ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:1.0` with default flags and **forget to pass `--exit-code 1`**, what happens when Trivy finds 12 `CRITICAL` vulnerabilities?
choicesEn: The pipeline automatically stops and sends a red alert immediately
Trivy prints the table of 12 vulnerabilities to the log output but still returns exit code `0`, causing the pipeline to pass GREEN and push the vulnerable image straight to Production!
Trivy automatically patches the Dockerfile source code and rebuilds the image
GitHub automatically deletes the repository for safety
C11-Q1.explainEn: By default, `trivy` uses `--exit-code 0` (reporting-only mode)! To turn Trivy into an actual Security Gate, you must pass `--exit-code 1`.

C11-Q2.qEn: The `--ignore-unfixed` flag on `trivy image` reduces practical noise by blocking the pipeline only for vulnerabilities that ALREADY HAVE an official patch from the OS or library maintainer.
C11-Q2.explainEn: True! Blocking developers over a CVE with no fix available anywhere only forces teams to helplessly enable `continue-on-error: true`. Combining `--severity CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed` ensures every red failure has a clear upgrade path.

C11-Q3.qEn: What numeric value must be set for the `fetch-depth` option on `actions/checkout@v4` so `gitleaks` fetches the full commit history to catch secrets that were later deleted?
C11-Q3.explainEn: `fetch-depth: 0` fetches the complete history for all branches and tags (instead of the default `1`, which only fetches a shallow snapshot of the latest commit).

C11-Q4.qEn: What is the difference in inspection target between **SAST** (like `Semgrep`) and **SCA** (like `npm audit`)?
choicesEn: SAST scans source code written by your own team (finding security logic bugs such as SQLi and XSS), whereas SCA checks third-party library packages listed in `package-lock.json` against known CVE vulnerability databases
SAST only runs on macOS while SCA only runs on Linux
SAST measures HTTP response latency while SCA compresses PNG images
The two terms are 100% identical
C11-Q4.explainEn: SAST = Static Application Security Testing (in-house code); SCA = Software Composition Analysis (open-source third-party dependencies in `node_modules`).

C11-Q5.qEn: Which operational challenge does an **SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)** exported in `CycloneDX` or `SPDX` format solve most effectively?
choicesEn: Doubling the JSON parsing speed of the V8 Engine
Recording an exact inventory of every package and version inside each release so that when a new Zero-day breaks, the organization can look up which services are affected in seconds
Completely replacing the Dockerfile
Automatically writing unit tests for an Express application
C11-Q5.explainEn: An SBOM is like the parts manifest of each manufactured aircraft: when a supplier announces batch X of bolts is defective, you look up the SBOM inventory and immediately know which planes need urgent patching!

C11-Q6.qEn: Using the `docker:dind` service with `privileged: true` on a shared GitLab Runner cluster allows code inside a Job to escalate privileges and break out of the container onto the physical host.
C11-Q6.explainEn: True! A container with `privileged: true` gets full access to host hardware devices and the Runner host kernel. The safe alternative is using Kaniko or rootless BuildKit.

C11-Q7.qEn: Which CLI flag for `npm audit` audits only Production runtime packages (`dependencies`) and skips development tools (`devDependencies`)?
C11-Q7.explainEn: Modern npm (Node 18/20/22+) uses `--omit=dev` (replacing the deprecated `--production` flag).

C11-C1.frontEn: Name the 5 layers of an enterprise DevSecOps Security Funnel in the right order.
C11-C1.backEn: 1) Secret Scanning (`Gitleaks`), 2) SAST static analysis (`Semgrep`), 3) SCA dependency audit (`npm audit --omit=dev`), 4) Container Image CVE gate (`Trivy image`), 5) `SBOM` export (`CycloneDX`).

C11-C2.frontEn: What are the two most important flags to remember when running `gitleaks detect` in CI?
C11-C2.backEn: Set `fetch-depth: 0` in the preceding `checkout` step to fetch full Git history, and pass `--redact` to `gitleaks` so secret strings are masked and never printed in logs.

C11-C3.frontEn: What is the pragmatic `trivy image` gate command that avoids false-positive noise?

C11-C4.frontEn: What is an SBOM, and what are the two most widely adopted SBOM formats in 2026?
C11-C4.backEn: Software Bill of Materials. The two international standard formats are **CycloneDX** (`cyclonedx`) and **SPDX** (`spdx-json`).

C11-C5.frontEn: Why is Kaniko dramatically safer than `docker:dind` on GitLab / Kubernetes Runners?
C11-C5.backEn: Kaniko builds images entirely in userspace without a Docker Daemon or `privileged: true`, eliminating the risk of privilege escalation to take over the Runner host.

C11-C6.frontEn: Why should you pass `--ignore-scripts` when running `npm ci` in a PR security audit step?
C11-C6.backEn: It prevents malicious `preinstall`/`postinstall` lifecycle scripts hidden in untrusted packages from automatically executing arbitrary code during installation.

C11-C7.frontEn: Briefly distinguish the inspection targets of `SAST` vs. `SCA`.
C11-C7.backEn:
- **SAST** (*Static Application Security Testing* — e.g., `Semgrep`, `CodeQL`): scans for security flaws in **code written by your own team** (`src/`).
- **SCA** (*Software Composition Analysis* — e.g., `npm audit`, `pip-audit`): scans for known CVEs in **third-party libraries you install** (via lockfiles).

cicd-ex-c11-1.titleEn: Configure DevSecOps Layer 1: Scan Full Git History with Gitleaks
cicd-ex-c11-1.promptEn:
Set up the first checkpoint to stop developers from accidentally pushing API keys into branch history:

1. On the `actions/checkout@v4` step: add `with.fetch-depth: 0` to fetch the entire commit history.
2. Add a step running `gitleaks detect --source . --no-banner --redact`.
hintsEn: `fetch-depth: 0` is an integer `0` (not wrapped in quotes).

cicd-ex-c11-2.titleEn: Configure Layers 2 & 3: SCA Audit (npm audit --omit=dev) and SAST (semgrep)
cicd-ex-c11-2.promptEn:
Complete the `code-security` Job so it genuinely enforces both SCA and SAST checks (no `continue-on-error` faking a green pass!):

1. Remove `continue-on-error: true` that swallows failures on the dependency audit step, and use the modern command `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`.
2. Add a final step running static analysis with `semgrep ci`.
hintsEn: Always use `--omit=dev` (Node 22 standard), not the legacy `--production` flag.

cicd-ex-c11-3.titleEn: Configure Layer 4: Container Image Vulnerability Gate with Trivy
cicd-ex-c11-3.promptEn:
The `Scan Docker image` step below runs `trivy image` without the exit-code flag, letting images with critical vulnerabilities pass right through a green gate!

Fix the `trivy image` command to include all 3 required parameters:
`trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:${{ github.sha }}`

cicd-ex-c11-4.titleEn: Configure Layer 5: Publish a CycloneDX SBOM as a Build Artifact
cicd-ex-c11-4.promptEn:
To satisfy supply-chain security audits, after building the `ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:${{ github.sha }}` image:

1. Run the command to generate a CycloneDX SBOM file at `sbom.cdx.json`:
   `trivy image --format cyclonedx --output sbom.cdx.json ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:${{ github.sha }}`
2. Use `actions/upload-artifact@v4` to upload `sbom.cdx.json` with `name: sbom-cyclonedx` and `retention-days: 30`.

cicd-ex-c11-5.titleEn: Replace Dangerous Privileged Docker-in-Docker with Rootless Kaniko on GitLab CI
cicd-ex-c11-5.promptEn:
The `.gitlab-ci.yml` below uses the `docker:27-dind` service in privileged mode, leaving the door wide open for container escapes on shared Runners!

Migrate the `build_image` Job to rootless **Kaniko**:
1. Completely remove the `services:` field (`docker:27-dind`).
2. Change `build_image.image` to `{ name: "gcr.io/kaniko-project/executor:debug", entrypoint: [""] }`.
3. In `script:`, invoke `/kaniko/executor --context "$CI_PROJECT_DIR" --dockerfile "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/Dockerfile" --destination "$CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE:$CI_COMMIT_SHA"`.
hintsEn: On GitLab CI, `kaniko-project/executor:debug` requires overriding `entrypoint: [""]` in the `image:` block so GitLab can feed `script:` into the BusyBox shell.

C12.titleEn: Cloud Authentication with Keyless OIDC, IAM Trust Policies & SLSA Provenance
C12.summaryEn: Eliminate long-lived AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID credentials permanently using OpenID Connect identity federation (id-token: write), lock down the sub claim in IAM Trust Policies, and sign SLSA Provenance attestations.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
Be honest and check whether your organization is still following this high-risk habit:
- [!] An administrator goes into AWS IAM, creates a `ci-deployer` service user, and exports a long-lived key pair **`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` (`AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`)** and **`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`** that expires... never!
- [!] That key pair is copy-pasted into **GitHub Secrets** across 15 different repositories, and for 3 years nobody dares rotate it for fear of breaking deployment pipelines!

If that static key is ever leaked via a compromised third-party Action, an attacker sitting in any coffee shop on earth can use it to mine crypto or wipe your AWS databases for weeks without it ever expiring!

By 2026, industry standards have **completely eliminated long-lived static keys in CI/CD** using the ==OpenID Connect (OIDC)== identity federation protocol (short-lived **JWT** tokens) paired with **SLSA Build Provenance** attestations.

steps.headingEn: Keyless Authentication Mechanism with OpenID Connect (OIDC)
steps.bodyEn:
Instead of storing long-lived credentials (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`) in GitHub Secrets, **Keyless OIDC** relies on a cryptographic trust relationship between the CI provider and the Cloud provider:
- When a deployment Job starts with `id-token: write`, the GitHub OIDC Provider issues a **short-lived JWT** containing organization, repository, and Git branch claims (`sub` & `aud`).
- The Runner sends this JWT to **AWS STS** (or **GCP Workload Identity Federation**). The cloud provider verifies GitHub's public signature, checks for an exact match in the Trust Policy conditions, and issues **temporary session credentials that auto-expire after 15–60 minutes**. *(This works just like issuing a temporary visitor badge that deactivates after one session instead of handing out a permanent master key).*

```visual
kind: flow
title: "Luồng Bắt Tay Xác Thực Không Khoá Tĩnh (Keyless OIDC Handshake) [!badge:emerald:Zero Static Secrets]"
subtitle: Chuyển đổi từ thẻ định danh JWT ký số của GitHub sang phiên làm việc tạm thời trên AWS STS hoàn toàn tự động
steps:
  - icon: workflow
    badge: "Bước 1 · Xin thẻ"
    title: GitHub Actions Job
    desc: Nhờ quyền id-token:write, Runner gọi tới OIDC Endpoint nội bộ của GitHub
    code: "id-token: write"
    tone: sky
    edge: ký số JWT
  - icon: key
    badge: "Bước 2 · Đúc thẻ JWT"
    title: GitHub OIDC Provider
    desc: Phát hành thẻ JWT ngắn hạn chứa danh tính repo, nhánh ref, commit sha
    code: "aud: sts.amazonaws.com"
    tone: cyan
    edge: AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
  - icon: shield-check
    badge: "Bước 3 · Đối chiếu"
    title: AWS STS & Trust Policy
    desc: Xác minh chữ ký công khai GitHub + kiểm tra khớp chặt aud và sub
    code: "sub == repo:acme-corp/..."
    tone: amber
    edge: cấp phiên ngắn hạn
  - icon: cloud
    badge: "Bước 4 · Triển khai"
    title: Short-lived Token (1h)
    desc: Cấp thông tin đăng nhập tạm thời tự huỷ sau 15-60 phút để đẩy lên EKS/S3
    code: "Auto-expires in <= 1h"
    tone: emerald
```

### Three Key Benefits and Two Required Workflow Settings
- [x] **Zero static keys stored in GitHub Secrets:** Nothing long-lived to steal, and no 90-day manual key-rotation reminders.
- [x] **Ultra-short automatic expiration:** As soon as the Job finishes (or after at most 1 hour), the session credentials become invalid.
- [x] **Granular context control down to the branch:** The cloud provider knows the exact repository, branch, and environment making the request.

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Chuyển Đổi Cấu Hình AWS Trên GitHub Actions: Khoá Tĩnh Cũ vs Keyless OIDC"
subtitle: "Xoá bỏ hoàn toàn cặp aws-access-key-id & aws-secret-access-key khỏi cả YAML lẫn GitHub Secrets!"
left:
  badge: "CÁCH CŨ RỦI RO CAO · Khoá tĩnh vĩnh viễn"
  title: "Lưu cặp Access Key / Secret Key dài hạn"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    deploy-aws:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
          with:
            # Lộ 2 biến này là mất quyền AWS dài hạn!
            aws-access-key-id: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
            aws-secret-access-key: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
            aws-region: ap-southeast-1
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Phải sinh khoá tĩnh `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` không tự hết hạn và rải thủ công vào từng kho Git"
    - "Không thể giới hạn ở phía AWS rằng khoá đó chỉ được phép gọi từ đúng nhánh `main`"
right:
  badge: "CHUẨN HIỆN ĐẠI 2026 · Keyless OIDC"
  title: "Dùng id-token: write + role-to-assume"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    deploy-aws:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      permissions:
        id-token: write       # BẮT BUỘC để xin thẻ OIDC JWT!
        contents: read
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        - uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
          with:
            role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/github-oidc-shop-api-prod
            aws-region: ap-southeast-1
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Bắt buộc khai báo quyền ==`id-token: write`== trong `permissions:` để Runner đúc thẻ JWT"
    - "Xoá sạch `aws-access-key-id` và `aws-secret-access-key`; chỉ truyền chuỗi ARN định danh ==`role-to-assume`=="
```

steps.headingEn: Strictly Locking Down the `sub` Condition in **AWS IAM Trust Policies**
steps.bodyEn:
> [!WARNING] Risk of Misconfiguring IAM Trust Policy Conditions
> Millions of users worldwide share the **exact same OIDC token issuer**: `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`!
> If in your AWS **IAM Role Trust Policy** you only check the issuer and **forget to lock down `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub` (Subject)**—or carelessly write a wildcard `"repo:*"`—then **any stranger on earth can create a personal GitHub repo, plug in your Role ARN, and take over your company's entire AWS account**!

```visual
kind: anatomy
title: Ba trường định danh quan trọng trong thẻ OIDC JWT và IAM Trust Policy
subtitle: AWS STS dùng khoá công khai của GitHub xác minh chữ ký rồi kiểm tra từng trường trong khối Condition.StringEquals
items:
  - keyword: "iss (Issuer)"
    role: Nhà phát hành thẻ
    tone: sky
    summary: Xác nhận thẻ JWT thực sự do hệ thống GitHub Actions chính thức ký phát hành.
    bullets:
      - "**Chưa đủ để phân quyền!** Vì mọi tài khoản GitHub trên toàn cầu đều có chung `iss` này"
    example: "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
    lang: text
  - keyword: "aud (Audience)"
    role: Dịch vụ đám mây đích
    tone: amber
    summary: Chỉ định rõ thẻ JWT này được đúc riêng cho dịch vụ AWS Security Token Service.
    bullets:
      - "Giá trị chuẩn mặc định khi xác thực với AWS STS luôn là ==`sts.amazonaws.com`=="
    example: "token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud: \"sts.amazonaws.com\""
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: "sub (Subject)"
    role: Định danh Kho & Nhánh gốc
    tone: emerald
    summary: Chuỗi định danh duy nhất khoá cứng đúng Tổ chức + đúng Kho + đúng Nhánh được phép đảm nhận Role.
    bullets:
      - "Khoá bằng `StringEquals` vào `repo:acme-corp/shop-api:ref:refs/heads/main` sẽ từ chối thẳng thừng cả nhánh thử nghiệm `feat/*` hay PR nội bộ!"
    example: "token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub: \"repo:acme-corp/shop-api:ref:refs/heads/main\""
    lang: yaml
```

Standard hardened configuration in an **AWS IAM Role Trust Policy**:

```yaml
Condition:
  StringEquals:
    token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud: sts.amazonaws.com
    token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub: repo:acme-corp/shop-api:ref:refs/heads/main
```

> [!TIP] Not Just AWS — Google Cloud (GCP) & Azure Use the Same OIDC Standard!
> Following the exact same principle as AWS STS: on **Google Cloud**, configure **Workload Identity Federation (WIF)** with `assertion.sub == 'repo:acme-corp/shop-api:ref:refs/heads/main'` via `google-github-actions/auth@v2` (eliminating long-lived JSON Service Account Keys); on **Microsoft Azure**, use **Federated Identity Credentials** with `azure/login@v2`!

---

steps.headingEn: Verifying Build Origin with **SLSA Build Provenance**
steps.bodyEn:
Even when source code is well protected, a Production Kubernetes cluster still needs to verify that the container image `ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:sha-9f8e7d` was **actually built automatically on GitHub Actions from the `main` branch**, rather than built manually on an external laptop and pushed over the Registry tag.

The **SLSA Build Provenance** (*Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts*) standard solves this by generating a cryptographic attestation bound to the artifact or container image, recording the exact source Git repository, commit SHA, workflow path, and builder identity. Using **OIDC (`id-token: write`)** combined with ==`attestations: write`==, you can sign build provenance at packaging time with `actions/attest-build-provenance@v2` (or keyless signing via **Sigstore Cosign**). *(If the `SBOM` from module `C11` is the ingredient list, `SLSA Build Provenance` acts as the certificate of origin verifying how the build was produced).*

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write
  id-token: write
  attestations: write

steps:
  # ... sau bước build & push ảnh container xuất ra digest ...
  - name: Ký chứng thực nguồn gốc bản dựng (SLSA Build Provenance)
    uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@v2
    with:
      subject-name: ghcr.io/acme/shop-api
      subject-digest: ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}
      push-to-registry: true
```

Before launching a Pod on the Kubernetes cluster (via **Kyverno** / Policy Controller) or running `gh attestation verify` on the CLI, the system verifies this cryptographic signature in an instant—ensuring the software package originated from the exact expected repository, commit SHA, and workflow file!

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - In GitHub Actions Workflows: Enable **`permissions: { id-token: write }`**, remove `aws-access-key-id` / `aws-secret-access-key`, and replace them with **`role-to-assume`**.
> - In **AWS IAM Trust Policies**: Lock down both **`aud: "sts.amazonaws.com"`** and **`sub: "repo:acme-corp/shop-api:ref:refs/heads/main"`** (never allow `"repo:*"`!).
> - Use **`actions/attest-build-provenance@v2`** (`attestations: write`) following **SLSA** to sign tamper-proof build provenance.

readings.noteEn: Deploying to AWS without storing any static secrets in GitHub Secrets by exchanging short-lived OIDC JWT tokens.
readings.taskEn: What happens if you forget to declare `id-token: write` in the Job's `permissions` block?
readings.answerEn: The `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4` action fails immediately with `Unable to get ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` because GitHub refuses to issue an identity JWT to a Job without `id-token: write` permission.

readings.noteEn: An AWS IAM Role Trust Policy enforcing `StringEquals` on both the `aud` and `sub` claims of the OIDC token.
readings.taskEn: Explain the security consequence if an administrator configures `StringLike` with `"repo:*:ref:refs/heads/main"` for the `sub` claim.
readings.answerEn: The `*` wildcard in the organization/repository segment allows ANY stranger in the world to create a personal GitHub repo with a `main` branch and assume your company's IAM Role to take control of your AWS infrastructure!

readings.noteEn: Stamping SLSA Build Provenance attestations and keyless container signatures (Cosign) tied to the Workflow's OIDC identity.
readings.taskEn: Which insider or supply-chain attack scenario does Build Provenance help a Kubernetes cluster defend against?
readings.answerEn: It prevents an attacker (or a compromised personal laptop belonging to an engineer with Registry push access) from building a backdoored container image outside the official CI pipeline and pushing it to masquerade as a valid release.

C12-Q1.qEn: Which required key in a GitHub Actions Job's `permissions:` block allows the Runner to request a cloud-authentication JWT from GitHub's OIDC provider? (Write the key name before `: write`)
C12-Q1.explainEn: `id-token: write` is the dedicated permission that allows a Job to call GitHub's OIDC Token Endpoint to obtain a short-lived JWT.

C12-Q2.qEn: In a **Keyless OIDC** authentication flow between GitHub Actions and AWS, what is actually sent from the Runner to AWS STS (`AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`)?
choicesEn: A static `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` pair saved from last year
An OIDC JSON Web Token (JWT) cryptographically signed by GitHub containing identity claims (`repo`, `ref`, `environment`, `sha`) that expires within minutes
The AWS administrator's personal account login password
An SSH private key file `~/.ssh/id_rsa`
C12-Q2.explainEn: GitHub signs the JWT using GitHub's private key; AWS STS uses GitHub's public key to verify the signature and validate the `aud` and `sub` claims before issuing temporary session credentials.

C12-Q3.qEn: When configuring an AWS IAM Role Trust Policy for GitHub OIDC, checking only the issuer `token.actions.githubusercontent.com` is completely secure without checking the `sub` claim.
C12-Q3.explainEn: False—and dangerously wrong! Millions of GitHub repositories worldwide share the exact same issuer `token.actions.githubusercontent.com`. Without locking `sub` to your specific `repo:org-name/repo-name:...`, anyone on GitHub can assume your AWS Role!

C12-Q4.qEn: When migrating to OIDC on `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4`, which two old inputs are **completely removed** and replaced by which input?
choicesEn: Remove `aws-region`, replace with `aws-zone`
Remove `aws-access-key-id` and `aws-secret-access-key`, replace with `role-to-assume` (containing the IAM Role ARN)
Remove `uses`, replace with `run: aws login`
Remove `node-version`, replace with `python-version`
C12-Q4.explainEn: No Access Key or Secret Key remains in YAML or GitHub Secrets—you only pass the non-secret identifier `role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::...:role/...`!

C12-Q5.qEn: What is the standard Audience (`aud`) domain value when authenticating GitHub Actions OIDC with the AWS Security Token Service?
C12-Q5.explainEn: For standard AWS accounts, the Audience value expected by `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` and checked by the IAM Trust Policy is `sts.amazonaws.com`.

C12-Q6.qEn: Build provenance attestation (**Artifact Build Provenance** under SLSA) creates non-repudiable cryptographic proof of the exact Git repository, commit SHA, and workflow file that produced a software package.
C12-Q6.explainEn: True! `actions/attest-build-provenance@v2` signs the build metadata using a short-lived certificate tied to OIDC, enabling transparent verification at deployment time.

C12-Q7.qEn: Which `sub` (Subject) identifier below most strictly restricts AWS IAM Role assumption to runs from the `main` branch of the `acme-corp/shop-api` repository?
choicesEn: repo:*
repo:acme-corp/*:ref:*
repo:acme-corp/shop-api:ref:refs/heads/main
github.com/acme-corp
C12-Q7.explainEn: `repo:acme-corp/shop-api:ref:refs/heads/main` locks down the exact organization (`acme-corp`), repository (`shop-api`), and official branch (`refs/heads/main`), rejecting any experimental branches or PRs.

C12-C1.frontEn: Why does Keyless OIDC eliminate the risk of long-lived cloud credential leaks in CI/CD?
C12-C1.backEn: Because no static keys (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` / `GCP_SA_KEY`) exist in GitHub Secrets; each Job exchanges a short-lived OIDC JWT for temporary credentials that auto-expire in 15–60 minutes.

C12-C2.frontEn: What are the two required configuration changes in a GitHub Actions Workflow to use AWS OIDC?
C12-C2.backEn: 1) Grant `permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }`, 2) Call `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4` with `role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::...` and `aws-region`.

C12-C3.frontEn: What are the two required `Condition.StringEquals` claims in an AWS IAM Trust Policy for GitHub OIDC?

C12-C4.frontEn: What severe vulnerability occurs if you forget to check `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub` on the cloud side?
C12-C4.backEn: Cross-tenant Impersonation: any GitHub user who knows your Role ARN can create their own Workflow and gain full control over your cloud account!

C12-C5.frontEn: Which two permissions must be declared in `permissions:` when using `actions/attest-build-provenance@v2`?
C12-C5.backEn: `id-token: write` (to obtain a short-lived OIDC identity certificate via Sigstore Fulcio) and `attestations: write` (to persist the provenance attestation).

C12-C6.frontEn: What threat does SLSA Build Provenance protect an organization against?
C12-C6.backEn: Artifact Tampering: it guarantees that container images running in Production were 100% compiled by the CI server from approved source code, rather than built illicitly outside CI.

cicd-ex-c12-1.titleEn: Grant Least-Privilege id-token: write Permission to Mint OIDC Tokens
cicd-ex-c12-1.promptEn:
The `deploy-cloud` Job is failing when requesting an OIDC token with `Unable to get ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` because it lacks token-minting permission!

Add a `permissions` block directly inside the `deploy-cloud` Job with exactly these 2 least-privilege permissions:

cicd-ex-c12-2.titleEn: Migrate from Static AWS Keys to Keyless OIDC role-to-assume
cicd-ex-c12-2.promptEn:
The legacy deployment file uses long-lived static credentials `aws-access-key-id` and `aws-secret-access-key`. The Infrastructure team has provisioned an OIDC Role with ARN `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/shop-api-oidc-deploy` in `ap-southeast-1`.

Upgrade the `deploy` Job to **Keyless OIDC**:
1. Add `permissions: { id-token: write, contents: read }` to the `deploy` Job.
2. Upgrade `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` to `@v4`.
3. Completely remove `aws-access-key-id` and `aws-secret-access-key`, replacing them with `role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/shop-api-oidc-deploy` (keep `aws-region: ap-southeast-1`).
hintsEn: Double-check all 3 places: add `permissions:` at the Job level, bump `@v2` to `@v4`, and replace the 2 static key lines with 1 `role-to-assume` line.

cicd-ex-c12-3.titleEn: Lock Down sub and aud Conditions in an AWS IAM Role Trust Policy
cicd-ex-c12-3.promptEn:
The IAM Role Trust Policy below is wide open with no `Condition`, allowing any GitHub account in the world to assume your company's Role!

Add a `Condition.StringEquals` block inside `Statement[0]` to strictly enforce both claims:
- `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:aud: sts.amazonaws.com`
- `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub: repo:acme-corp/shop-api:ref:refs/heads/main`
hintsEn: `Condition:` goes inside the `- Effect: Allow` item (indented at the same level as `Effect`, `Principal`, and `Action`).
Verify every character of `repo:acme-corp/shop-api:ref:refs/heads/main`.

cicd-ex-c12-4.titleEn: Sign SLSA Build Provenance Attestations with actions/attest-build-provenance@v2
cicd-ex-c12-4.promptEn:
Complete the `release-bundle` Job to stamp a cryptographic SLSA Build Provenance attestation onto the release artifact `dist/app.tgz`:

1. In `jobs.release-bundle.permissions`: grant `contents: read`, **`id-token: write`**, and **`attestations: write`**.
2. Add a final step calling `actions/attest-build-provenance@v2` with `with.subject-path: dist/app.tgz`.
hintsEn: Add `id-token: write` and `attestations: write` under `permissions:`, then append `- uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@v2` at the end of `steps:`.

C13.titleEn: Release Governance: GitHub Environments, CODEOWNERS & AI PR Review
C13.summaryEn: Configure GitHub Environments to isolate Staging/Production with manual approval gates, enforce permissions via .github/CODEOWNERS, and optimize AI PR Reviewers for low noise and safety against Fork PRs.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
In the previous stage, you built automated security guardrails (5-Layer DevSecOps & Keyless OIDC). However, in real-world enterprise environments, automated scanning tools alone are not enough:
- [>] **Who** is authorized to approve a Production release at 11:00 AM on a Friday?
- [>] **Who** is responsible for signing off when a Pull Request quietly modifies `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` or adds SQL statements that alter the database schema?
- [>] How do you leverage an **AI PR Reviewer** (such as CodeRabbit or GitHub Copilot Code Review) to catch logic bugs early without generating noisy comments or leaking `OPENAI_API_KEY` from a Fork?

This lesson covers all 3 pillars of **Release Governance**: **GitHub Environments**, **CODEOWNERS + Branch Protection**, and a **Low-Noise AI Review Gate** — ensuring ==strict risk control== without slowing down release velocity.

```visual
      - "Bật **Required Reviewers** làm cổng duyệt tay có nhật ký kiểm toán (*Audit Log*)"
```

If you dump all sensitive variables into **Repository Secrets**, any job in the repository (including a draft job running on a feature branch if misconfigured) can read the same `DATABASE_URL` or `AWS_ROLE_ARN` — which is no different from keeping `.env.development` and `.env.production` together with zero isolation!

**GitHub Environments** (`staging`, `production`) lock secrets behind **Protection Rules**:
- [x] **Environment Secrets & Variables:** A variable like `AWS_ROLE_ARN` stored in the `production` Environment is **only decrypted and exposed to the runner when the job explicitly declares `environment: production` AND passes all protection rules** (allowed branch + a reviewer clicking **Approve**).
- [x] **Visual link display with `environment.url`:** Declaring the ==`url`== key inside the `environment` object adds a direct button to open the newly deployed website right on the Pipeline graph and in GitHub's Deployments tab.

```visual
    code: "npm run test:smoke"

  - icon: lock

    title: Required Reviewers

    code: "branch == main + Approve"
    tone: amber

  - icon: rocket

```

```yaml
jobs:
  deploy-staging:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: staging
      url: https://staging.shop.example.com
    steps:
      - run: ./scripts/deploy.sh staging

  smoke-staging:
    needs: deploy-staging
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: npm run test:smoke -- --baseUrl=https://staging.shop.example.com

  deploy-production:
    needs: smoke-staging
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://shop.example.com
    steps:
      - run: ./scripts/deploy.sh production
```

steps.headingEn: .github/CODEOWNERS & Branch Protection: Path-Based Access Control
steps.bodyEn:
In a project with 20 developers, if Branch Protection only enables *"Require 1 approval"*, two Frontend developers could cross-approve each other's PR... modifying IAM permissions or editing `.github/workflows/release.yml` itself!

The **`.github/CODEOWNERS`** file maps sensitive paths to their dedicated owning teams (GitHub Teams):

```ini
# 1) Quy tắc tổng quát đầu file: Mặc định do nhóm Backend cốt lõi phụ trách
*                           @acme/backend-maintainers

# 2) Các quy tắc cụ thể ở dưới sẽ GHI ĐÈ quy tắc tổng quát ở trên (Last Match Wins!)
/.github/workflows/         @acme/platform-devops @acme/security-team
/Dockerfile                 @acme/platform-devops
/db/migrations/             @acme/dba-team
/src/auth/                  @acme/security-team
```

> [!WARNING] Two important rules when configuring `CODEOWNERS`
> 1. **Precedence order — ==The last matching line wins (*Last match wins*)==:** Just like `.gitignore`, `CODEOWNERS` is evaluated from top to bottom; a file at `/src/auth/jwt.ts` matches both `*` and `/src/auth/`, so the final deciding owner is `@acme/security-team`.
> 2. **Creating `.github/CODEOWNERS` alone does NOT block merges!** Unless you enable **Branch Protection** or a **Repository Ruleset** with the **`"Require review from Code Owners"`** option, `CODEOWNERS` only automatically assigns suggested reviewers and will not lock the Merge button!

At the same time, always maintain a lightweight Governance job that verifies `.github/CODEOWNERS` exists and checks that PR titles follow **Conventional Commits** (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`) safely via an ==`env:`== environment variable (never interpolate `${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}` directly into `run:` to avoid Script Injection vulnerabilities!):

```yaml
- name: Kiểm tra tiêu đề PR chuẩn Conventional Commits an toàn
  env:
    PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
  run: |
    test -f .github/CODEOWNERS
    printf '%s\n' "$PR_TITLE" | grep -Eq '^(feat|fix|chore|docs|refactor|test)(\(.+\))?: .+'
```

---

steps.headingEn: AI Review Gate (AI PR Gate): Reducing Noise & Preventing Secret Leaks from Forks
steps.bodyEn:
AI code review tools (such as **CodeRabbit** via `.coderabbit.yaml` or an internal LLM workflow) help catch missing `await` calls, memory leaks, or SQL Injection within the first 45 seconds. However, real-world adoption requires avoiding **2 common pitfalls**:

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Triển Khai AI PR Reviewer: Cấu Hình Dễ Lộ Khoá vs Chuẩn Doanh Nghiệp Ít Nhiễu"
subtitle: "Vừa lọc bỏ tệp sinh tự động (lockfile, dist) vừa khoá chặt OPENAI_API_KEY trước các Pull Request từ nhánh Fork"
left:
  badge: "RỦI RO BẢO MẬT · Nhiễu & Lộ Secret"
  title: "Dùng pull_request_target + Không lọc lockfile"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    # LỖ HỔNG PWN REQUEST LÀM LỘ OPENAI_API_KEY:
    on: pull_request_target
    jobs:
      ai-review:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
            with:
              ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          - env:
              OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
            run: node scripts/run-ai-review.js
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Dùng `pull_request_target` kèm checkout code từ Fork cho phép kẻ tấn công sửa `scripts/run-ai-review.js` hoặc `package.json` để **đánh cắp `OPENAI_API_KEY` và `GITHUB_TOKEN` quyền ghi**!"
    - "Không cấu hình bộ lọc đường dẫn khiến AI đốt hàng chục nghìn token bình luận vô nghĩa vào 12.000 dòng `package-lock.json` và `*.snap`"
right:
  badge: "CHUẨN AN TOÀN · .coderabbit.yaml & Fork Guard"
  title: "Tách lọc đường dẫn + Bảo vệ Secret nội bộ"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # 1) .coderabbit.yaml — Lọc nhiễu & Giao đề bài chuyên sâu:
    reviews:
      path_filters:
        - "!**/*.lock"
        - "!**/package-lock.json"
        - "!**/dist/**"
        - "!**/*.snap"
      path_instructions:
        - path: "src/auth/**"
          instructions: "Soi kỹ xác thực JWT, RBAC, timing attack và cấm log token."

    # 2) Workflow tự dựng: Dùng on: pull_request + Chặn Fork PR:
    # if: github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "**`reviews.path_filters`** loại trừ tệp máy sinh; ==`reviews.path_instructions`== truyền chỉ thị kiểm tra chuyên biệt cho từng vùng code nhạy cảm như `src/auth/**`"
    - "Workflow AI tự dựng luôn dùng `on: pull_request`, quyền tối thiểu `{ contents: read, pull-requests: write }` và kiểm tra `head.repo.full_name == github.repository` trước khi nạp khóa LLM"
```

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **Environment Secrets (`production`)** are only decrypted when a job satisfies all Protection Rules · **`environment.url`** displays a direct link button to the deployed site on the Pipeline graph.
> - **`.github/CODEOWNERS`** follows the **last match wins** rule and requires **Branch Protection / Rulesets** to actually block merges.
> - In **`.coderabbit.yaml`**: use **`reviews.path_filters`** to skip lockfiles/dist, and use **`reviews.path_instructions`** to provide custom review prompts per directory.
> - Never use **`pull_request_target` + checking out PR code** in a workflow that has access to `OPENAI_API_KEY`!

readings.noteEn: Standard environment promotion chain from Staging -> Smoke Test -> Production with a Required Reviewers gate.
readings.taskEn: Observe how the deploy-production job uses both environment and concurrency. Why is cancel-in-progress set to false?
readings.answerEn: In Production, canceling an in-progress deployment midway (cancel-in-progress: true) can leave infrastructure in a half-applied state; setting false queues the new deployment safely until the previous one completes.

readings.noteEn: Mandatory gatekeeper permission pattern for CI/CD Pipelines, Dockerfiles, and SQL migration directories.
readings.taskEn: If a PR modifies both src/index.ts and .github/workflows/ci.yml, which teams must click Approve?
readings.answerEn: Both @acme/core-backend-maintainers (matching the * rule for src/index.ts) and @acme/security-team plus @acme/platform-devops (matching /.github/workflows/) must approve when Require review from Code Owners is enabled.

readings.noteEn: Configuring the AI PR review assistant to focus on workflow security and SQL migrations without noise from lockfiles.
readings.taskEn: Why should !**/package-lock.json and !**/dist/** be declared in the AI reviewer's path_filters?
readings.answerEn: Lockfiles and compiled build artifacts contain tens of thousands of auto-generated lines; excluding them saves LLM context budget and avoids cluttering the PR with meaningless comments.

C13-Q1.qEn: What is the biggest security benefit of storing AWS_ROLE_ARN in an Environment Secret named "production" instead of a Repository Secret?
choicesEn: It doubles the loading speed of environment variables on the runner
The secret is only provided to jobs that declare environment: production AND pass protection rules such as Required Reviewers / allowed branches
It allows automatically sharing the secret with all external Fork branches
It lets you print the secret value to logs without being masked as ***
C13-Q1.explainEn: Environment Secrets are locked behind Protection Rules (only allowed main/tag refs + reviewer approval can decrypt them), preventing jobs on feature branches from accessing Production.

C13-Q2.qEn: In .github/CODEOWNERS, if a file path matches multiple rule lines, the LAST matching line (reading from top to bottom) determines the owner of that file.
C13-Q2.explainEn: Like .gitignore, CODEOWNERS is evaluated top to bottom, and the last more specific rule (last match wins) overrides the general * rule above it.

C13-Q3.qEn: Why must an AI PR Review workflow that uses OPENAI_API_KEY NEVER use the pull_request_target trigger together with actions/checkout on the PR's code?
choicesEn: Because pull_request_target does not support Node.js 22
Because an attacker from a Fork can open a PR modifying scripts/package.json to steal OPENAI_API_KEY and a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN in the base repo's trusted context
Because GitHub forbids calling third-party APIs in pull_request_target
Because pull_request_target cannot read the PR title
C13-Q3.explainEn: pull_request_target runs in the trusted context of the base repository (with Secrets and elevated token permissions loaded). Checking out and executing untrusted Fork code leads to a critical Pwn Request vulnerability.

C13-Q4.qEn: In the GitHub Actions job definition below, which configuration key inside the environment object displays a direct link button to the deployed website right on the Pipeline graph?
C13-Q4.explainEn: The environment.url property attaches the target environment URL directly to the workflow graph UI and GitHub's Deployments tab.

C13-Q5.qEn: In .coderabbit.yaml, which section is used to give specialized review instructions (e.g., closely checking JWT handling and RBAC permissions) specifically for the src/auth/** directory?
choicesEn: reviews.path_filters
reviews.path_instructions
reviews.ignore_keywords
reviews.auto_merge
C13-Q5.explainEn: path_filters only includes/excludes files to review (using !... globs), whereas path_instructions lets you pass targeted review prompts for specific areas of the codebase.

C13-Q6.qEn: Simply creating .github/CODEOWNERS and pushing it to main automatically blocks all merges until the code owner approves, even without enabling Branch Protection or Rulesets.
C13-Q6.explainEn: Without enabling Branch Protection or a Repository Ruleset with "Require review from Code Owners", CODEOWNERS only automatically requests suggested reviewers and does NOT block merging!

C13-Q7.qEn: Which approach below validates a Pull Request title against Conventional Commits SAFELY against Script Injection in GitHub Actions?
choicesEn: run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}" | grep -E "^(feat|fix|chore):"
Assign env: PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} and inspect the "$PR_TITLE" variable inside the run: block
Pass ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }} directly as an argument to sh -c
Use continue-on-error: true on the title check step
C13-Q7.explainEn: Passing the value via an env: environment variable ensures the shell treats the entire PR title (including $(...) or double quotes) as plain string data rather than executable commands.

C13-C1.frontEn: What 2 core governance problems do GitHub Environments solve compared to regular Repository Secrets?
C13-C1.backEn:
1) Isolate Secrets per environment (staging vs production).
2) Enforce Protection Rules such as Required Reviewers (manual approval), Wait Timer, and deployment branch restrictions.

C13-C2.frontEn: How do you write the environment syntax that displays a clickable URL in the GitHub Actions UI?

C13-C3.frontEn: How does path-matching precedence work in .github/CODEOWNERS?
C13-C3.backEn: Evaluated from top to bottom; the LAST matching line wins (last match wins). Therefore, put the default `*` rule at the top and sensitive directories (`/.github/workflows/`, `/db/migrations/`) at the bottom.

C13-C4.frontEn: What should you configure in .coderabbit.yaml so the AI PR Reviewer doesn't leave noisy comments on lockfiles and build directories?
C13-C4.backEn: Declare `reviews.path_filters` with negation prefixes `!`, for example: `["!**/*.lock", "!**/package-lock.json", "!**/dist/**"]`.

C13-C5.frontEn: How do you protect an AI PR Review workflow from leaking API keys or having permissions abused by external Forks?
C13-C5.backEn: Use `on: pull_request` (never `pull_request_target` running untrusted code), grant minimal permissions (`contents: read` + `pull-requests: write`), and check `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`.

C13-C6.frontEn: Why should you place a smoke-staging job between deploy-staging and deploy-production?
C13-C6.backEn: To automatically verify that the build is healthy on real infrastructure (Staging) before requesting manual Production approval from the Tech Lead.

C14.titleEn: Zero-Downtime Deployment: Rolling Update, Blue-Green, Canary & Automated Rollback
C14.summaryEn: Tag immutable images by Git SHA, orchestrate zero-downtime traffic shifting with Argo Rollouts (Blue-Green / Canary), run post-deploy Smoke Tests, and automatically roll back on failure.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
Imagine your Node.js application processes 2,000 orders per minute. You merge a new feature into `main`, the CI pipeline turns green, and it pushes the update to Production. Suddenly, over the next 20 seconds:
- [!] Customers get flooded with `502 Bad Gateway` errors while containers are being replaced.
- [!] Or worse: a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` slips past Unit Tests because real Production data contains `discountCode: null` that your local mocks never accounted for!

How do engineering teams release dozens of times a day with **Zero-Downtime** for customers, limit blast radius using **Canary / Blue-Green**, and have the system **automatically roll back in under 30 seconds (Automated Rollback)** when errors occur? This is achieved by combining the 3 deployment techniques below.

```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "cicd:c14"
src: "/illustrations/cicd/cicd-canary-progressive-traffic.jpg"
alt: "So sánh chuyển mạch tức thì Blue-Green với phát hành thăm dò Canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) kèm tự động quay lui khi tỷ lệ lỗi vượt ngưỡng"

caption: "Cơ chế gạt công tắc tức thì của Blue-Green trên thẻ ảnh SHA bất biến đối chiếu với nhịp mở lưu lượng Canary giám sát bởi chỉ số Prometheus"
```

steps.headingEn: Immutable Image Tags — The Prerequisite for Rollback
steps.bodyEn:
A common mistake when getting started with Docker in CI/CD is repeatedly building and overwriting the exact same `:latest` tag:

- [!] **Losing track of the previous stable release:** `:latest` is a *mutable tag* — just like publishing an npm package by constantly deleting and overwriting version `1.0.0`. At 2:00 AM when the new release crashes, the previous stable image reference has already been overwritten!
- [!] **Version skew across Nodes:** On a Kubernetes cluster with `imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent`, Node A keeps the old cached `:latest` while Node B pulls the new `:latest`, creating a mixed-version state that is notoriously hard to diagnose.

> [!TIP] Mandatory Production Standard
> Every commit passing through CI must produce an **immutable tag (==Immutable Tag==)** tied to the Git commit SHA (`ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:sha-${{ github.sha }}`) or a Semantic Version (`v1.4.2`). When a Rollback is needed, the system simply points the Deployment back to the exact `sha-<old_commit>` still sitting intact in the Container Registry!

---

steps.headingEn: Comparing 3 Release Strategies: Rolling Update vs Blue-Green vs Canary
steps.bodyEn:
Instead of terminating all old Pods before starting new Pods (*Recreate*, which causes downtime), Kubernetes and **Argo Rollouts** (`argoproj.io/v1alpha1`) provide 3 zero-downtime traffic orchestration strategies:

```visual
kind: groups
title: So Sánh 3 Chiến Lược Phát Hành Không Gián Đoạn (Zero-Downtime Strategies)
subtitle: Lựa chọn đánh đổi phù hợp giữa chi phí hạ tầng, tốc độ gạt lưu lượng và bán kính ảnh hưởng rủi ro (Blast Radius)
columns: 3
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: refresh
    title: Rolling Update
    badge: Mặc định K8s · Tiết kiệm
    tone: sky
    bullets:
      - "Thay thế cuốn chiếu từng Pod cũ sang Pod mới (kết hợp `readinessProbe` + `preStop`)"
      - "**Ưu điểm:** Không tốn gấp đôi hạ tầng, tích hợp sẵn trong `Deployment` chuẩn"
      - "**Hạn chế:** Khó chia chính xác tỷ lệ nhỏ kiểu 5% người dùng; tốc độ quay lui phụ thuộc nhịp bật lại Pod"
    footer: Phù hợp dịch vụ nội bộ & API tiêu chuẩn
  - num: 2
    icon: layers
    title: Blue-Green
    badge: Gạt 100% tức thì · Tốn ~2x cụm
    tone: cyan
    bullets:
      - "Dựng song song toàn bộ cụm **Green** (mới) cạnh cụm **Blue** (đang phục vụ khách)"
      - "Kiểm thử qua **`previewService`** trước khi gạt **`activeService`** 100% sang Green trong `< 1 giây`"
      - "**Chi phí:** Tạm thời tốn **gấp đôi (~2x)** CPU/RAM trong lúc duy trì song song hai cụm"
    footer: Lý tưởng khi cần QA kiểm tra cổng Preview trước giờ G
  - num: 3
    icon: activity
    title: Canary
    badge: Nhỏ giọt 5% → 25% → 100%
    tone: emerald
    bullets:
      - "Chuyển dần từng phần trăm nhỏ lưu lượng người dùng thật kèm nhịp nghỉ theo dõi metric"
      - "**Ưu điểm nổi bật:** Thu hẹp **bán kính ảnh hưởng (*Blast Radius*)** — nếu bản mới lỗi, 95% khách hàng còn lại không bị ảnh hưởng."
      - "**Yêu cầu:** Cần Argo Rollouts / Ingress / Service Mesh và đo lường HTTP 5xx"
    footer: Tiêu chuẩn vàng cho thanh toán & lưu lượng lớn
```

*(To visualize the difference: **Rolling Update** is like swapping buses one by one on an active route so two versions run side by side briefly; **Blue-Green** is like preparing a complete new environment alongside the old one and switching all traffic over once testing passes; and **Canary** comes from miners using canaries to detect toxic gas early — routing just 5% of initial users to the new version to monitor `5xx` error rates and `p99` latency before scaling up to 100%).*

In **Argo Rollouts**, the **Blue-Green** configuration cleanly separates real customer traffic (`activeService`) from the internal test endpoint (`previewService`):

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: shop-api
spec:
  replicas: 4
  strategy:
    blueGreen:
      activeService: shop-api-active     # Lưu lượng khách hàng thật hiện hành
      previewService: shop-api-preview   # Cổng nội bộ trỏ vào bản mới để chạy E2E/QA
      autoPromotionEnabled: false        # Đợi lệnh xác nhận mới gạt activeService sang bản mới
```

With the **Canary** strategy, the `steps` array alternates between `setWeight` (traffic percentage) and `pause`:
- Writing **`pause: { duration: "2m" }`**: Automatically waits and monitors error metrics for 2 minutes before advancing to the next step.
- Writing ==`pause: {}`== (an empty object with no `duration`): **Pauses indefinitely** as a manual gate until an operator or pipeline runs `kubectl argo rollouts promote`!

```yaml
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
        - setWeight: 5
        - pause: { duration: "2m" }   # Tự động chờ 2 phút quan sát lỗi 5xx / p99
        - setWeight: 25
        - pause: {}                   # Tạm dừng vô thời hạn chờ lệnh promote tường minh!
        - setWeight: 100
```

steps.headingEn: Post-Deploy Smoke Tests & Automated Rollback
steps.bodyEn:
Never assume a `deploy` command returning exit code `0` means "release succeeded"! The deploy command only submits configuration to the cluster; the Node.js process inside might be stuck connecting to Redis or missing an environment variable, returning `503 Service Unavailable` at `/readyz`.

```visual

title: Chu Trình Phát Hành Tự Phục Hồi — Canary + Smoke Test + Auto-Rollback
subtitle: Phát hiện lỗi thực tế ngay sau triển khai và tự động quay lui về thẻ SHA ổn định trước đó trong dưới 30 giây

  - icon: package
    badge: Bước 1 · Bất biến
    title: Immutable SHA Image
    desc: Đóng gói ảnh gắn chặt mã commit sha-<git_sha>, không bao giờ ghi đè :latest
    code: "shop-api:sha-8f3c2a1"
    tone: sky
    edge: nâng nấc lưu lượng
  - icon: zap
    badge: Bước 2 · Nhỏ giọt
    title: Canary / Blue-Green
    desc: Mở thử nghiệm lưu lượng có kiểm soát qua Argo Rollouts
    code: "setWeight: 5 -> pause"
    tone: cyan
    edge: kiểm tra /readyz
  - icon: doctor
    badge: Bước 3 · Hậu kiểm
    title: Smoke Test (curl --fail)
    desc: Thử lại có độ trễ chờ Load Balancer đồng bộ; ép mã HTTP >= 400 báo đỏ
    code: "curl --fail --retry 5"

    edge: "khi gãy -> if: failure()"
  - icon: rollback
    badge: Bước 4 · Phanh khẩn cấp

```

```visual
    - "Mọi job có `needs:` trong GitHub Actions ngầm định `if: success()` — khi `smoke-test` gãy, `rollback` bị **bỏ qua (`skipped`)** thay vì chạy!"

    rollback:
      needs: [deploy-prod, smoke-test]
      if: failure()     # BẮT BUỘC để thức dậy khi bước trước thất bại!

    - "Điều kiện ==`if: failure()`== đánh thức job `rollback` ngay khoảnh khắc `deploy-prod` hoặc `smoke-test` thất bại"
```

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - Always use **immutable image tags (`sha-${{ github.sha }}` / `v1.4.2`)**; never overwrite `:latest` in Production.
> - **Blue-Green** uses **`activeService`** & **`previewService`** (~2x resources, instant cutover) · **Canary** shifts traffic incrementally (`5% → 25% → 100%`), where `- pause: {}` pauses indefinitely awaiting `promote`.
> - Smoke Tests must use **`curl --fail`** with **`--retry 5 --retry-delay 3`**, and a `rollback` job with `needs:` must declare **`if: failure()`**!

readings.noteEn: Multi-stage Canary release plan (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) to limit blast radius in Production.
readings.taskEn: In argo-rollouts-canary.yaml, what happens at the pause: { duration: 2m } step right after setWeight: 5?
readings.answerEn: Argo Rollouts holds exactly 5% of traffic on the new version for 2 minutes so monitoring systems (Prometheus/Datadog) can collect HTTP 5xx error rates and latency before deciding whether to expand to 25% or abort automatically.

readings.noteEn: Blue-Green strategy with an internal previewService completely isolated from customer-facing activeService.
readings.taskEn: What benefit does the autoPromotionEnabled: false flag provide for QA and E2E Automation teams?
readings.answerEn: It holds the new version (Green) in a waiting state on previewService so E2E test suites or QA can verify it on real Production infrastructure before a single live customer is routed to it.

readings.noteEn: Combining curl --fail --retry for post-deploy Smoke Tests with an automated rollback job triggered by if: failure().
readings.taskEn: What happens if you forget the --fail flag in the curl command checking /healthz and the server returns HTTP 503?
readings.answerEn: By default, curl prints the 503 error response body and exits with code 0! The pipeline will report a False Green and the rollback job will never trigger.

C14-Q1.qEn: Why does overwriting the Docker Image tag `:latest` in a Production pipeline pose a serious danger to Rollback capability?
choicesEn: Because Docker Engine v27 no longer supports pulling the :latest tag
Because `:latest` is a mutable tag: the previous stable version gets overwritten and loses its reference, and K8s Nodes may pull mismatched versions causing chaos
Because the `:latest` tag doubles the Image size
Because GitHub Container Registry charges 3x more for `:latest`
C14-Q1.explainEn: An immutable tag such as `sha-${{ github.sha }}` guarantees each build is unique, allowing you to point back to any stable version in seconds.

C14-Q2.qEn: What is the core difference between the Blue-Green and Canary deployment strategies?
choicesEn: Blue-Green only runs on VMs, whereas Canary only runs on Kubernetes

Blue-Green spins up a full parallel environment (~2x resources) and switches 100% of traffic at once after Preview verification; Canary shifts small percentages of traffic gradually (5% -> 25% -> 100%)
Canary requires 5 minutes of downtime, whereas Blue-Green has zero downtime
Blue-Green cannot roll back to the previous version
C14-Q2.explainEn: Blue-Green optimizes for testing on a Preview endpoint and instant cutover (at the cost of double cluster capacity during transition), while Canary optimizes for incremental risk exposure with live users.

C14-Q3.qEn: Which long flag (starting with --) of `curl` is mandatory in a Smoke Test step so that HTTP 500/502/503 responses produce a non-zero exit code?
C14-Q3.explainEn: Without `--fail` (or `--fail-with-body`), `curl` treats receiving an HTTP 500 response from the server as "network communication succeeded" and exits with code 0!

C14-Q4.qEn: In GitHub Actions, a fallback job with `needs: [deploy-prod, smoke-test]` will be SKIPPED by default if `smoke-test` fails — unless you explicitly declare a status check function like `if: failure()`.
C14-Q4.explainEn: By default, any job with `needs` implies `if: success()`. For the `rollback` job to run when an upstream step fails, you must explicitly specify `if: failure()`.

C14-Q5.qEn: In an Argo Rollouts `Rollout` resource (`argoproj.io/v1alpha1`), which pair of fields under `spec.strategy.blueGreen` separates live customer traffic from the internal testing endpoint?
choicesEn: publicPort and privatePort
activeService and previewService
prodIngress and testIngress
primaryPod and secondaryPod
C14-Q5.explainEn: `activeService` serves live customer traffic, while `previewService` points directly to the new ReplicaSet awaiting promotion.

C14-Q6.qEn: In an Argo Rollouts Canary configuration, a `- pause: {}` step (without `duration`) pauses traffic progression indefinitely until an operator or pipeline runs the promote command.
C14-Q6.explainEn: `pause: { duration: "2m" }` resumes automatically after 2 minutes, whereas an empty `pause: {}` acts as a manual gate waiting for explicit confirmation (`kubectl argo rollouts promote`).

C14-Q7.qEn: Why should a post-deploy Smoke Test include `--retry 5 --retry-delay 3` instead of running `curl --fail` only once?
choicesEn: To reduce CPU load on the database server
To avoid false alarms (flaky rollbacks) during the first few seconds while Ingress / Load Balancers update their new EndpointSlice routing tables
Because curl requires --retry to support HTTPS
To automatically recompile TypeScript source code on error
C14-Q7.explainEn: In distributed systems, it takes a few seconds for Load Balancers to register new Pods; controlled retries distinguish "network propagation delay" from "application actually crashed".

C14-C1.frontEn: What is the standard formula for an immutable Docker Image tag in GitHub Actions?
C14-C1.backEn: Attach the Git commit SHA: `ghcr.io/<org>/<app>:sha-${{ github.sha }}` (never just overwrite `:latest`).

C14-C2.frontEn: What are the three core properties in `spec.strategy.blueGreen` of Argo Rollouts?
C14-C2.backEn:
1) `activeService`: service receiving live traffic.
2) `previewService`: service for testing the new version before cutover.
3) `autoPromotionEnabled: false`: holds an approval gate before switching to Active.

C14-C3.frontEn: What are the two basic directives inside the `steps` array of an Argo Rollouts `canary` strategy?
C14-C3.backEn: `- setWeight: <percentage>` (e.g., 5, 25, 100) alternating with `- pause: { duration: "2m" }` to observe error metrics before increasing traffic further.

C14-C4.frontEn: What is the standard set of flags for `curl` in a Post-Deploy Smoke Test step?
C14-C4.backEn:
`curl --fail --silent --show-error --retry 5 --retry-delay 3 https://.../readyz`
(`--fail` is critical so HTTP >= 400 returns a non-zero exit code).

C14-C5.frontEn: How do you configure a `rollback` job to run automatically whenever `deploy-prod` or `smoke-test` fails in GitHub Actions?
C14-C5.backEn: Declare `needs: [deploy-prod, smoke-test]` combined with the condition `if: failure()`.

C14-C6.frontEn: Between `/healthz` (Liveness) and `/readyz` (Readiness), which endpoint best reflects whether a service is ready to handle traffic in a Smoke Test?
C14-C6.backEn: `/readyz` — because it also checks dependencies like Database/Cache connections, ensuring the app can actually serve customer requests.

cicd-ex-c14-1.titleEn: Build Docker Images with a Git SHA Immutable Tag
cicd-ex-c14-1.promptEn:
The current image build workflow uses the mutable tag `ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:latest`, making it impossible for operations to tell what code is running or roll back accurately on failure.
Update `with.tags` in the `docker/build-push-action@v6` step to the immutable tag `ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:sha-${{ github.sha }}` (removing `:latest` completely).
hintsEn: Change the `tags:` line to `ghcr.io/acme/shop-api:sha-${{ github.sha }}`.
Make sure `:latest` no longer appears anywhere in the `tags` field.

cicd-ex-c14-2.titleEn: Configure Blue-Green Deployment with Preview Gate (Argo Rollouts)
cicd-ex-c14-2.promptEn:
Complete the `Rollout` manifest (`apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1`, `kind: Rollout`) for the `shop-api` service using the **Blue-Green** strategy:
1. Set `spec.strategy.blueGreen.activeService: shop-api-active`.
2. Set `spec.strategy.blueGreen.previewService: shop-api-preview`.
3. Set `spec.strategy.blueGreen.autoPromotionEnabled: false` to hold an E2E testing gate before switching live traffic.
hintsEn: Under `spec.strategy.blueGreen:`, declare all 3 keys: `activeService`, `previewService`, and `autoPromotionEnabled`.
Note that `false` is a YAML boolean (do not wrap it in quotes as `"false"`).

cicd-ex-c14-3.promptEn:
Instead of sending 100% of customers to the new checkout release at once, configure a **Canary** strategy (`spec.strategy.canary.steps`) with exactly 4 steps in order:
1. Step 0: `setWeight: 5` (test with 5% of traffic).
2. Step 1: `pause: { duration: "2m" }` (pause for 2 minutes to monitor HTTP 5xx errors).
3. Step 2: `setWeight: 25` (increase to 25% of traffic).
4. Step 3: `setWeight: 100` (complete 100% rollout).
hintsEn: Each item in the `steps:` array begins with a hyphen `- `.
`setWeight` values (`5`, `25`, `100`) are integers, while `duration: "2m"` is a string with minute units.

cicd-ex-c14-4.titleEn: Write a Post-Deploy Smoke Test Step Preventing False Greens
cicd-ex-c14-4.promptEn:
The `Smoke Test` step below runs a bare `curl https://api.shop.example.com/readyz` — when the service fails and returns HTTP `503 Service Unavailable`, `curl` still exits with code `0`, causing a False Green pipeline!
Fix the `run` command in the second step of the `smoke-test` job so it calls `curl` on `https://api.shop.example.com/readyz` with all required flags: `--fail`, `--silent`, `--show-error`, and `--retry 5`.
hintsEn: Write out the full long flags: `curl --fail --silent --show-error --retry 5 https://api.shop.example.com/readyz`.

cicd-ex-c14-5.titleEn: Automated Rollback & Alerting on Deployment or Smoke Test Failure
cicd-ex-c14-5.promptEn:
Complete the `rollback` job at the end of the release workflow so it automatically restores the system whenever an issue occurs:
1. Declare `needs: [deploy-prod, smoke-test]` to monitor both the deployment and verification jobs.
2. Set `if: failure()` so the job only triggers when one of the upstream jobs fails.
3. Attach `environment: production` and run `./scripts/rollback-release.sh` with an alert message in the `run:` step.
hintsEn: Use the array `needs: [deploy-prod, smoke-test]` and `if: failure()` on the `rollback` job.
Don't forget to add `environment: production` so the `rollback` job has access to the target environment configuration.

C15.titleEn: Practical GitOps with Argo CD: Pull-Based Sync, Self-Heal & Sync Waves
C15.summaryEn: Eliminate the anti-pattern of granting Kubernetes Admin permissions to CI, transition to a Pull-Based GitOps architecture with ArgoCD Application, automate configuration drift prevention (selfHeal/prune), Helm valueFiles, and orchestrate deployment order using Sync Waves.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
In previous lessons, when deploying applications to a Kubernetes cluster, the common initial model was **Push-based CD**: GitHub Actions or GitLab Runner servers held K8s cluster admin credentials (`KUBECONFIG` / Cloud Admin Role), and then externally ran `kubectl set image` or `helm upgrade` against the Production cluster.

The **Push-based CD** model is easy to set up for a small service, but as the system scales to dozens of microservices alongside security audit requirements (*PCI-DSS, SOC2*), it exposes many risks. The ==Pull-based GitOps== architecture with **Argo CD** (or **Flux CD**) and a **Single Source of Truth in Git** thoroughly resolves these risks.

```visual
caption: "Luồng khép kín từ CI đẩy Image & cập nhật thẻ phiên bản vào kho GitOps Config tới ArgoCD phát hiện sai lệch (Drift) và tự đồng bộ 24/7"
```

steps.headingEn: Why Is Push-based kubectl apply from CI a Security Anti-Pattern?
steps.bodyEn:
The core difference between the two models lies in where administrative privileges are held and the direction of the connection:
- **Push-based CD:** The CI Runner located outside the cluster must store a high-privilege `KUBECONFIG` and actively connect to the Production cluster's API Server to push changes.
- **Pull-based GitOps:** The controller (**ArgoCD Controller**) is installed directly **inside the Kubernetes cluster**, actively pulling configuration state from the Git repository (*Single Source of Truth*) to reconcile and continuously auto-sync 24/7. *(Instead of granting remote admin credentials to an external server to log into the Production server, the coordinator living inside the cluster automatically reconciles and updates according to the canonical configuration in Git).*

```visual
kind: layers

subtitle: Đảo ngược chiều kết nối để xoá bỏ hoàn toàn chìa khoá K8s Admin nằm phơi trên CI Pipeline bên ngoài

    badge: Chuẩn vàng Cloud-Native · Zero-Trust
    tone: emerald

        note: Không mở API Server ra Internet

        note: Đồng bộ liên tục 24/7
        tone: cyan
    footer: Toàn bộ lịch sử hạ tầng nằm gọn trong git log · Rollback chuẩn là git revert!
```

> [!TIP] Choosing a GitOps Tool: **Argo CD** or **Flux CD**?
> Both are popular **CNCF Graduated** projects operating on the **Pull-based GitOps** model, but they serve two different usage needs:
> - **Argo CD:** Stands out with an **extremely intuitive graphical Web UI resource tree**, built-in centralized multi-cluster SSO/RBAC permissions, and seamless pairing with *Argo Rollouts* — the #1 choice when you want every Developer to visually inspect the health of their own Pods.
> - **Flux CD:** Designed as lightweight, pure Kubernetes CRD microservice controllers (*GitOps Toolkit*), without the heavy Web UI layer, excelling at automating Helm/Kustomize/Image synchronization via CLI & Terraform across hundreds of edge clusters (*Fleet / Edge Clusters*).

steps.headingEn: Separating 2 Repositories: App Repo vs GitOps Config Repo
steps.bodyEn:
In a standard GitOps architecture, we separate the **Application Source Repository (`shop-api`)** from the **Deployment Config Repository (`shop-gitops`)** (containing Kustomize overlays or Helm values for `dev`, `staging`, `prod`):

- [x] **Avoid infinite CI loops:** If CI modifies YAML files directly inside `shop-api` and runs `git push`, that very commit would re-trigger the entire application lint/test/build pipeline!
- [x] **Clear separation of duties:** Developers merge feature code into `shop-api`, while only the CI Bot and SRE/Platform team have write access to the `main` branch of `shop-gitops`.

steps.headingEn: Structure of the ArgoCD Application Object (argoproj.io/v1alpha1)
steps.bodyEn:
Inside the Kubernetes cluster, you define the link between the `shop-gitops` repository and the target cluster through the Custom Resource `kind: Application`:

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: shop-api-prod
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: default
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/acme/shop-gitops.git
    targetRevision: main
    path: overlays/prod
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: production
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true       # Xoá tài nguyên trên K8s nếu file YAML tương ứng đã bị xoá khỏi Git
      selfHeal: true    # Tự động khôi phục về chuẩn Git nếu ai đó sửa tay trực tiếp trên cụm!
    syncOptions:
      - CreateNamespace=true
```

If your team uses a **Helm Chart** instead of Kustomize, the `spec.source` block specifies environment-specific override files via the ==`helm.valueFiles`== field:

```yaml
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/acme/shop-gitops.git
    targetRevision: main
    path: charts/shop-api
    helm:
      valueFiles:
        - values-prod.yaml
```

```visual

title: Các tham số cấu hình quan trọng trong ArgoCD Application
subtitle: Nắm chắc sự khác biệt giữa prune, selfHeal, CreateNamespace và sóng đồng bộ sync-wave

      - "Nếu để `prune: false`, các `CronJob` hay `ConfigMap` cũ đã xoá trên Git vẫn sống dai dẳng như \"bóng ma\" trên cụm!"
    example: "prune: true"

  - keyword: "automated.selfHeal: true"
    role: Chống trôi dạt cấu hình
    tone: emerald
    summary: Giám sát các tài nguyên đang quản lý và tự động ghi đè về chuẩn Git nếu ai đó gõ tay `kubectl edit` / `scale` trên cụm.
    bullets:
      - "Nhờ `selfHeal: true`, thao tác Rollback chuẩn trong GitOps bắt buộc là ==`git revert`== trên kho GitOps (chứ không phải gõ tay `kubectl set image`!)"
    example: "selfHeal: true"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: "CreateNamespace=true"
    role: Tự khởi tạo Namespace đích
    tone: sky
    summary: Tuỳ chọn nằm trong mảng `spec.syncPolicy.syncOptions` cho phép ArgoCD tự tạo `destination.namespace` ở lần đồng bộ đầu tiên.
    bullets:
      - "Tránh lỗi đồng bộ thất bại do Namespace `production` chưa được tạo sẵn bằng tay"
    example: "syncOptions:\n  - CreateNamespace=true"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: "spec.source.helm.valueFiles"
    role: Ghi đè cấu hình Helm Chart
    tone: cyan
    summary: Tương đương cờ `-f values-prod.yaml` của Helm CLI khi `spec.source.path` trỏ vào thư mục chứa Helm Chart.
    bullets:
      - "Cho phép dùng chung 1 Chart gốc cho cả `values-staging.yaml` và `values-prod.yaml`"
    example: "helm:\n  valueFiles:\n    - values-prod.yaml"
    lang: yaml
  - keyword: "argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave"
    role: Điều phối thứ tự sóng triển khai
    tone: cyan
    summary: Annotation nhận chuỗi số nguyên (mặc định `\"0\"`), thực thi tuần tự từ **số âm nhỏ nhất tăng dần lên số dương**.
    bullets:
      - "ArgoCD **đợi tất cả tài nguyên ở Wave nhỏ hơn đạt `Healthy` / `Succeeded`** rồi mới áp dụng Wave lớn hơn!"
    example: "metadata:\n  annotations:\n    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: \"-1\""
    lang: yaml
```
