steps.headingEn: Orchestrating Deployment Order with Sync Waves (argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave)
steps.bodyEn:
When ArgoCD syncs an entire directory containing dozens of YAML files, what happens if the new application `Deployment` starts **before** the database upgrade `Job` (`db-migrate`) finishes adding a new column to PostgreSQL? The application Pods will crash simultaneously due to SQL query errors!

The ==`argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave`== annotation cleanly solves multi-tier dependency ordering without needing bash scripts in CI:
- [>] **Wave `"-2"`**: Foundational `Namespace`, `ServiceAccount`, `ConfigMap`.
- [>] **Wave `"-1"`**: Kubernetes `Job` running `db-migrate` (for example `npx prisma migrate deploy` for the backward-compatible Expand phase) — ArgoCD waits for this Job to report **`Succeeded`** completely!
- [>] **Wave `"0"` (default)**: `Deployment` `shop-api` and `Service` begin rolling out safely.
- [>] **Wave `"1"`**: `Ingress` or post-deployment verification Job after the service is `Healthy`.

```visual
kind: troubleshoot
title: Các lỗi vận hành GitOps & ArgoCD thường gặp
items:
  - symptom: "Gõ tay kubectl set image để Rollback khẩn cấp nhưng 5 giây sau Pod lại tự quay về bản lỗi!"
    badge: Cơ chế selfHeal
    tone: rose
    cause: "Ứng dụng đang bật syncPolicy.automated.selfHeal: true nên ArgoCD coi thao tác sửa tay trên cụm là Configuration Drift và lập tức ghi đè lại theo kho Git."
    fix: "Trong mô hình GitOps, mọi thao tác Rollback phải thực hiện bằng git revert commit cập nhật tag ảnh trên kho cấu hình GitOps."
    cmd: "git revert HEAD && git push origin main"
  - symptom: "Đã xoá tệp cronjob-cleanup.yaml trên kho Git nhưng CronJob vẫn tiếp tục chạy mỗi đêm trên K8s"
    badge: Thiếu prune
    tone: amber
    cause: "Cờ automated.prune đang để mặc định false nên ArgoCD không xoá tài nguyên cũ khỏi cụm."
    fix: "Bật tường minh prune: true bên dưới spec.syncPolicy.automated."
    cmd: "automated:\n  prune: true\n  selfHeal: true"
```

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **Pull-based GitOps (ArgoCD)** places the deployment agent **inside the K8s cluster**, completely eliminating the need to store `KUBECONFIG` in CI.
> - Enable the pair **`prune: true`** (deletes orphaned resources removed from Git) + **`selfHeal: true`** (auto-recovers when someone makes manual edits on the cluster) and **`CreateNamespace=true`** in `syncOptions`.
> - Standard GitOps rollback is **`git revert`** on the GitOps repo · Use **`argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "-1"`** to force the DB migrate Job to reach `Succeeded` before the Deployment in wave `"0"`.

readings.noteEn: Standard ArgoCD Application object declaration for the Production environment with both prune and selfHeal enabled.
readings.taskEn: If an operations engineer accidentally types kubectl edit deployment on the Production cluster, which flag in argocd-application-prod.yaml will automatically restore the canonical state from Git?
readings.answerEn: The syncPolicy.automated.selfHeal: true flag enables ArgoCD to detect drift between the live cluster and Git, and automatically sync back to match the exact declaration in the GitOps repository.

readings.noteEn: The CI workflow of the application source repository only packages the Image and pushes a commit updating the new tag to the GitOps repository.
readings.taskEn: Why should the infrastructure configuration repository (shop-gitops) be separated from the application source repository (shop-api)?
readings.answerEn: Separating them ensures that image tag update commits from the CI Bot do not trigger an infinite loop of application tests/builds, while also cleanly separating code merge permissions from Production infrastructure modification permissions.

readings.noteEn: Dangerous security anti-pattern: stuffing cluster-admin kubeconfig into a CI secret variable to push kubectl commands directly from outside.
readings.taskEn: What happens if an npm dependency is compromised with malware during a build on a runner that holds KUBE_CONFIG_ADMIN?
readings.answerEn: If the install or build step can read KUBE_CONFIG_ADMIN and the API Server is externally reachable, the attacker gains full superuser administrative control over the entire Production Kubernetes cluster!

C15-Q1.qEn: What is the most important architectural difference between Pull-Based GitOps (ArgoCD) and Push-Based CD (`kubectl apply` in GitHub Actions)?
choicesEn: ArgoCD rewrites Node.js source code into Go
The deployment agent (ArgoCD) resides INSIDE the Kubernetes cluster and actively pulls state from Git to reconcile, so external CI never needs to hold K8s cluster admin credentials
Pull-Based GitOps no longer requires a Container Registry
Pull-Based GitOps allows direct manual edits on the server without saving them to Git
C15-Q1.explainEn: Keeping administrative privileges inside the cluster and treating Git as the Single Source of Truth seals off the attack surface from external CI Pipelines.

C15-Q2.qEn: In `syncPolicy.automated` of an ArgoCD `Application`, what happens if you enable `selfHeal: true` but leave `prune: false`?
choicesEn: ArgoCD cannot create any new Deployments
When you delete an old resource YAML file in the Git repository, that resource continues to linger on the Kubernetes cluster instead of being cleaned up automatically
ArgoCD will delete the entire Namespace every night
The Helm Chart will fail to read the values-prod.yaml file
C15-Q2.explainEn: `selfHeal` fixes drift on currently managed resources, whereas `prune: true` is responsible for deleting resources on the cluster once their definition files have been removed from Git.

C15-Q3.qEn: Enter the ArgoCD annotation name (including its domain prefix) used to specify the sync wave order (e.g., running a migrate Job at step "-1" before a Deployment at step "0"):
C15-Q3.explainEn: The `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave` annotation accepts an integer string (negative runs earlier, positive runs later; default is "0") to orchestrate conditional deployment order.

C15-Q4.qEn: When using Sync Waves, ArgoCD by default waits for all resources in a lower Wave (e.g., a Job in wave "-1") to reach Healthy / Succeeded status before starting to apply resources in a higher Wave (e.g., a Deployment in wave "0").
C15-Q4.explainEn: This is precisely why Sync Waves are exceptionally safe for database upgrade scenarios before launching a new application version.

C15-Q5.qEn: In an ArgoCD `Application` object, if `spec.source.path` points to a directory containing a Helm Chart (`charts/shop-api`), which field specifies the override values file for the Production environment?
choicesEn: spec.source.kustomize.patches
spec.source.helm.valueFiles
spec.destination.values
metadata.labels.helmValues
C15-Q5.explainEn: `spec.source.helm.valueFiles` takes a list of values files (e.g., `["values-prod.yaml"]`), similar to the `-f values-prod.yaml` flag in the Helm CLI.

C15-Q6.qEn: To roll back a faulty release in a GitOps model with `automated` sync enabled, the most standard operation is running `kubectl set image` directly against the Production cluster while leaving Git untouched.
C15-Q6.explainEn: If you make manual edits with `kubectl` on a cluster with `selfHeal: true`, ArgoCD will immediately overwrite them back to the broken version in Git! The standard GitOps rollback is `git revert` on the image-tag update commit in the GitOps repo.

C15-Q7.qEn: Which option in the `spec.syncPolicy.syncOptions` array allows ArgoCD to automatically create the target Namespace (e.g., `production`) if it does not already exist on the cluster?
choicesEn: AutoNamespace=enabled
CreateNamespace=true
MakeNamespace=yes
InitTargetNamespace=1
C15-Q7.explainEn: Adding `"CreateNamespace=true"` to `syncOptions` allows ArgoCD to automatically create `spec.destination.namespace` during the initial sync.

C15-C1.frontEn: Why should `KUBE_CONFIG_ADMIN` not be stored in GitHub Actions of the application source repository?
C15-C1.backEn: Because if CI is compromised or pulls a malicious npm package, attackers gain full control of the K8s cluster; furthermore, direct pushes from CI cannot detect and self-heal configuration drift.

C15-C2.frontEn: At which step does CI's responsibility stop in a Pull-Based GitOps model?
C15-C2.backEn: Run Tests/Scans -> Build & Push Image with an immutable tag (`sha-...`) -> Commit the updated Image tag to the GitOps repo (`kustomize edit set image` + `git push`). Applying changes to K8s is handled by ArgoCD.

C15-C3.frontEn: What is the meaning of the `prune: true` and `selfHeal: true` pair in an ArgoCD `Application`?
C15-C3.backEn:
- `prune: true`: automatically deletes leftover resources on K8s when their YAML files are removed from Git.
- `selfHeal: true`: automatically restores the canonical state from Git if someone edits resources manually on the cluster.

C15-C4.frontEn: How does the execution order of `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave` work?
C15-C4.backEn: From the smallest integer to the largest (`"-2"` -> `"-1"` -> `"0"` -> `"1"`), advancing to the next wave only once all resources in the current wave are Healthy.

C15-C5.frontEn: How do you specify the `values-prod.yaml` file when deploying a Helm Chart with an ArgoCD `Application`?

C15-C6.frontEn: What is the standard way to roll back in a GitOps workflow?
C15-C6.backEn: Run `git revert` on the version upgrade commit in the GitOps repository and push to `main` — this both triggers ArgoCD to automatically roll back and preserves a complete audit trail in Git.

C15-C7.frontEn: Compare the core strengths of the two leading CNCF GitOps tools: **Argo CD** vs **Flux CD**?
C15-C7.backEn:
- **Argo CD**: excels in an intuitive resource-tree Web UI, centralized multi-cluster SSO permissions, and integration with *Argo Rollouts*.
- **Flux CD**: lightweight pure Kubernetes CRD microservice architecture without a heavy Web UI, optimized for CLI/Terraform automation across hundreds of edge clusters.

cicd-ex-c15-1.titleEn: Remove Admin kubectl from CI — Switch to Updating the GitOps Repo
cicd-ex-c15-1.promptEn:
The workflow below suffers from a critical security anti-pattern: loading `KUBE_CONFIG_ADMIN` and running `kubectl apply` directly from the app repo's CI!

cicd-ex-c15-3.promptEn:

cicd-ex-c15-4.titleEn: Integrate a Helm Chart with values-prod.yaml in ArgoCD Application
cicd-ex-c15-4.promptEn:
The payments team packages their service using a **Helm Chart** located at `charts/payment-service` in the GitOps repo. Without specifying an override file, ArgoCD only reads the default `values.yaml` (configured for dev)!
Configure `spec.source.path: charts/payment-service` and set `spec.source.helm.valueFiles` to an array containing `"values-prod.yaml"`.

cicd-ex-c15-5.titleEn: Order DB Migrate Job Before Deployment Using Sync Waves
cicd-ex-c15-5.promptEn:
The multi-document YAML file (`---`) below contains a Kubernetes `Job` (`db-migrate`) and a `Deployment` (`shop-api`). Currently both run concurrently, causing the new `shop-api` Pods to start before the new SQL columns are created!
Add the `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave` annotation to `metadata.annotations` of both resources:
1. On `Job` `db-migrate`: set `"argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave": "-1"` so it runs and finishes first.
2. On `Deployment` `shop-api`: set `"argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave": "0"` so new Pods only roll out after the Job in wave `-1` has succeeded.
hintsEn: Values in Kubernetes `metadata.annotations` must be strings (wrapped in double quotes `"-1"` and `"0"`); unquoted integers will be rejected by the K8s API!
Double-check the exact key name: `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave`.

C16.titleEn: Zero-Downtime DB Migration (Expand-Contract), Monorepo CI & DORA Metrics
C16.summaryEn: Design zero-downtime database migration workflows (Expand-and-Contract), optimize Monorepo CI to run only affected packages using Paths Filter / Turborepo, and measure the 4 DORA metrics.

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
When an application is still in an MVP stage with few users at midnight, you can directly run a SQL column rename, wait for all 12 packages in the repository to rebuild from scratch, and gauge productivity by gut feeling. But when stepping up to **Large-Scale System Architecture** — serving tens of thousands of concurrent transactions in a Monorepo with 8 engineering teams pushing hundreds of PRs daily — three major challenges emerge:

- [>] **Zero-Downtime DB Migration:** How do you alter a SQL schema without crashing old-version Pods (`v1`) running alongside new Pods (`v2`) during a Rolling Update?
- [>] **Smart Monorepo CI:** How do you run Lint/Test/Build only for affected services (including transitive dependents) instead of burning CI budget needlessly?
- [>] **Engineering Telemetry:** How do you measure pipeline health objectively using the **4 industry-standard DORA metrics**?


steps.headingEn: Risks of Renaming or Dropping SQL Columns & the 3-Phase Expand-and-Contract Pattern
steps.bodyEn:
Consider a common Production incident: a developer renames column `full_name` to `display_name` (or `total` to `grand_total`), creates a migration file `ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN full_name TO display_name;`, and pushes straight to `main`.

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Thay Đổi Lược Đồ SQL Trong Lúc Rolling Update: Phá Huỷ Tức Thì vs Tương Thích Ngược"
subtitle: "Tại thời điểm chuyển giao Zero-Downtime, luôn tồn tại đồng thời cả Pod v1 và Pod v2 cùng truy vấn vào 1 Database duy nhất!"
left:
  badge: "GÂY DOWNTIME · Phá vỡ tương thích ngược"
  title: "Chạy RENAME COLUMN / DROP COLUMN trực tiếp"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    -- Phút 00:00: Chạy xong trên PostgreSQL trong 50ms!
    ALTER TABLE users
      RENAME COLUMN full_name TO display_name;

    -- Phút 00:01 -> 00:45 (Đang Rolling Update 10 Pod):
    -- Các Pod v1 cũ vẫn đang sống và gọi:
    SELECT id, full_name FROM users;
    -- -> Gây lỗi HTTP 500 trên toàn bộ Pod v1!
  lang: sql
  bullets:
    - "Trong 45 giây cuộn Pod từ `v1` sang `v2`, mọi Pod `v1` đang phục vụ khách hàng lập tức sập vì `column \"full_name\" does not exist`!"
    - "**Mất đường lui:** Nếu code `v2` dính lỗi logic và bạn bấm **Rollback** về `v1`, bản `v1` cũng chết cứng vì Database đã bị biến dạng!"
right:
  badge: "CHUẨN ZERO-DOWNTIME · An toàn 100%"
  title: "Mở rộng trước (Expand) + Nối chặt DAG needs: [migrate]"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    -- Pha 1 (Expand): Chỉ THÊM cột cho phép NULL
    ALTER TABLE users
      ADD COLUMN display_name TEXT NULL;

    # Trong Workflow YAML — Cấm chạy song song migrate & deploy!
    deploy-app:
      needs: [migrate]   # Đợi thêm cột xong mới bật Pod mới!
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Pod `v1` cũ vẫn đọc/ghi cột `full_name` bình thường như chưa có chuyện gì xảy ra; Rollback bất cứ giây nào cũng an toàn"
    - "Bắt buộc cấu hình ==`needs: [migrate]`== trên `deploy-app` và đặt **SQL Migration Linter** (`grep -E -i \"DROP COLUMN|RENAME COLUMN\"` / `squawk`) chặn lệnh phá huỷ!"
```

The only standard solution is splitting a breaking change into ==3 independent releases (Expand → Switch Read → Contract)== — think of it as **building a new bridge parallel to the old bridge while traffic (`Pod v1`) is still flowing**: you must finish the new bridge, smoothly route 100% of traffic onto the new bridge, and only in the final release dismantle the old bridge!

```visual
kind: flow
title: Quy Trình Di Trú Cơ Sở Dữ Liệu 3 Pha Expand-and-Contract (Zero-Downtime)
subtitle: Đổi tên cột full_name sang display_name êm ái mà không làm rớt bất kỳ giao dịch nào của khách hàng
steps:
  - icon: database
    badge: Pha 1 · Mở rộng
    title: Expand & Dual-Write
    desc: Thêm cột display_name NULL; code v1.1 ghi đồng thời 2 cột + chạy Backfill dữ liệu cũ
    code: "ADD COLUMN ... NULL"
    tone: sky
    edge: 100% dữ liệu đồng bộ
  - icon: refresh
    badge: Pha 2 · Chuyển đọc
    title: Switch Read (v1.2)
    desc: Code v1.2 chuyển hẳn sang đọc/ghi display_name; ngừng chạm vào cột full_name
    code: "SELECT display_name"
    tone: amber
    edge: hết sạch Pod cũ
  - icon: trash
    badge: Pha 3 · Thu hẹp
    title: Contract (Cleanup)
    desc: Chỉ sau khi 100% Pod chạy ổn định trên cột mới mới phát hành lệnh xoá cột cũ
    code: "DROP COLUMN full_name"
    tone: emerald
```

steps.headingEn: Optimizing Monorepo CI: Path Filtering & Turborepo Dependency Graph
steps.bodyEn:
In a Monorepo containing `apps/web`, `apps/payment-api`, `apps/notification`, and a shared package `packages/shared-dto`, re-running all 4 services when a developer edits 1 line of CSS in `apps/web` wastes 75% of CI cost. There are two levels of smart filtering:

### Level 1: Directory Path Filtering with `dorny/paths-filter@v3`
A lightweight `filters` job runs first (~3 seconds) to detect changed directories. An important note in GitHub Actions: all `outputs` passed between jobs are always **strings (`'true'` or `'false'`)**, so the standard conditional expression is:
`if: needs.filters.outputs.payment == 'true'`

### Level 2: Package Dependency Graph Filtering with `Turborepo --filter`
If a PR modifies a foundational package `packages/shared-dto` (or `packages/shared-utils`), simple directory path filtering can easily miss that `apps/payment-api` imports it! **Turborepo** solves this thoroughly by reading the `package.json` dependency tree combined with Git history (requiring ==`fetch-depth: 0`== on checkout!) via the ==`--filter=...[origin/main]`== syntax:

```visual
kind: flow
title: "Cơ Chế Lọc Thông Minh Theo Đồ Thị Phụ Thuộc Của Turborepo (--filter=...[origin/main])"
subtitle: "Ba dấu chấm '...' phía trước đảm bảo kiểm thử cả gói vừa sửa LẪN mọi ứng dụng cha phụ thuộc ngược vào nó!"
steps:
  - icon: folder-git
    badge: Bắt buộc đủ lịch sử
    title: "checkout (fetch-depth: 0)"
    desc: Tải trọn vẹn lịch sử Git để có nhánh tham chiếu origin/main tính toán diff
    code: "fetch-depth: 0"
    tone: amber
    edge: sửa gói dùng chung
  - icon: package
    badge: Gói trực tiếp đổi
    title: packages/shared-dto
    desc: Lập trình viên thay đổi kiểu dữ liệu DTO trong thư viện nội bộ
    code: "changed vs origin/main"
    tone: sky
    edge: truy vết "..." dependents
  - icon: boxes
    badge: Tự động kéo theo
    title: payment-api & web
    desc: Turborepo chạy lint/test/build cho cả 2 app có import shared-dto; bỏ qua notification!
    code: "--filter=...[origin/main]"
    tone: emerald
```

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0   # BẮT BUỘC: mặc định là 1 (shallow clone) sẽ không thấy origin/main!
- run: npx turbo run lint test build --filter=...[origin/main]
```

steps.headingEn: Measuring Engineering Performance with the 4 DORA Metrics (Four Keys)
steps.bodyEn:
How do you know whether a team is shipping quickly in a sustainable way rather than rushing speed at the cost of constant outages? The **DORA (*DevOps Research and Assessment*)** research program provides ==4 industry-standard metrics (Four Keys)== — balancing **2 Throughput metrics** and **2 Stability metrics**:

```visual
kind: groups
title: "Bộ 4 Chỉ Số Chuẩn Công Nghiệp DORA (\"Four Keys\") [!badge:emerald:Elite Benchmarks]"
subtitle: Hai chỉ số đầu đo Tốc độ giao nhận (Throughput) · Hai chỉ số sau đo Chất lượng & Khả năng phục hồi (Stability)
columns: 2
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: rocket
    title: Deployment Frequency
    badge: Tốc độ · Tần suất phát hành
    tone: sky
    desc: Đội ngũ đưa mã nguồn lên Production thành công bao lâu một lần?
    bullets:
      - "**Nhóm Elite:** Phát hành theo yêu cầu — **nhiều lần mỗi ngày**"
      - "Phản ánh kích thước lô thay đổi (*batch size*) nhỏ gọn và tự động hoá CI/CD mượt mà"
  - num: 2
    icon: zap
    title: Lead Time for Changes
    badge: Tốc độ · Thời gian dẫn
    tone: cyan
    desc: Mất bao lâu tính từ lúc lập trình viên tạo Commit cho tới khi chạy thực tế trên Production?
    bullets:
      - "**Nhóm Elite:** **Dưới 1 giờ**"
      - "Phản ánh tốc độ pipeline kiểm thử song song, rà soát PR nhanh và không bị tắc nghẽn duyệt tay"
  - num: 3
    icon: shield-alert
    title: Change Failure Rate (CFR)
    badge: Ổn định · Tỷ lệ phát hành lỗi
    tone: amber
    desc: Bao nhiêu phần trăm các đợt phát hành lên Production gây suy giảm dịch vụ cần Hotfix hoặc Rollback?
    bullets:
      - "**Nhóm Elite:** Chỉ từ **`0% – 5%`**"
      - "Được kéo giảm mạnh nhờ 5-Layer DevSecOps, Smoke Test và Expand-and-Contract DB"
  - num: 4
    icon: rollback
    title: Mean Time to Restore (MTTR)
    badge: Ổn định · Thời gian khôi phục
    tone: emerald
    desc: Khi sự cố nổ ra trên Production, mất trung bình bao lâu để khôi phục dịch vụ bình thường?
    bullets:
      - "**Nhóm Elite:** **Dưới 1 giờ** (thậm chí dưới 1 phút nhờ Canary + Auto-Rollback / `git revert`!)"
      - "Còn gọi là *Failed Deployment Recovery Time* trong các báo cáo DORA mới nhất"
```

Right after the `deploy-prod` job succeeds (`needs: [deploy-prod]`, `if: success()`), a lightweight `dora-metrics` job recording `commit_sha`, timestamp `deployed_at`, and `environment: production` turns the CI/CD Pipeline itself into the most accurate source of truth for continuous engineering improvement!

> [!REMEMBER] Key Takeaways
> - **3-Phase Expand-and-Contract:** Only execute **`DROP COLUMN`** in **Phase 3 (Contract)** after data is fully backfilled and 100% of Pods have switched to the new column; the `deploy-app` job must always have **`needs: [migrate]`**.
> - **Monorepo Turborepo:** Set **`fetch-depth: 0`** on checkout and use **`--filter=...[origin/main]`** (the leading `...` includes upstream dependent packages). Outputs from `dorny/paths-filter` must always be compared as strings: `== 'true'`.
> - **4 DORA Metrics:** **Deployment Frequency** + **Lead Time for Changes** (Throughput) and **Change Failure Rate (CFR)** + **Mean Time to Restore (MTTR)** (Stability).

readings.noteEn: Automated gate to detect and reject backward-incompatible SQL statements during Phase 1 (Expand).
readings.taskEn: Why is ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN phone_number TEXT NULL completely safe for v1 Pods running concurrently?
readings.answerEn: Because the new column allows NULL, existing INSERT/SELECT statements from v1 Pods that do not reference phone_number continue executing normally without constraint errors.

readings.noteEn: Common misconfiguration: running RENAME/DROP COLUMN immediately before updating new Pods, causing old Pods to return HTTP 500 errors.
readings.taskEn: Beyond crashing v1 Pods during a Rolling Update, what recovery capability does running DROP COLUMN immediately destroy?
readings.answerEn: It destroys Rollback capability! If v2 code has a critical logic bug requiring an emergency rollback to v1, the old column has already been deleted, making it impossible for v1 to run again.

readings.noteEn: Optimizing a Monorepo pipeline using fetch-depth: 0 combined with Turborepo's dependency graph filter.
readings.taskEn: What happens if fetch-depth: 0 is omitted from the actions/checkout@v4 step when running turbo --filter=...[origin/main]?
readings.answerEn: By default, actions/checkout@v4 performs a shallow clone of only the last 1 commit (fetch-depth: 1), so Git lacks the origin/main branch history and Turborepo either fails to compute the diff or is forced to run the entire repository!

C16-Q1.qEn: Why does running `ALTER TABLE orders RENAME COLUMN total TO grand_total;` right before a Kubernetes Rolling Update cause service downtime?
choicesEn: Because PostgreSQL does not support RENAME COLUMN inside containers
Because during the Rolling Update, old-version Pods (v1) are still running concurrently and querying the old `total` column, causing widespread SQL 500 errors and breaking Rollback to v1
Because Kubernetes automatically deletes the table when it sees ALTER TABLE
Because RENAME COLUMN fills up the GitHub Runner's disk
C16-Q1.explainEn: In a Zero-Downtime environment, during the transition window both v1 and v2 code coexist talking to a single Database — so the DB schema must remain compatible with both!

C16-Q2.qEn: In the **Expand-and-Contract** migration pattern to rename `full_name` to `display_name`, at which stage is `DROP COLUMN full_name` allowed to run?
choicesEn: Right in Phase 1 before deploying any new code
In Phase 3 (Contract), only after data has been fully backfilled AND 100% of Production Pods have stably switched to reading/writing `display_name` (no process touches `full_name` anymore)
Concurrently alongside ADD COLUMN inside one large transaction
Manually directly on a developer's local machine
C16-Q2.explainEn: Separating the Expand and Contract phases into independent releases guarantees continuous backward compatibility and safe Rollback at every step.

C16-Q3.qEn: When using `actions/checkout@v4` for `npx turbo run test --filter=...[origin/main]`, what integer should `fetch-depth` be set to in order to fetch full Git history for branch comparison?
C16-Q3.explainEn: `fetch-depth: 0` fetches the full commit history and branch refs instead of the default 1-commit shallow clone (`fetch-depth: 1`).

C16-Q4.qEn: In Turborepo, how does `--filter=...[origin/main]` (with the leading ellipsis `...`) differ from `--filter=[origin/main]`?
choicesEn: It only runs changed Markdown files
It selects packages directly changed compared to `origin/main` PLUS all packages that depend on them (dependents) in the workspace graph
It skips TypeScript type-checking
It clears the cache before running
C16-Q4.explainEn: If `packages/shared-utils` changes, the leading `...` ensures `apps/payment-api` and `apps/web` (which import `shared-utils`) are also re-tested to prevent integration breakage!

C16-Q5.qEn: Which is the accurate list of the **4 DORA Metrics (Four Keys)** used to measure software delivery performance?
choicesEn: Lines of Code (LOC), PRs per Week, Unit Test Coverage (%), Sprint Meeting Hours
Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes, Change Failure Rate (CFR), and Mean Time to Restore / Failed Deployment Recovery Time (MTTR)
CPU Usage, RAM Usage, Disk IOPS, and Network Bandwidth
GitHub Stars, Number of Git Branches, Docker Image Size, and CI Minutes
C16-Q5.explainEn: The first two metrics (Deployment Frequency, Lead Time) measure Throughput, while the latter two (Change Failure Rate, MTTR) measure Stability.

C16-Q6.qEn: When using `dorny/paths-filter@v3` to detect directory changes in a `filters` job, the output values `needs.filters.outputs.<name>` in GitHub Actions `if:` expressions are always strings (`'true'` or `'false'`).
C16-Q6.explainEn: All job outputs in GitHub Actions are passed as strings, so the most accurate comparison is `== 'true'`.

C16-Q7.qEn: To save waiting time, the `migrate` job (adding a new column to the DB) and the `deploy-app` job (starting Pods that read that new column) should run in parallel without a `needs` dependency.
C16-Q7.explainEn: If they run in parallel and `deploy-app` finishes before `migrate` adds the new column, the new application will query a non-existent column and crash immediately! `deploy-app` must declare `needs: [migrate]`.

C16-C1.frontEn: What are the three phases of the zero-downtime **Expand-and-Contract** database migration workflow?
C16-C1.backEn:
1) **Expand**: Add backward-compatible new column/table (`NULL` or with default), Dual-Write + Backfill.
2) **Switch**: Switch code to read completely from the new column.
3) **Contract**: Drop the old column (`DROP COLUMN`) in a separate release once no old Pods remain running.

C16-C2.frontEn: Which SQL statements should be automatically blocked by the CI Linter in standard release flows?
C16-C2.backEn: `DROP COLUMN`, `DROP TABLE`, `RENAME COLUMN` (or `ALTER COLUMN ... SET NOT NULL` on large tables without a safe default value).

C16-C3.frontEn: What configuration pair runs only affected packages in a Monorepo using Turborepo in GitHub Actions?
C16-C3.backEn:
1) `actions/checkout@v4` with `with: { fetch-depth: 0 }`.
2) `npx turbo run lint test build --filter=...[origin/main]`.

C16-C4.frontEn: What are the 2 Throughput metrics among the 4 DORA metrics?
C16-C4.backEn:
1) **Deployment Frequency**: How often deployments to Production succeed.
2) **Lead Time for Changes**: Time from code commit to running in Production.

C16-C5.frontEn: What are the 2 Stability metrics among the 4 DORA metrics?
C16-C5.backEn:
1) **Change Failure Rate (CFR)**: Percentage of releases causing a failure that requires rollback/hotfix.
2) **Mean Time to Restore (MTTR)**: Average time to restore service after an incident.

C16-C6.frontEn: How do you configure the `test-payment` job to run only when the `filters` job reports changes in the `payment` directory?
C16-C6.backEn: Declare `needs: filters` and the condition `if: needs.filters.outputs.payment == 'true'`.

cicd-ex-c16-1.promptEn:
The release workflow below has 2 dangerous architectural flaws: (1) It allows running any SQL file directly, including destructive `DROP COLUMN` / `RENAME COLUMN` statements, and (2) The `deploy-app` job runs in parallel with `migrate`!
Fix both:
1. In the first step after `checkout` inside the `migrate` job, use `grep -E -i "DROP COLUMN|RENAME COLUMN" db/migrations/*.sql` to block and `exit 1` if any backward-incompatible statement is detected, before running `npm run migrate:deploy`.
2. On the `deploy-app` job, add `needs: [migrate]` so new Pods only roll out after the DB Expand phase finishes.
hintsEn: In the `Block destructive SQL in Expand phase` step, use the command `if grep -E -i "DROP COLUMN|RENAME COLUMN" db/migrations/*.sql; then exit 1; fi`.
Add `needs: [migrate]` directly under `deploy-app:`.

cicd-ex-c16-2.titleEn: Selective Execution in a Monorepo with dorny/paths-filter
cicd-ex-c16-2.promptEn:
The Monorepo has two independent services `apps/payment` and `apps/web`. The `filters` job already uses `dorny/paths-filter@v3` to detect changes, but forgot to export job-level `outputs`, and `test-payment` still runs blindly on every PR!
Complete the workflow:
1. Declare `jobs.filters.outputs.payment: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.payment }}`.
2. On the `test-payment` job, add `needs: filters` and the condition `if: needs.filters.outputs.payment == 'true'`.
hintsEn: Add an `outputs:\n  payment: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.payment }}` block inside the `filters` job.
In `test-payment`, declare `needs: filters` and `if: needs.filters.outputs.payment == 'true'`.

cicd-ex-c16-3.titleEn: Optimize Monorepo Dependency Graph with Turborepo Affected Filter
cicd-ex-c16-3.promptEn:
The Turborepo Monorepo workflow currently has 2 issues: (1) `actions/checkout@v4` lacks `fetch-depth: 0`, so it is missing the `origin/main` branch history, and (2) it runs `npx turbo run lint test build` for all 25 packages instead of only the affected ones!
Fix both:
1. Add `with: { fetch-depth: 0 }` to the `actions/checkout@v4` step.
2. Update the command in the final step to `npx turbo run lint test build --filter=...[origin/main]`.
hintsEn: Add `with:\n  fetch-depth: 0` (the number 0, without quotes) directly under `uses: actions/checkout@v4`.
Update the last `run:` line to `npx turbo run lint test build --filter=...[origin/main]`.

cicd-ex-c16-4.titleEn: Record Release Events for the 4 DORA Metrics
cicd-ex-c16-4.promptEn:
To automatically measure **Deployment Frequency** and **Lead Time for Changes**, complete the `dora-metrics` job that runs sequentially right after `deploy-prod` succeeds:
1. Declare `needs: [deploy-prod]` and the explicit condition `if: success()`.
2. In the `Emit DORA deployment event` step, output a payload / log containing all 3 standard fields: the `commit_sha` key set to `${{ github.sha }}`, the `deployed_at` timestamp, and `"environment": "production"`.
hintsEn: Add `needs: [deploy-prod]` and `if: success()` to the `dora-metrics` job.
In the `run:` block, build a JSON or string printing `commit_sha` (`${{ github.sha }}`), `deployed_at`, and `"environment": "production"`.

C17.titleEn: Diagnosing & Resolving 4 Typical Production CI/CD Incidents
C17.summaryEn: Hands-on diagnosis and hotfixing of 4 critical real-world CI/CD incidents: a 42-minute bottlenecked pipeline (B1), a Production deployment race condition (B2), a leaked secret in YAML (B3), and a false-green pipeline swallowing error codes (B6).

steps.headingEn: Overview & Context
steps.bodyEn:
Congratulations on reaching the final stage of the **CI/CD Mastery** course. YAML configuration knowledge only truly proves its worth in practice when you have to diagnose and resolve an active pipeline incident:
- [!] The product team has to wait **42 minutes** for every emergency hotfix (**Case B1**).
- [!] Two deployments **overwrite each other (Race Condition)**, corrupting the Production infrastructure state lock (**Case B2**).
- [!] An alerting system detects an **API key exposed directly** in a workflow file pushed to Git (**Case B3**).
- [!] The hardest case to spot: the entire pipeline reports a **false-green success (False-Green)** while users are hitting **HTTP 500** errors (**Case B6**).

> [!TIP] Production Incident Response Principle: Restore Service First (Reduce MTTR), Analyze Root Cause Later
> When Production breaks after a new release, the standard operations engineering rule is to **restore service as fast as possible (under 2 minutes)** by **rolling back** to the previous stable Image SHA tag (or disabling a **Feature Flag**) — rather than debugging live while customers are experiencing `500` errors. Only choose **Roll-Forward** (pushing a new patch) when the fix is minimal and verified, or when the database has migrated into a non-reversible state.

```visual
kind: troubleshoot
title: "Phân loại và quy trình xử lý 4 sự cố CI/CD phổ biến [!badge:rose:Incident Triage]"
subtitle: Tra cứu nhanh triệu chứng hiện trường, nguyên nhân gốc rễ (RCA) và hành động khắc phục tức thì
items:
  - symptom: "[Hồ sơ B1] Mỗi PR sửa 1 dòng code phải chờ 42 phút; job treo ngốn sạch 360 phút mặc định"
    badge: Critical Path
    tone: amber
    cause: "Dùng npm install không cache, chạy nối đuôi tuần tự lint -> typecheck -> 400 bài test trên 1 máy, gài sleep 45 cảm tính và quên đặt timeout-minutes."
    fix: "Bật cache: 'npm' + npm ci, tách lint chạy song song với test chia 4 mảnh (shard 1..4), bỏ sleep 45 và khoá timeout-minutes: 15."
    cmd: "strategy: { matrix: { shard: [1, 2, 3, 4] } }  # 42m -> < 5m"
  - symptom: "[Hồ sơ B2] Hai commit merge vào main cách nhau 40 giây làm đứt ngang đợt deploy đang chạy"
    badge: Race Condition
    tone: rose
    cause: "Copy-paste nhầm cấu hình concurrency của nhánh PR sang job deploy-production với cờ cancel-in-progress: true."
    fix: "Trên môi trường Production bắt buộc đặt group cố định kèm cancel-in-progress: false để đợt sau xếp hàng (Pending) chờ đợt trước hoàn tất."
    cmd: "concurrency: { group: production-deploy, cancel-in-progress: false }"
  - symptom: "[Hồ sơ B3] Phát hiện khoá API thật bị gõ cứng trong khối env: của .github/workflows/ci.yml"
    badge: Secret Leak
    tone: rose
    cause: "Lập trình viên viết thẳng chuỗi bí mật vào tệp YAML và đã git push lưu vết vĩnh viễn trong lịch sử git log."
    fix: "1) Thu hồi & xoay vòng (Revoke/Rotate) khoá ngay lập tức + đổi sang secrets.* · 2) Dựng cổng quét Gitleaks kèm fetch-depth: 0."
    cmd: "gitleaks detect --source . --no-banner --redact"
  - symptom: "[Hồ sơ B6] 14 bài Unit Test đỏ rực và server trả HTTP 500 nhưng Pipeline vẫn báo tích XANH"
    badge: Silent False-Green
    tone: cyan
    cause: "Mã thoát lỗi khác 0 bị nuốt mất bởi continue-on-error: true, toán tử shell '|| true', hoặc gọi curl thiếu cờ --fail."
    fix: "Xoá bỏ continue-on-error: true và '|| true' khỏi mọi cổng kiểm định/bảo mật; luôn truyền cờ --fail cho lệnh curl Smoke Test."
    cmd: "npm test && curl --fail --silent --show-error https://api.shop.example.com/healthz"
```

steps.headingEn: Case B1: 42-Minute Slow Pipeline — Critical Path Bottleneck Analysis
steps.bodyEn:
```visual
kind: illustration
diagram: "cicd:c17"
alt: "Bản đồ phân loại và xử lý 4 khủng hoảng CI/CD gồm nghẽn 42 phút & treo 360 phút, đua tranh deploy Production, lộ khoá Git và lỗi False-Green"
title: "Quy trình xử lý 4 tình huống sự cố CI/CD nghiêm trọng"
subtitle: "Quy trình phản ứng chuẩn kỹ sư nền tảng khi pipeline tắc nghẽn, hỏng khoá hạ tầng, lộ bí mật hoặc báo thành công giả"
caption: "Tóm tắt triệu chứng và biện pháp xử lý cho 4 tình huống sự cố: Tối ưu đường găng, Xếp hàng Concurrency, Xoay vòng Secret và Chặn False-Green"
callouts:
  - num: 1
    label: "Cắt đứt nghẽn cổ chai 42 phút & Treo máy 360 phút"
    desc: "Áp trần timeout-minutes: 15 ngay lập tức, thay sleep mù quáng bằng thăm dò /healthz và chia 4 mảnh kiểm thử song song xuống dưới 5 phút."
    tone: amber
  - num: 2
    label: "Chặn đua tranh Production & Nhiễm độc bộ đệm"
    desc: "Đổi concurrency trên Production sang cancel-in-progress: false để xếp hàng tuần tự và khoá quyền chỉ đọc cache đối với các nhánh PR."
    tone: rose
  - num: 3
    label: "Ứng cứu lộ khoá Git & Triệt tiêu False-Green"
    desc: "Thu hồi và xoay vòng khoá ngay lập tức (xoá dòng bằng commit mới không xoá được git log!), chuyển sang OIDC và cấm tuyệt đối || true."
    tone: rose
```

**Real-world symptoms:** Every time a developer pushes a single commit to fix a typo on a PR, the whole team has to wait **42 minutes**. Occasionally an integration test hangs on a connection, leaving the runner stuck for GitHub Actions' default ==360 minutes (6 hours)== and burning through the entire month's runner-minute quota!

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Hồ Sơ B1 — Tối Ưu Đường Găng (Critical Path): Từ 42 Phút Xuống Dưới 5 Phút!"
subtitle: "Triệt tiêu thời gian tải mạng lặp lại, phá bỏ chuỗi tuần tự độc đạo và khoá trần thời gian treo"
left:
  badge: "HIỆN TRƯỜNG LỖI · 42 Phút / PR"
  title: "Tuần tự 1 luồng + Không Cache + Thiếu Timeout"
  tone: rose
  code: |
    jobs:
      ci:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        # Thiếu timeout-minutes -> Treo mặc định tới 360 phút (6h)!
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - run: npm install          # Tải lại 1.200 gói mất 4 phút, lệch lockfile
          - run: npm run lint
          - run: npm run typecheck
          - run: sleep 45             # Ngủ đông cảm tính vô nghĩa!
          - run: npm test             # Chạy nối đuôi 400 bài test trên 1 máy
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "`npm install` không có bộ đệm phải kéo mạng từ đầu mỗi lần khởi tạo ephemeral runner"
    - "Mọi bước xếp hàng 1 cột dọc khiến tổng thời gian bằng tổng cộng dồn tất cả các bước"
right:
  badge: "CẤU HÌNH CHUẨN · Dưới 5 Phút / PR"
  title: "Cache npm ci + Tách DAG Song Song + Sharding 4 Luồng"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    jobs:
      lint:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 10
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with: { node-version: 22, cache: "npm" }
          - run: npm ci && npm run lint && npm run typecheck

      test:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        timeout-minutes: 15
        strategy:
          matrix:
            shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
            with: { node-version: 22, cache: "npm" }
          - run: npm ci && npx vitest run --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "`cache: \"npm\"` + `npm ci` rút bước cài gói xuống vài giây và khoá cứng theo `package-lock.json`"
    - "`lint` chạy song song độc lập với 4 mảnh `test`; loại bỏ `sleep 45` và khoá `timeout-minutes` chặt chẽ"
```

steps.headingEn: Case B2: Concurrent Deployment Conflict (Deployment Race Condition)
steps.bodyEn:
**Real-world symptoms:** At `14:02:00`, Commit `A` (upgrading the payment service) is merged into `main` and begins updating infrastructure. At `14:02:40` (40 seconds later), Commit `B` (editing the README) is merged right behind it. Suddenly the system throws an inconsistency error, leaving half the cluster with a partial configuration (*partial deploy*) and a corrupted *state lock*!

```visual
kind: compare
title: "Hồ Sơ B2 — Khác biệt cấu hình cancel-in-progress giữa PR nháp và Production"
subtitle: "Sử dụng nguyên cấu hình concurrency của PR cho Production sẽ gây hủy ngang đợt triển khai đang chạy"
left:
  badge: "DÀNH RIÊNG CHO PR NHÁP · Tiết kiệm phút CI"
  title: "Huỷ ngay bản chạy cũ đã lỗi thời (true)"
  tone: sky
  code: |
    # TRÊN PULL REQUEST: Nhóm động theo số PR / tên nhánh
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Khi lập trình viên đẩy tiếp commit mới lên nhánh PR, kết quả test của commit nháp cũ không còn giá trị nên huỷ ngay là hoàn toàn hợp lý"
    - "**CẤM dùng cấu hình `true` này cho Job triển khai hạ tầng / Production!**"
right:
  badge: "BẮT BUỘC CHO PRODUCTION · Tuần tự an toàn"
  title: "Xếp hàng chờ đợt đang chạy hoàn tất (false)"
  tone: emerald
  code: |
    # TRÊN PRODUCTION: Nhóm cố định + Không hủy ngang đợt đang chạy!
    deploy-production:
      environment: production
      concurrency:
        group: production-deploy
        cancel-in-progress: false
  lang: yaml
  bullets:
    - "Đặt ==`cancel-in-progress: false`== đảm bảo đợt triển khai Commit `A` đang chạy migration/Helm được hoàn tất trọn vẹn 100%"
    - "Đợt Commit `B` đến sau sẽ lịch sự đứng ở trạng thái **`Pending` (xếp hàng)** chờ tới lượt an toàn"
```

steps.headingEn: Case B3: Exposed Sensitive Credentials (Hardcoded Secret) in Workflow YAML
steps.bodyEn:
**Real-world symptoms:** Wanting to quickly test a payment integration, an engineer hardcodes `STRIPE_API_KEY: "<HARDCODED_SECRET_EXAMPLE>"` directly inside the `env:` block of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and runs `git push` to the GitHub repository!

> [!WARNING] Common Mistake When Handling Leaked Secrets in Git
> Many people assume that simply creating a new commit to replace that line with `${{ secrets.STRIPE_API_KEY }}` is enough. **COMPLETELY WRONG!** A new commit only removes the key string from the current `HEAD` snapshot, while the real secret remains intact forever in `git log` history (and automated secret-scanning bots take only seconds to harvest it)!

**Standard DevSecOps remediation requires completing both steps:**
- [x] **Part 1 — Immediate Remediation:** Immediately go to the third-party provider's admin console to **Revoke & Rotate (==Revoke / Rotate==)** the leaked key so the string in Git history becomes worthless, while updating the YAML to `${{ secrets.STRIPE_API_KEY }}`.
- [x] **Part 2 — Preventive Gate:** Add a commit-history scan step using **Gitleaks** paired with ==`fetch-depth: 0`== on `actions/checkout@v4` at the very start of the pipeline — catching even cases where someone accidentally commits a secret in commit #1 and deletes it in commit #2 within the same PR!

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0   # Bắt buộc tải toàn bộ lịch sử các commit trong PR!
- name: Cổng chặn rò rỉ khoá bí mật Gitleaks
  run: gitleaks detect --source . --no-banner --redact
```

---

steps.headingEn: Case B6: Silent False-Green Pipeline
steps.bodyEn:
**Real-world symptoms:** A codebase containing compilation errors and 14 failing Unit Tests still shows a bright **green checkmark** on the PR, marches straight into Production, and brings down the checkout flow!

```visual
kind: groups
title: "Ba nguyên nhân phổ biến gây báo thành công giả (Exit Code != 0 bị chuyển thành 0)"
subtitle: Chỉ cần tồn tại 1 trong 3 cấu hình này, các bước kiểm tra chất lượng và bảo mật sẽ không thể chặn PR lỗi.
columns: 3
items:
  - num: 1
    icon: alert
    title: "continue-on-error: true"
    badge: Tắt phanh cổng chặn
    tone: rose
    bullets:
      - "Thường bị ai đó bật tạm trên `unit-test` hoặc `trivy-scan` để ép qua PR gấp rồi bỏ quên suốt 6 tháng"
      - "Dù Trivy bắt được 10 lỗ hổng `CRITICAL` và trả mã thoát `1`, pipeline vẫn báo **XANH** và đẩy thẳng lên Production!"
    code: |
      # XOÁ NGAY dòng này trên mọi cổng Hard Gate:
      continue-on-error: true
    codeLang: yaml
  - num: 2
    icon: terminal
    title: "Toán tử Shell || true"
    badge: Nuốt lỗi dòng lệnh
    tone: amber
    bullets:
      - "Trong shell, toán tử OR logic ==`||`== sẽ chạy vế phải (`true`, luôn trả mã thoát `0`) khi lệnh bên trái thất bại"
      - "Biến `npm test` đang đỏ (`exit 1`) thành `exit 0` êm ru trước mắt GitHub Actions!"
    code: |
      # SAI: npm test || true
      # ĐÚNG — giữ nguyên mã thoát trung thực:
      run: npm test
    codeLang: yaml
  - num: 3
    icon: globe
    title: "curl thiếu cờ --fail"
    badge: Mù trước lỗi HTTP 500
    tone: cyan
    bullets:
      - "Không có `--fail` (`-f`), lệnh `curl` nhận phản hồi `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` từ server đang sập vẫn báo `exit 0`!"
      - "Luôn bắt buộc truyền `--fail` trong mọi kịch bản Smoke Test hậu triển khai"
    code: |
      curl --fail --silent --show-error \
        --retry 5 --retry-delay 3 \
        https://api.shop.example.com/healthz
    codeLang: shell
```

> [!REMEMBER] Pocket Summary (Incident Response Takeaways)
> - **B1 (Speed & Hangs):** Use `cache: "npm"` + `npm ci`, split into a parallel DAG + 4-way sharding, remove arbitrary `sleep` calls, and always set **`timeout-minutes`** (GitHub Actions defaults to **360 minutes**!).
> - **B2 (Prevent Overlapping Deploys):** On Production, always lock **`concurrency: { group: "production-deploy", cancel-in-progress: false }`**.
> - **B3 (Leaked Secret):** Always **Revoke/Rotate** the compromised key immediately (removing it in a new commit does not erase `git log`) + enforce **`gitleaks detect`** with **`fetch-depth: 0`**.
> - **B6 (Eliminate False-Greens):** Eliminate every **`continue-on-error: true`**, **`||` (`|| true`)** operator, and `curl` command missing **`--fail`**!

readings.noteEn: Side-by-side comparison of cancel-in-progress configuration between PR branches (true) and Production deployments (false).
readings.taskEn: Why does the same concurrency feature use a per-PR group on PRs, whereas on Production it uses a single fixed string?
readings.answerEn: On PRs, each independent PR needs its own group (pr-ci-42) so one person's PR does not cancel another person's PR. On Production, there is only one live environment, so everything must share a single fixed lock key to queue sequentially.

readings.noteEn: Typical profile of a sequential, uncached pipeline that runs npm install repeatedly and idles with sleep.
readings.taskEn: List the 3 biggest reasons why the pipeline in this file takes over 40 minutes.
readings.answerEn: 1) Using npm install without dependency caching in every job; 2) Chaining all lint, test, and e2e steps sequentially in a single stream; 3) Running the entire heavy test suite on a single runner instead of sharding.

readings.noteEn: Three classic traps that turn compilation errors, test failures, and HTTP 500s into false-green checkmarks.
readings.taskEn: If you remove continue-on-error: true but keep run: npm test || true, will the job stop when Jest fails?
readings.answerEn: NO! The || true operator in Bash forces the overall command to always return exit code 0, so GitHub Actions still mistakenly assumes all tests passed.

C17-Q1.qEn: [Case B1] When inheriting a PR workflow that takes 42 minutes because it runs `npm install` -> `npm run lint` -> `npm test` -> `sleep 45` sequentially, which combination of improvements shortens the Critical Path most effectively and safely?
choicesEn: Add continue-on-error: true to all steps and delete 50% of the tests

Use `actions/setup-node@v4` (`cache: "npm"`) + `npm ci`, split `lint` and `test` into 2 parallel jobs, shard `test` with `strategy.matrix.shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]`, remove `sleep 45`, and set `timeout-minutes`
Switch `ubuntu-latest` to running manually on the tech lead's personal laptop
Combine all commands into a single Bash line separated by semicolons
C17-Q1.explainEn: Combining npm caching + `npm ci` + a parallel DAG + 4-way sharding directly addresses both installation time and the test-suite bottleneck.

C17-Q2.qEn: [Case B2] What happens in practice if the `deploy-production` job sets `concurrency: { group: "production-deploy", cancel-in-progress: true }` when 2 commits are merged into `main` 40 seconds apart?
choicesEn: GitHub automatically squashes the 2 commits and waits for the first run to finish cleanly before starting the second
The first deployment receives a mid-flight cancellation signal right in the middle of updating infrastructure/migrations, causing corrupted state (partial deploy / corrupted lock) on Production!
The second commit is rejected from merging into main
It has no effect because concurrency does not work on the main branch
C17-Q2.explainEn: On Production, you must set `cancel-in-progress: false` so the newer release queues (`Pending`) and waits for the active deployment to finish safely.

C17-Q3.qEn: [Case B3] When a real API key is discovered hardcoded in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and already pushed to GitHub, simply creating a new commit that replaces it with `${{ secrets.STRIPE_API_KEY }}` makes the old key completely safe with no need to revoke/rotate it.
C17-Q3.explainEn: A new commit only removes the key string from the current HEAD revision; the leaked key remains intact in `git log` history (and may already have been harvested by bots)! You MUST Revoke/Rotate the key immediately AND add a Gitleaks scanning gate.

C17-Q4.qEn: [Case B6] In the command `npm test || true`, which 2-character operator before the `true` keyword swallows the test runner's non-zero exit code?
C17-Q4.explainEn: The shell logical OR operator `||` runs the right-hand command (`true`, which always returns exit code 0) whenever the left-hand command fails, turning the entire line's exit code into 0!

C17-Q5.qEn: [Case B6] In a security validation pipeline, what is the consequence of setting `continue-on-error: true` on the `trivy-scan` job or step?
choicesEn: It makes Trivy scan devDependencies even more deeply
Even when Trivy detects a CRITICAL vulnerability and returns exit code 1, the pipeline still reports GREEN and allows the vulnerable build straight into Production
It automatically upgrades the vulnerable npm package version
It sends the security report to GitHub's Security tab
C17-Q5.explainEn: `continue-on-error: true` turns a security hard gate into a harmless warning that gets completely ignored.

C17-Q6.qEn: [Case B3] Why should a secret-leak scan step using `gitleaks detect` in CI be paired with `fetch-depth: 0` in the `actions/checkout@v4` step?
choicesEn: Because Gitleaks is written in Rust and needs to read the .git/config file
So Gitleaks scans across the entire commit history in the PR (catching cases where a developer accidentally commits a secret in commit #1 and deletes it in commit #2!)
To minimize the amount of source code downloaded
Because GitHub forbids running Gitleaks without fetch-depth: 0
C17-Q6.explainEn: If only the final file snapshot is scanned (`fetch-depth: 1`), an attacker or careless developer who commits a secret in an intermediate commit and deletes it in the final commit will still leak that secret into Git history upon merge!

C17-Q7.qEn: In GitHub Actions, if you omit `timeout-minutes` on a job, a deadlocked test process will consume runner resources for the default **360 minutes (6 hours)** before the system automatically terminates it.
C17-Q7.explainEn: GitHub Actions' 360-minute default is a leading cause of exhausting monthly CI runner minutes after just a few hung-connection PRs.

C17-C1.frontEn: What is the 4-step solution to completely fix the **42-Minute Pipeline incident (Case B1)**?
C17-C1.backEn:
1) `setup-node@v4` (`cache: "npm"`) + `npm ci`.
2) Split `lint` and `test` to run in parallel.
3) Enable `strategy.matrix.shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]` for `test`.
4) Remove arbitrary `sleep` calls & add `timeout-minutes`.

C17-C2.frontEn: What is the standard configuration to prevent a **Production Deployment Race Condition (Case B2)**?
C17-C2.backEn:
Attach `environment: production` AND declare:
`concurrency:`
`  group: production-deploy`
`  cancel-in-progress: false`

C17-C3.frontEn: What is the 2-step response workflow for a **Hardcoded Secret Leak in YAML (Case B3)**?
C17-C3.backEn:
1) Remove the hardcoded key from YAML and replace it with `${{ secrets.<NAME> }}` (while immediately revoking/rotating the real key).
2) Add a `gitleaks detect` gate with `fetch-depth: 0` to block recurrences across commit history.

C17-C4.frontEn: What are the three common root causes of a **False-Green Pipeline (Case B6)**?
C17-C4.backEn:
1) `continue-on-error: true` on a test/scan step.
2) Appending `|| true` to a test command.
3) Calling `curl <url>` for health checks without the `--fail` flag.

C17-C5.frontEn: What is the difference between `cancel-in-progress` on a PR branch versus Production?
C17-C5.backEn:
- **PR**: `cancel-in-progress: true` (cancels stale runs, saves runner minutes).
- **Production**: `cancel-in-progress: false` (queues sequentially, preserves infrastructure integrity).

C17-C6.frontEn: Why should you always set an explicit `timeout-minutes` on every CI/CD job?
C17-C6.backEn: To prevent GitHub Actions' 360-minute (6-hour) default from clogging queues and draining your runner budget when a network call or test hangs.

cicd-ex-c17-1.titleEn: Case B1 — Optimize a 42-Minute Pipeline to Under 5 Minutes
cicd-ex-c17-1.promptEn:
**Incident scenario:** The engineering team is blocked: every Pull Request has to wait **42 minutes** in the queue! Inspecting the current workflow file reveals 4 critical issues: using `npm install` with no cache, lumping `lint` and all `test`s into a single sequential flow, inserting a pointless `sleep 45`, and having no `timeout-minutes` limit at all.

Refactor the broken workflow file below end-to-end:
1. Split into 2 parallel jobs: `lint` and `test` (both with `timeout-minutes: 10` or `<= 15`).
2. In both jobs, use `actions/setup-node@v4` with `node-version: "22"` and `cache: "npm"`, and install dependencies with `npm ci` (remove `npm install`).
3. In the `test` job, enable parallel sharding with `strategy.matrix.shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]`, run `npm test -- --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4`, and **completely remove** the `sleep 45` command.
hintsEn: Split `monolith-slow-check` into two sibling jobs `lint:` and `test:` (do not put `needs` between them).
In both jobs, add `cache: "npm"` under `with:` of `actions/setup-node@v4` and use `run: npm ci`.
In `test:`, declare `strategy.matrix.shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]` and run `npm test -- --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4`.

cicd-ex-c17-2.titleEn: Case B2 — Resolve a Production Race Condition Incident
cicd-ex-c17-2.promptEn:
**Incident scenario:** At 15:10 this afternoon, two Pull Requests were merged back-to-back into `main`. The second deployment **killed the first deployment mid-flight** while changes were actively being applied to Production because `cancel-in-progress: true` was set, leaving the system in a broken half-deployed state!

Apply an emergency patch to the `deploy-production` job:
1. Bind the job to the protected environment `environment: production`.
2. Set a fixed concurrency lock group name `concurrency.group: "production-deploy"`.
3. Change `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: false` so subsequent releases queue sequentially instead of cancelling the active run.
hintsEn: If `group` includes `${{ github.sha }}`, every commit creates its own group so they still overwrite each other! Change it to the static string `production-deploy`.
Change `cancel-in-progress` to `false` and add `environment: production`.

cicd-ex-c17-3.titleEn: Case B3 — Remediate a Leaked Secret & Add a Gitleaks Gate
cicd-ex-c17-3.promptEn:
**Incident scenario:** The security alerting system just sounded a red alarm: the hardcoded key `STRIPE_API_KEY: "sk_test_placeholder_leaked_in_yaml"` appeared inside the payment integration workflow file! In addition to revoking the key in the Stripe dashboard, you need to clean up the YAML file and put an automated scanning gate in place to prevent recurrences.

Completely remediate incident B3 on the `integration-check` job:
1. Update the first `actions/checkout@v4` step to include `with: { fetch-depth: 0 }` (to fetch full commit history).
2. Immediately after checkout, insert a secret-leak scan step running `gitleaks detect --source . --verbose` before installing dependencies & running tests.
3. In the final test step, replace the hardcoded value of `env.STRIPE_API_KEY` with the secure reference `${{ secrets.STRIPE_API_KEY }}`.
hintsEn: After inserting the Gitleaks step at `steps[1]`, the `steps` array will have 5 elements total (0: checkout, 1: gitleaks, 2: setup-node, 3: npm ci, 4: test:integration).
Change `STRIPE_API_KEY` to `${{ secrets.STRIPE_API_KEY }}`.

cicd-ex-c17-4.promptEn:
**Incident scenario:** A broken release carrying 12 Unit Test failures, 2 CRITICAL security vulnerabilities, and a `/healthz` endpoint returning HTTP `500` just sailed straight into Production with... **100% green checkmarks**! Track down every neutralized gate in this workflow file.

Restore strict enforcement across the quality gates in the `release-gate` job:
1. Remove `continue-on-error: true` from the `unit-test` step AND remove the `|| true` operator from the `npm test` command.
2. Remove `continue-on-error: true` from the `trivy-scan` step so CRITICAL/HIGH vulnerabilities block the pipeline.
3. Add the `--fail` flag (along with `--silent --show-error`) to the `curl https://api.shop.example.com/healthz` command in the final step.
hintsEn: Completely delete both `continue-on-error: true` lines in the `unit-test` (`steps[3]`) and `trivy-scan` (`steps[4]`) steps.
Clean up `npm test || true` to `npm test`.
Update the final step to `curl --fail --silent --show-error https://api.shop.example.com/healthz`.
